films.syn: What happens when reality kicks in? On a beach at twilight's dawn, a little girl meticulously builds up an ecosystem. She intends to make her little world perfect. But soon, the tide is coming in...

In every sense a KABOOM music video! The clip for Red Snapper's new single B Planet is a journey into psychedelic abstraction, pulling us into the now. A reality peppered with acidic distortions that transforms space into a super-vitaminated universe.

Bakermat's music videos are always a treat, and this is no exception! The song Ain't Nobody ft. LaShun Pace gets an animated delight where Matt and his new friends accidentally end up on a journey through time and space.

Kitchen monster alert! In this combination of hand-drawn animation and cut-out, a loving grandmother gets everything ready for dinner with her big family, but this is so much work that she literally has to grow extra limbs. As everything goes wrong in the kitchen, she turns into a monster, but with the help of her family, she can turn back into herself.

There's something magical about Irish animation, and Bardo is no different. A woman questions her lifestyle choices when the travails of urban living are one day jolted into juxtaposition with a simpler way of life. A film about connection across generations.
In this lovely textured and experimentally tickling short, a lady meets a lovely beast, albeit a gigantic slimy cheesy one.
A short story about a small-town beauty thrust into 1800s stardom. Loosely based on Philippine folklore, this animated film defines "hot girl problems".

Beep Beep is an animated journal based on phone conversations the director had with her parents, without them knowing she was recording them. Documented in a lighthearted way, the film is a representation of the relationship Mihaela Mindru has with her parents while being far away from home for the first time.

Ambitiously animated, this short explores the tension in watching and being watched, and the effects of rejection can have on one's self-image. An uncanny and eerie watch that will make you question the looks you give and receive.

A hyper-modern reimagining of Beauty & the Beast directed by Mamoru Hosoda which is the best emotional eye-candy you will get all year. Welcome to the world of U. A hyper-modern quasi-reimagining of the classic Beauty & the Beast fairy tale, Belle is ambitious and riveting eye-candy at the service of a poignant story about our contemporary society and the human condition. Mirai director Mamoru Hosoda's latest imaginative coming-of-age story brings a wild vision of an online virtual world - U - which is basically an endless metropolis where you can live as 'another you'. Make an avatar based on your biometric data and enter a different reality; that's how simple it is. This emotion-packed Japanese tale follows a shy high-school girl, Suzu, who has been anything but happy since her mother died when she was a small child. Still wounded, Suzu one day decides to have a got at the U hype. She creates an avatar and dives into the alternate reality as Belle. Before long, all of U's eyes are fixed on Belle, who - to her own surprise - discovers her singing voice again. But then, at one of her concerts, a mysterious dragon-like figure appears and creates havoc. Who is this beast? Belle is a visually breathtaking film of almost epic proportions which still foregrounds the intimate. The great filmmaker Mamoru Hosoda has always been a man with limitless eye-popping imagination and perspective. The man behind modern anime classics such as The Girl Who Leapt Through Time , Summer Wars and Wolf Children is known for experimenting with exuberant visions of virtual realms and magical fantasies. Hosoda's previous film, the cute and inspirational Mirai was as groundbreaking as any of his other features, becoming the first non-Studio Ghibli anime to pick up a nomination in the Best Animated Feature category at the Oscars. Maximalist at its core, Belle is a film of grand ideas, of familiar themes, and of the good old beloved anime sentimentality. Add to the equation: a grandiose use of original J-Pop songs that will surely get you teary-eyed. Yet, for all its lush visuals and extravaganza, the film is also a heartfelt commentary on how we deal with pain and sorrow, on how - perhaps - social media can bring us together after all, and on how we learn to be ourselves despite wanting to be someone else. For its character design, Hosoda teamed up with veteran animator Jin Kim, who is responsible for the look of loads of Disney characters, and with the Irish animation studio Cartoon Saloon which produced Wolfwalkers . Enough selling points?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Based on true events, Bestia explores the life of a secret police agent during the military junta headed by Pinochet in Chile. Haunted by the atrocities she has committed, the agent's mind begins to fracture. So we get a glimpse into the mind of a stooge for a fascist dictatorship. You'll never forget that porcelain face, mark our words.

An absurd drama about a shocking house, Bewogen Woerde uses black-and-white imagery and red-blue riso animation to tell the story of a crumbling house. In a ramshackle farm - damaged by earthquakes, lives a young man, Dwon. His only roommate is a strong man who supports the ceiling so the house won't fall apart. One day, they get a visit by an engineer from the local government and his measuring system: a scanning robot that looks a bit like a duck. The investigation seems to be falling apart.

films.t: Bob Spit – We Do Not Like People
films.syn: The wrath of an author in crisis won't spare his creations. And to avoid being eaten by the pop, the punk must face his creator... No feature film embraces the Kaboom craziness as Cesar Cabral's Bob Spit - We Do Not Like People . Welcome to an ultrameta and foul-mouthed stop-motion animation film where an old, angry punk named Bob Spit is trying to escape a post-apocalyptic desert full of grotesque characters, including feral miniature Elton Johns with sharp teeth (it's quite literally pop trying to kill punk). Wait, it gets better: the wasteland is actually a purgatory inside the mind of Bob's creator, Angeli, a stubborn cartoonist going through a creative crisis. Mixing documentary, comedy and road movie, Cabral's hallucinatory voyage into the conflict between creator and creation is not even entirely fictitious! The story is inspired by the life and work of one of the most celebrated Brazilian cartoonists of all time, Angeli. He became famous in the 70s by releasing political cartoons during Brazil's military dictatorship. Angeli's characters - and one in particular: Bob Spit, a rude ogre-like punk with an impressive mohawk - became more famous than himself. And when Angeli decided to move on and bury Bob, fans were asking for more, which left the cartoonist struggling with his creation. Building on a short film and a TV series, the film is a weird, post-modern, even philosophical rollercoaster embracing the subversive, countercultural and anarchic spirit of Angeli's original cartoons. The question remains: can Bob escape Angeli's brain and teach him a lesson for killing him off? Bob Spit - We Do Not Like People won the Contrechamp Award at the Annecy Festival. Strap in for a bizarre cocktail that finally proves ... Punk is not dead!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: A hand-drawn short about an unconventional relationship, BoxBallet shows a delicate ballerina and a rough, surly boxer, and the same timid feeling that arises between them. Will they overcome everything external and superficial, behind which fragile loving souls are hidden?

This moving and beautiful short conveys the different journeys, and accompanying emotions women go on with their breasts; from pride and embarrassment as their breasts develop, to their breasts attracting attention from others, to breastfeeding and attending mammogram appointments. Made for charity Breast Cancer Now.
When to most beautiful brush in the jar suddenly dries out, he does everything he can to save his beautiful bristles to be able to paint again. But uh-oh, what a mess!
A damning reflection of society, Elena Felici's tense short is set on a bus with passengers who fail to address a back seat scenario.

Six years in the making, the philosophical genre film Camouflage is a dystopian thriller in which we follow four days in the life of office clerk Amouf, while he desperately tries to hold his life together while the world around him gets darker and darker, following the rise of De Jager. This flamboyant and highly intimidating creature is a hate-instigating vigilante, who has sworn to systematically prosecute certain groups. A hand-drawn animated film with over 800(!) character-animations.

Each year, Chanel's Métiers d'Art honours the craft of the house's talented artisans, but also gives the chance to talented filmmakers to present a short film, promoting these designers. The hour is coming. Through the folds and boxes of the Lognon workshops, Akon makes her way backstage where she meets the other models. The fashion show is about to begin.

Each year, Chanel's Métiers d'Art honours the craft of the house's talented artisans, but also gives the chance to talented filmmakers to present a short film, promoting these designers. Among a multitude of shoes, one of them comes to life. Rianne sets off in pursuit of it, in a frantic race that leads her to the heart of the Massaro workshop.

Each year, Chanel's Métiers d'Art honours the craft of the house's talented artisans, but also gives the chance to talented filmmakers to present a short film, promoting these designers. Pan contemplates and wanders with enchantment through fantastic sceneries. Strange and wonderful landscapes, full of precious minerals. As if on a journey to another planet: that of the embroideries of the Montex workshop.

Whatever our age, we all experience loneliness. In Chitchat we meet Oscar who, searching for social links, contacts strangers by phone, until he finds Arlette. During the conversation, he shares his insights about the world.

Chronic is a painfully honest and visually engaging portrayal of everyday unwanted intimacies. An ordinary woman's day is becoming more and more stressful: neither on the street, nor in the office, nor in the bar, she can feel at peace and safe until she reaches the point of no return.

films.t: Clipphanger: What is the Yo-Yo Effect?
films.syn: Clipphangers are really short animations which answer the most diverse questions in a funny and surprising way. This one lightheartedly explains the effect of the Yo-Yo-effect on your body. Made for NTR.

Animator Michaël Veerman playfully explains us how paint gets loose from a painting and how a restorer reattaches the paint. Made for the Mauritshuis in The Hague, home to a formidable collection of Dutch and Flemish paintings from the 17th century.

On 23 February 2005, the radio announces a bill about the benefits of French colonization: "School curriculums must acknowledge the positive impact of the French presence overseas, especially in North Africa." This announcement disrupts Louise and her family's daily life. Her house turns out to be inhabited by peculiar presences. Has history taught us anything?

In times where information has exploded, disinformation secretly affects people's cognition and judgment of politics, economy, technology, and environmental ecology. True and false information on the internet has become a globally concerned issue. Commissioned by the Taiwan Information Security Center.

C'mon admit it, pigeons are often a pain in the ass. But here, they manage to create a magical moment in a lonely and boring place. In a coach station a collection of tired travellers are waiting for the coach. Somehow, in that cold and. depressing place, the resident pigeons are the reason for a little bit of harmony...

Alone in an elevator? People do the craziest things. Together in an elevator... Totally different. Inspired by everyday life and the difference in people's behaviour when they are alone (in contrast to the socially acceptable behaviour when they are in a public space), this student short is a clever and funny study of the awkward public setting of an elevator.
In this family-friendly and emotional Qatari short a young girl attempts to prevent the imminent death of her beloved grandmother by harnessing the magical powers of a local Ramadan drummer.

What a raw and peaceful document of the past, of past people, places, and machines! Filmed on 16mm film, this visual expression is rooted in archival materials, drawing its inspiration from a poem by Hans Magnus Enzensberger which appears in the film. It speaks of forgotten people, their lives and their deeds. These two archives were found at a flea market in Zagreb. One is of a famous architect and the other of a famous composer. The film ponders on this occurrence, as well as on the vanishing and forgetfulness of humans.

Inspired by Picasso's hypermasculine print series 'Vollard Suite', South-Korean animator Chaerin Im sought to deconstruct the mythical figure of the Minotaur. With the use of light, reflection, and shadow of the engraved plexiglass and cyanotypes, the film goes through the gender-shifting faces of the creature, as he has a violent struggle between the two sexes. Until, finally, lines blur and boundaries of sexes disappear.
Welcome to a dreamlike fantasy world where two characters are witness to the surprising and playful behaviour of their environment.

When a girl wakes up in the middle of the night to her alarm clock ringing, she knows something is up. These suspicions are confirmed after looking in the mirror. A broken connection to herself sets off a haunting night. Told in a refreshing visual style, this claustrophobic short will leave you with a figment yourself.

A firefighter scans the city, ready to brave all dangers. But there is no fire. He wanted to put out everything that smoulders, smokes or burns. Even the Sun! Until he meets a woman and he flares up himself... from love.

Twins are often inseparable, and Mela and Zenia are REALLY close! The twin sisters take a trip to spend a lazy summer evening together by the lake. Their bond is so close that there is no telling where one ends and the other begins... each verges on being both the greatest blessing and saddest burden for the other.

How far do we let AI go? Created with the experimental technique of using LiDAR to capture real-life moments and environments, Forever explores the boundary of advanced technology and the human experience. The short shows how a life insurance company uses an AI algorithm to determine the risk of a new applicant. The subsequent denial sparks a period of introspection for the individual in question.

A heartwarming slice-of-life seaside tale about a big, loud mother and her quiet daughter. Following the brilliant Children of the Sea (one of our favourite anime films of recent years), director Ayumu Watanabe and Studio 4°C's newest love child is a slice-of-life seaside tale that focuses on a quietly curious schoolgirl - Kikuko - and her big, loud and immature mother Nikuko, who has been in relationships with men who either exploited or abandoned her. Nikuko works in the local tavern, while Kikuko attends the local elementary school. Mother Nikuko of course embarrasses her daughter as any mom of a pre-teen would, but Nikuko's bold spirit makes her especially well-known in a town where Kikuko herself just wants to stay under the radar. As the little girl navigates the everyday social dramas of middle school, enhanced with touches of magical realism from her ever-present imagination, a shocking revelation from the past threatens to uproot the pair's tender relationship. An observational and heartwarming comedy, Fortune Favors Lady Nikuko is a film about the small things in life with an unconventional mother-and-daugher pair at its centre. Mother's motto? "Being ordinary is best of all!" But far from ordinary, this Ghibli-esque feature often leans into the surreal and includes cute visual homages to My Neighbor Totoro . Continuing the trademark top-notch animation of Studio 4°C, the character design is as simple as it is complex. With joyful and life-affirming humour, this adaptation of Kanako Nishi's eponymous novel will put you in a 'summer chill mood'. Oh, and there's a lot of food in the film. A lot. An animated gem that serves the heart ánd the stomach!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: This Polish animation deals with the problem of growing anger, frustration and aggression that seeks an outlet. Our heroine is a person who loses control of her anger. Losing herself in emotions, she cannot stand the tension. The animation - composed of organic dense lines and appropriately expressive colour - makes anger painfully tactile.

Football is the most important of the least important things in the world. But, still it's hard for girls to live in this male-dominated sport. What is it like to be a girl in a boy's world? Six girls share their own experiences play woman's football. Their stories are translated by different animation techniques to explore various narrative possibilities.

A short but really sweet animation of the female nude, embodying all of her forms throughout the history of art. Her body twists and gnarls itself into these static poses, but she cannot be contained. In perpetual motion, she is released from her form and allowed to finally stare back at us.

Madness. Mayhem. The game is on! Three interlocking vignettes of motorized mayhem attack your brain with their over-the-top zany characters and design. Guns are blazing, cars are racing, craziness is piling up... By being more like an early 2000s game, you keep asking one question: where the hell do I plug in my controller?!
Ever wondered why Golden Hour is named as such? Two friends find out the reason why an hour before sunset is called "The Golden Hour" as they go for a quick swim before it gets dark.

"It's hard to think it's gonna be good, much easier to think it's gonna be bad." Israeli singer-songwriter Tova Gertner sings about identity, relationship and dreams. This music clip for a song of hers was shot by Israeli-German animator Gil Alkabetz based on his paradoxical and absurd drawings that speak of anxiety and uncertainty in the future.

A title that is funnier than the story behind it. A story needing to be told, Granny's Sexual Life is a harrowing animated film based on the anonymous testimonials gathered by Milena Miklavcic in the book Fire, Ass and Snakes are not Toys . Go on an eye-opening trip into grandmother's youth and the memories of her intimate life which illustrate the status of Slovenian women in the first half of the 20th century.

"I have made this film for you to relax. To ease your senses between real films. To take a nap. Sweet dreams", director Karolina Kajetanowicz says about her ethereal and soothing short. Roadside greenery is a no man's land. It was created to be passed, not to be in it. Geometrical and artificial, yet taken by wild weeds - does it belong to man, or to nature? Detach from reality for a brief moment. Meditate with us.

The fear of being forgotten, of feeling disconnected haunts us all. Daniel Gray's heartrending short starts with a joyous game of hide and seek by two brothers, while their parents cook diner. As one counts, the other hides in a small cabinet. Seconds pass... then minutes... years... and decades. An almost sensorial experience, Hide is a prescient story about family and disconnect, in a world that is increasingly fragmented and unrecognizable.

The story of the sweetest hijacking ever and the real drunk history of a Norwegian flight on June 21, 1985. What happened on this flight seems unbelievable, but trust us: it's all quite true! An intoxicated man spontaneously hijacks a plane. But of course, seizing an aircraft is a tiring chore, so he guzzles a beer. And another. Then a few more. Needless to say, nothing goes his way...
In the dark woods, we witness the dying hour of the Alpha male of a wolf pack. As he howls to the moon, he - and we with him - remember his sacrifice for the pack. Cry along!

Did you know we are the only species on Earth that actually cook their food? Human Recipe is an observation of the relationship we as humans have with food, something that distinguishes us from animals. Bon appétit!

Old home videos of your childhood... Embarrassing, yet incredibly nostalgic. I Don't Know Anything is an exploration of nostalgic feelings of the filmmakers' childhood, with home videos as a reference.

Get set for an explosive and jarring experience. I Wish is a true testament to the infamous experimental nature of Russian animation studio Soyuzmultfilm's work. The short follows a sort of hallucinatory dream-poem of a girl. She wants to sleep, but it's not that simple. She has lost her pillow, and the little forest pranksters do not help her to search at all for some reason.

films.t: Impossible Figures and Other Stories I
films.syn: The first - and paradoxically - the final part of Marta Pajek's triptych, Impossible Figures and Other Stories I follows an elegant elderly woman wandering deserted city streets, recalling what was and what could have been. As a flood slowly swallows the city, she shares a final moment of grieving beauty.
In nature, a couple is a male and a female. Well, not always! A couple is also a female and a female. Or a male and a male. You may not be aware of it, but homosexuality isn't just a human story.

Experimenting has always been key to finding new paths of cinema. Composed of a single take, Incomplete is an audiovisual project that conceptually uses Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The camera follows anonymous bodies in perpetual free-fall and moves through an endless choreography of updating images that reflect a world in constant change.

Based on the Polish comic book by Sascha Hommer, this incredibly bleak and poignant story follows Pascal who lives with his parents in a city full of smog. The smoke hides the secrets of both people and infamous ... insects. When Pascal discovers one of those secrets his life changes. Director Marcin Podolec is a Polish comic book artist and filmmaker and perfectly translates Insekt to the big screen. It's a must-must-see allegory of racism and exclusion. Animation at its most grim, but - ultimately - also liberating.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Leaders for festivals are a craft on its own. And this leader really delivers! Enjoy the spot for Bit Bang 2020, the Animation, Games and Digital Art Festival in Buenos Aires.

However small, war stories have to be told and remembered. Here, a grandfather - between two telephone calls - recalls an episode from the time when he was twenty and fought in Wold War II. Unfortunately, director Mathias de Panafieu didn't live to see his pencil-drawn bittersweet short. After an intense battle against cancer he passed away in 2019. His partner and loved ones completed the film.

It was raining in Eindhoven in July '21. A sweet, experimental short drawn on paper using pencils, oil pastels, ink and markers. It consists of 12 panels: 6 for the rain. 6 for the sun. Each phase of the shape loop was scanned and processed before the next one was drawn on top of it.
A catchy song requires catchy visuals. A university soccer-related music clip for a song by Korean artists JNKYRD and Ohhyuk.

In an imaginary space a woman lets go of herself and overcomes fearing her own greatness. She discovers her body, she embraces her emotions, and learns to own all the parts that make her HER. With stark black-and-white imagery, this music video for Canadian singer-songwriter kai is a story about the female nature and body.

This meme inspired music video is essentially a cry from the everyday driver of Australia frustrated by the general incompetence on the roads - in a ridiculous and hysterical way. On the menu: annoying situations, funny characters, road rage vibes and funky visuals.

Phew, is it getting hot in here? Exploring the inner world of female lust and pleasure, this student short reaches an orgasm, not by explicitness, but by associative images and sensual movement. We follow Barbie, who's emerging like Alice in Wonderland into a magical world, a place of temptation and pure joy. Here, she gets rid of her stiffness and repression, ultimately reaching a climax.

A young Mexican smuggler and a little girl travel illegally on top of a cargo train, called La Bestia - and better known in real life as The Death Train, to get to the United States. An injury, however, transforms the smuggler's perception of the journey. An atmospheric short commenting on the horrors migrants go through on the road to a better life.

Layang-Layang is a sweet short film centered around the nostalgic memories that filmmaker Dewi Hartono has been told by her father from his childhood in Indonesia. The film follows his journey from Indonesia until he met Hartono's mother, and moved to the Netherlands. Her father learned to adapt and live in a foreign country, and thus she grew up with two cultures that are completely different but equally beautiful.

Made by students in Beirut, this poignant short explores the human condition in Lebanon. Traveling in the city of Beirut, a small fire particle finds its way into a middle-aged man's home. In this small, ragged apartment, the particle floats through the history of this household, and where, upon its entry, the reality of this man shifts from seemingly-normal to a never-ending nightmare.

At its best, a poem can transcend everything we know while saying exactly what we should know. This excerpt from a poem by the Russian-American Nobel laureate Joseph Brodsky captures the Soviet empire of the 1980s. It's a metaphorical reckoning with a technocratic regime and a nightmarish illustration of war.
'King of Ukrainian animation' Mykyta Lyskov was commissioned by the LINOLEUM Contemporary Animation and Media Art Festival 2020 to direct the official festival trailer.

In a mix of 3D animation and watercolour paint, this truly painterly short tells the story of a father-son relationship. Chris' mother disappears without a trace, he and his father Toon are both confronted with great sadness. While Chris is able to cry and emote, Toon cannot bring himself to be vulnerable and literally swallows his tears. His body starts to fill up and he grows away - even literally - from Chris.

films.t: Love Is Just A Death Away
films.syn: This darkly humorous student work embodies both the cute and the macabre. With deliciously gross puppets, Love Is Just a Death Away shows how, for some, life starts after death for someone else. Like for a little parasite, who walks with a rotting corpse of a dead dog around on an old landfill. Trapped in his unpalatable body he tries to find love and friendship.

Czech-Vietnamese director Diana Cam Van Nguyen is a talent to watch. Her latest short is a compelling personal story about ties and and gaps between a child and a parent. Diana rediscovers love letters her dad used to write her from prison. That love seems to be gone now. Now, she decides the write back - in the form of a film - in hope to find the connection again. Using a mix of archive photography and animation, she tries to understand the family's break-up.
A full moon keeps everyone awake, especially one-moon obsessed ladybird. An imaginative and hypnotic short commissioned by Adult Swim.

films.t: Manfredi Simonetti ft. Kimberly Mangano – Marte
films.syn: A music clip with a WTF level through the roof, plus thousands of colours? Sign us up! Marte is song by Italian artist Manfredi Simonetti (ft. Kimberly Mangano) and tells a love story and a break-up between two caterpillars.

We can all agree: Marvin Gaye is a legend! In 2021, the iconic track/album "What's Going On" celebrated its 50th birthday. This animation re-imagines Marvin Gaye's unforgettable track by following him through scenes of civil unrest, the Vietnam War, poverty, and environmental damage.

László Moholy-Nagy was born on July 20, 1895 and became one of the great intellectuals and technical innovators of the 20th century. The oeuvre of the world-famous Hungarian artist is well known in many countries around the world. His works are auctioned at record prices and have been exhibited in recent years in the largest museums in London, New York, Chicago and L.A. attracting huge audiences. Get to know Moholy-Nagy with this short commissioned by the Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design in Budapest.

Overthink life, dear people? Young Yacob is no different. While thinking too much about what the future brings, on a summer day he meets a spirit in the field who takes him into the flash forwards of his life, showing that the flow of that life is unconventionally beautiful.

Mother is a brave Indian animated short about a woman who is haunted by the nightmare of her childhood and her own destiny - the destiny of becoming the next village circumciser. When she is asked to take up the job and circumcise her own daughter, she realizes she can't abide by the traditions and customs of her community. She must fight back.

A hell of a ride! Explosive, funny and horrific at the same time, this anarchic short takes you on a trip with the diligent soldier Mr. Pete who does everything to meet the high standards of his baroness. To satisfy her insatiable lust for speed he shovels madly on her new iron horse's voyage.

What do you have to do to get your father's attention?! Drawn from personal experience, the beautiful yet painful short film shows a reckless boy seeking attention of his father, a photographer. Being confronted with his father's artistic chaos and his obsessive fascination for photography-life, on his way of growing up these elements eventually become essential for strengthening their father-son bond. Using a combination of hand-drawn and stop-motion animation in the collage technique, the filmmaker takes you on a ride through much more than just a personal experience.

A deeply personal and insightful tale about the female experience in (historical) Taiwan, Wu-Ching Chang's short is a tribute to his grandmother who, as a T'ung-yang-hsi, was sold as a young girl to another family to be raise as a future daughter-in-law. Trying to be true to the historical context, the narration is based on interviews with the director's grandmother's children, and research in feminism. With a variety of animation techniques, including egg yolk as paint, the film aims to reflect on a past in order to fight for a better future. As the metaphor of women, the eggs are the symbolization of the productive roles in a male-dominated society. Eggs are fragile, but at the same time tough. Wu-Ching Chang's grandmother is an egg.

A Czech woman marries into a working-class Afghan family in 21st-century Kabul in Michaela Pavlátová's latest feature film. Acclaimed director Michaela Pavlátová – an Academy Award nominee, winner of a Golden Bear and a Best Film winner at Annecy – finds a highly original narrative angle to dissect the condition of women in post-Taliban Kabul. Based on a novel by Czech journalist Petra Procházková (who is married to an Afghan man), My Sunny Maad tells the story of Helena (later called Herra), a young Czech woman who falls in love at first sight with Nazir, an Afghan. Two months and three days later, Herra is married into a working-class Afghan family in 21st-century Kabul. The film eerily captures the place of women in Afghan society, but also questions our own Western xenophobia towards traditions we don't always (want to) understand. Here, a white European woman learns how to adapt to a society she hardly knew, facing misogyny as well as the warmth of an Afghan family. Pavlátová offers a nuanced and humanistic perspective of life. In a vibrant Middle East city, which is stunningly brought to life by lithe 2D animation and an atmospheric sound design, Herra becomes our guide into understanding Afghan social mores and cultural differences Western outsiders in the city encounter. Seven years in the making, My Sunny Maad is an exhilarating portrait that will certainly strike a chord.
