films.syn: In the thirteenth century, at the time of the attack of the Mongols, a young musician and the love of his life are separated from each other. Fifty years after the incident, after Persia bowed to the invaders, the musician is summoned to perform at the castle of the Mongols where his beloved is being held. Meticulously crafted and with an achingly beautiful score, the film pays homage to love in times of extreme sorrow.

Sharing the title with George A. Romero's ultimate zombie classic, Ida Melum's sweet horror stop-motion short is a funny, yet visceral depiction of anxiety. When a power-cut ruins Ruby's bedtime routine she finds herself haunted by embarrassing past version of herself. The only way for Ruby to get a peaceful night of sleep is to confront her visitors and accept herself just as she is.
A colourful cut-out music video for a song by cuban artist Carlos Fidel.

On the Surface is a touching narration by Fan Sissoko - a French-Malian artist and filmmaker based in Reykjavik - about being an immigrant, a Black woman and a mother. With textured brush strokes, the film portrays Ada, a young black woman who goes swimming in the Icelandic sea as she reflects on her experience of raising a child in a country that feels nothing like home. She enters the freezing water and relives her traumatic pregnancy and postnatal depression. But nature has always proven to be healing.

Any one who has ever worked in a restaurant or had to wash piles of dishes can relate to this joyful short! We follow a girl who works as a spooly of a restaurant and starts to daydream during her shift. It doesn't take long before her imagination starts to mix with reality and she gets caught in the middle of it all.

Never, never press buttons that you are not supposed to press. But discourage by waiting for his coffee, Patrick enters a curious room filled with buttons. Transported by the music, he is unaware of the consequences of each button he presses. A short about how humanity unwittingly(?) is destroying the planet.

Petipou and his friend Egg live happily in their world of games and recklessness. But one day, a Foot-Bird bursts into their peaceful life and kidnaps Egg. Petipou leaves to chase the Foot-Bird and discover the true goal of these creatures. Creative in every way - to surrealist and Lynchian extremes - Elliot Audigé's student work is a feast of imagination.

A brilliant explainer, this educational short film explains the importance of physical distancing to help reduce Covid-19 infection. Written and produced by Development Media International and targeted to the whole African continent.

Not every burglar is a handyman. This burglar ... well, he makes a mess trying to break into a museum to steal a piece of art. This Dutch short is a wonderful and creative piece of art itself. A joy to watch, even if its protagonist really sucks at his job. Maybe he can't steal art, but he can steal the show!

Plug into the pig! A group of animals hook up a power grid to the socket-shaped snout of one big, sleeping pig. The animals use the pig's energy for simple things at first, but soon they render themselves dependent on a city where every single thing - the useful and the useless - is automated ... How long can that last? A humorous fable that leaves it up to the viewer to draw their own conclusions about our resources and the climate crisis.

Holy cow, this is a WTF phantasmagoric free-fall into craziness! Montrealer Davide Di Saro's music video for oddball Toronto art-popper Ronley Teper follows the adventure of Red the Pimple, crossing multiple dimensions and surviving vertiginous falls, psychedelic landscapes and colourful voracious creatures. To survive, creativity is the only possible salvation.

The fresh and colourful Poum Poum! is a musical animated film which celebrates the simple and childish joy of hitting drums, scribbling on paper using marker pens, splashing paint or making cracked cymbals screech. The short finds chaos, mishaps amusing and aims at spreading a spontaneous creative energy.

What is the secret of Chimney Town, a town covered in smoke, where everyone has forgotten to look up? If you believe, the world will change. Ever had a friend who smells terrible? Well, Lubicchi has one. But hey, that friend is also literally a creature made out of trash. Yet, they are the ones who will change Chimney Town, a grimy metropolis, forever. What is the secret of Chimney Town, a town covered in smoke, where everyone has forgotten to look up? Dreams are laughed at. Stars? Haha, don't make the townspeople laugh! But one man, Bruno the tailor, believed that "beyond the smoke, there might be stars". One day, Bruno disappeared, leaving behind his son Lubicchi who - despite a fear of heights - is a dedicated chimney sweeper following his father's teachings to look up to the sky. Lubicchi meets Poupelle, a garbage monster. Together they embark on a thrilling and heartfelt adventure. Poupelle of Chimney Town is Yusuke Hirota's directorial debut and the latest feature by the Tokyo-based animation studio STUDIO4°C, which is world-renowned for its cutting-edge visual expression. Just google Mind Game , Genius Party , Tekkonkinkreet and Children of the Sea and you'll see what we mean! This multifaceted anime eco-fable is based on Nishino Akihiro's popular picturebook which sold over 700,000 copies. The comedian-author had always wanted to see a film version of his book and wrote the screenplay and served as a producer here. Reminiscent of the best Miyazaki stories, this anime treasure will touch both kids and adults, and will make you look up. Just don't hurt your neck!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: A passionate short about grandma Catherina and her love for ballet. Commissioned by Stichting De Grote Haay.

Apart from being a helluva good word in a scrabble game, Prosopagnosia is a neurodiverse behaviour known as "face blindness", which basically means you can't remember or recognize faces. Filmmaker Steven Fraser lives with prosopagnosia and uses stop-motion animation, cassette tapes, sketchbooks, photos, and diary extracts to convey his feelings about this. By means of film, we begin to understand the importance of faces, the coping mechanisms that can be exercised and the different ways you can you live your life when you cannot remember a face.

MURDER MYSTERYYYY!!! A series of murders in strange circumstances is devastating the city and there is only one person who is capable of finding the culprit: Toni Clues. Reminiscent of Aardman's stop-motion films and with clever funny references to classics as Seven and Psycho, this hilarious spoof on the detective genre holds an unmistakable commentary on meat consumption. It's also deliriously gory!

How do you look at yourself? Are you in peace with your flaws? Sanna de Vries' award-winning short shows the power of taking some distance, of 'zooming out' and stepping out of that spiral of self-loathing. We follow protagonist Fiep who lives in a little house with mirrors. Fiep focuses on her physical imperfections so intensely that her distorted self-image grows out of proportion - literally...
There is always a reason to keep going! This short presents a discussion about the positive and negative aspects of living in the world of today. Motivational speech: check!

Animal lives matter! In this cute and lighthearted film, a Czech animal rescuer talks about her experience with adoption of handicapped animals and shares stories of an old sick Chihuahua, a paralyzed French Bulldog and a frightened cat finding their perfect human companion.

films.t: Save Ralph – A Short Film with Taika Waititi
films.syn: No animal should suffer and die in the name of beauty. Produced by The Humane Society International, directed by Spencer Susser ( Hesher ) and featuring an all-star multinational cast including Taika Waititi, Ricky Gervais, Zac Efron, Olivia Munn, Pom Klementieff and more, Save Ralph is a powerful stop-motion short in which the bunny Ralph is being interviewed for a documentary while going through his daily routine as a "tester" in a lab.

Never stop resisting the forces of repression. This film is a traumatic memory, a testimony, and a radical protest. Mutated bodies come into the frame as an alien power tries to subdue them. But resistance is on the rise. Cinema as a haunting scream that disrupts everything the cycle of oppression.

Perhaps the first ever animation film of its kind in the Malayalam language, Seen It! takes you on a spooky tour of some local Indian spirits, guided by the ever-vibrant Mr. Panicker who has several shockers up his sleeve. With its cartoony style and the look of black-and-white graphic novel, the film paints a quirky picture of the supernatural encounters of its narrator.

Well, that's a bit awkward ... A cat goes to a job interview where his skills are valued by ... three mice. As the interview progresses the situation becomes increasingly uncomfortable for everyone involved. A perfect portrayal of how threatening and terrifying an audition is ... even for a cat.

K, the musician who covers his face, and untouchable cat 'Chicha', are both lonely. They are always together but never get close. After finally getting a scratch on his hand, K lays down and starts singing a serenade for Chicha alone. A colourful and dreamy music clip.

films.t: Shikoko – My Lover is Made in Cairo
films.syn: A 'faux old' tribute to Mahmoud Shikoko - an Egyptian actor and puppet artist - and a sort of animated remake of one his songs: Habibi Shoghl Cairo, which means "My Love is Made in Cairo".

Winter, 1895. In a small Ukrainian village, farmer Shlomo is expecting his tenth child. Thrown into a panic, he runs to the rabbi for some advice and discovers that, in life as in physics, everything is relative. But not before slapstick ensues and we get to witness pure mayhem at the family house!

We can all agree: it's not easy to reveal your feelings to someone. Yet, Prom - your local lesbian fantasy postal worker - is willing to give it a try. Sincerely follows her as she finally decides to deliver her most important letter yet; a letter to her crush. That is, of course, if Prom and her letter can make it to their destination in one piece.
Perhaps the most important thing in a relationship is space. Zhong Xian's short lightheartedly captures the essence of a romantic relationship.

"It's like a gnome shagged a mushroom!", says one of the rowdy teenagers who are trekking into an isolated forest and discover peaceful mushroom creatures. But the adorable little creatures also turn out to be an unexpected force of nature. Sprite Fright is an 80s-inspired horror comedy which looks like a demented take on The Smurfs and The Lorax . It will most certainly caught you off guard!

Made in traditional 2D animation, Summer Nights is a wild and warm music video for the Argentinian electropop rock band Siamés. Three old friends have a ritual to welcome a new member of the "cool kid" gang. A get-together with past summers, that brings back childhood memories.

Phew, this is some hot stuf! One hot summer afternoon, Rosa is sunbathing in her garden, when suddenly her peace and quiet is cut short by the sound of a lawnmower. The gardener is out working next door, and Rosa is watching, increasingly intoxicated by the tender way he handles the garden's flowers. A kinky, cute summer short!

If corona has reminded us of anything, it's that having dinner together with a group of people fills with happiness. Here, a group gathers around a table. The food is served in a noisy environment, toasts are made and a happy birthday is sung, while we listen to the conversations. At some point there are already people sleeping, reading, and even flirting. And in the end, only dirty dishes and silence remain. A joyful, yet quiet short about the lively experience of being together.

films.t: TED-ED: How the Monkey King Escaped the Underworld
films.syn: A wonderful cut-out animation on the famous Chinese tale of the Monkey King. This legendary troublemaker succeeds in stealing the Dragon Lord's most treasured weapon: a magical staff. Returning to his kingdom to show off his treasure to his tribe of warrior monkeys, he finds himself caught in the clutches of two soul collectors, dragging him. to his death. Shunan Teng details the Monkey King's journey to the underworld. Commissioned by TED-Ed.

films.t: TED-ED: The Myth of the Stolen Eyeballs
films.syn: It's all about myths at this year's Kaboom! And oh boy, have we got a myth for you. Deep in the Amazon rainforest in the river Nea'ocoyá lived a school of particularly big and tasty fish. When the rains came and the water rose the fish appeared, and swam away as the waters fell. Villagers along the river followed them to a lagoon and set up camp. But their young shaman soon sensed they might not be completely alone ... Nathan D. Horowitz details the Siekopai myth of the air goblins. Commissioned by TED-Ed.

Telling a sort of new Genesis with a whole unique cosmography, the stupendously animated Terra Incognita follows life on a mysterious island, inhabited by immortal beings. These beings lead a pre-civilized life forgotten by time, spending their endless days in hedonistic lethargy. Through anecdotal vignettes, the film shows what happens when these beings are visited by the outside world, and whether or not there is a greater meaning to it all.

When a New Year, in the form of a rowdy toddler, arrives in a frozen forest, and brings along the thaw, the Previous Year, in the form of an old man of snow and ice, tries to protect "his" forest. An impressively animated short made in the framework of Ultrakort.
A child, a young man, an adult, and an old man walk alternately to doom, finding two shiny shoes on their way. Quirkily animated, the latest short by Paul Driessen is again a cynical must-see!

Made in Hong Kong by French animators Stéphanie Lansaque & François Leroy, The Awakening of the Insects is one hell of a powerful and disturbing short. Set in Hong Kong, this 2D animated film focuses on Mr. Lam, an old gentleman slipping who is losing his memory, and his caretaker Ms. Meng, a devout Taoist. On March 5, the day of the awakening of the insects, Lam receives an unexpected visit of his caretaker who is determined to exorcise the demons lodging in the head of the old man. Hold tight for a rollercoaster of paranoia and confusion.

Who will best play her part: the dancing lioness or the little girl we attempt to tame? Only the Boob Fairy will know who is really worthy of her attention. This grotesque short shows two portraits that combine and characterize the violence of two oppressions of our time: the conditioning and education of young girls with a certain definition of femininity and the training of wild animals for entertainment.

An ode to the people, cultures and landscapes of South America, The Cloudmaker lets us get acquainted with the charismatic Hipólito, an old man who transforms clouds into wondrous figures. But he has grown weary, and in order to return to his true love on Earth, he first has to find a worthy successor.

Mermaid movies are the best! And here's a new one! In this cute Ukrainian short, a lonely chubby mermaid is keen on peeking at people through water pipes using magic. One day, during such a spying, the mermaid falls in love with a man, and blinded by passion, comes to his apartment.

films.t: The Difference Between Mongol and Mongoloid
films.syn: Some people are different. Some humans are born with a set of variable characteristics, which they call Down syndrome. A flying saucer, dinosaurs and storks help us try to understand what it is and what the difference is between having it or not. With its cut-out collage style, newspaper texture and quick pace, this short is way more than just a (personal) history lesson.

films.t: The Girl Who Built a Rocket
films.syn: The Girl Who Built a Rocket is a heartfelt tale based on real-life humans and their very real struggles. In February 2021, three space missions went into the Mars orbit, with the aim to look for water on the planet. This film, however, was made to bring a new angle to the water crisis - here on Earth. Follow the story of Fara, a young Madagascan girl who imagines building a spaceship to go to Mars and find water for her dry town... The short was made for the powerful WaterAid campaign to raise awareness on the shortage of clean water in many parts of the world.

How many times have you longed to escape reality? You can maybe get some help from The Intronauta, the navigator of inner space! Jose Arboleda's clever Colombian short is a DIY cardboard style animation and a first-person journey into an escapist world. In a world saturated with media information, the protagonist escapes to a fantastical space thanks to his ability to draw. Through his drawings, a plant emerges from the cracks of the city, but the social oder wipes it out, motivating him to become The Intronauta.
What if Laughter itself, laughingly, left mankind? Picture for a moment a world without colour or spark... right before you burst into laughter!

The Candle. The Myth. The Legend. Mountain Lodge. Jordan Wong has succeeded in making a horny desktop film... about a candle. This short is a digital collage of sorts in which Wong dives into the Internet rabbit hole, perhaps the weirdest hole of all.

films.t: The Name of the Plum Blossom
films.syn: Family really matters. Gather round for a touching personal story of a daughter, and her mum who became a tailor in 80s China, just to give her brothers a chance for an education. The Name of the Plum Blossom is a mixed-media film that combines hand-drawn animation, animated photo collage and stop-motion techniques.

What is real and what is hallucination? In this Dionysian fantasy à la David Lynch, a couple rushes out of glamorous party. On their way home, an argument leads to a brutal car accident. When the man regains consciousness, the woman has disappeared. He will then experience a real descent into hell. The night is full of surprises.

Are we not that different from animals after all? For a long time, humanity has separated itself from animality. But the more scientists know about non-human animals, the more they see similarities with humans. We need animal emancipation to go forward. This short makes a start in breaking down human's hierarchical ideas about other animals, using real-life examples.
On a journey through history, we see how reuse has been the norm up until now. How will history judge us. Made as part of The Animation Workshop (Viborg, Denmark).

On 17 October 1961, the "Algerian workers" in France decided to demonstrate peacefully in the streets of Paris against the curfew imposed on them by the police headquarters. An exceptional, moving and political graduation film by a wonderful team of animators.

Journey into Inuit mysticism with Zacharias Kunuk's beguiling short. Based on an Inuit story the director heard, this authentic film follows a young shaman facing her first test: a trip underground to visit Kannaaluk, The One Below, who holds the answers to why a community member has become ill. Filmmaker Zacharias Kunuk won the Caméra d'Or in Cannes in 2001 with Atanarjuat: The Fast Runner , the first indigenous Inuk film with an all indigenous cast and entirely in Inuktitut. His work is steeped in Inuit traditional beliefs and spirituality.

films.t: The Tale of the Green Cheese
films.syn: Did someone say bestiality? This wickedly menacing and deliriously funny short follows a farmer who lives an idyllic life in the Swiss Alps, until one of his goats gives birth to a creature that looks more like the farmer than a goat. Trying to hide the traces of this, he hits on a winning formula for a new brand of cheese.

Get on board for this one, because The Timekeepers of Eternity is one of the most unique and radical storytelling experiments of the year. It's also radically entertaining and marks a groundbreaking use of archive film footage and a scrapbook-like collage technique. Stephen King fans can rejoice! Greek director Aristotelis Maragkos has taken the 1995 miniseries, television film so you will, The Langoliers and turned it into a hypnotic remix art piece that spirals into the upper echelon of King adaptations. Maragkos has printed every frame of Tom Holland's TV movie to paper and then meticulously reconstructed and reshaped it through black and white collage animation. Actual film footage is torn and manipulated to create a wholly new take on the discarded and forgotten adaptation of The Langoliers . By pushing the medium's boundaries, the director has revitalized an almost campy and over-the-top piece of television. Stephen King's novel (and its TV adaptation) tells the peculiar story of a group of strangers who have woken up aboard a redeye flight from Boston to L.A. to the surreal discovery that the plane's crew and passengers have vanished. As they take control of the aircraft and investigate the mystery, a terrible sound emerges. One of the passengers is Mr. Toomey, a businessman who obsessively tears paper to control his childhood monsters. In Maragkos' film, this delusional character takes front and center as Toomey must confront the paper nightmare which threatens to rip everything apart.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.t: The Ultimate “Star Wars: A New Hope” Recap Cartoon
films.syn: With their recap videos of iconic films and series, Cas van de Pol & Junaid Chundrigar are kings of the internet. This hilarious spoof summarizes the first Star Wars movie in truly unique fashion. It's maybe not entirely how you remembered Star Wars, but hey, you don't hear us complaining! The force is strong with this one!

films.t: There Must Be Some Kind of Way Out of Here
films.syn: Why do we love disaster films? Why do we love the idea of seeing the apocalypse on screen? Exploiting the spectacular images of destruction, Rainer Kohlberger's toys with our desire to overturn the status quo and the opposite desire to find it instantly restore, and questions postmodern pop culture. Are we our own doom?

There She Is!! was a popular South Korean flash cartoon series back in 2004, and thanks to some crowdfunding there is now a new episode! In a society where interracial love is dismissed, three brothers, a mixed breed of rabbit and lion, have memories of hatred and discrimination from an early age. For fans: this episode explores the origins of the Jjintta Set and why they ultimately decided the help Doki and Nabi (the protagonists of the early There She Is!! ) find their love.
We all love uncomfortable, dark cinema from time to time. In Thing a little creature with sharp teeth haunts a man, who is ultimately driven to the edge.

films.t: This is Why Girls Go to the Bathroom Together
films.syn: The million dollar question: why do girls go the bathroom together? This short finally reveals the true reason.

Australian animator Felix Colgrave is a creative wonder, which is why his Youtube channel is so popular. As weird as it is, Colgrave's style is utterly distinctive. Throat Notes is a psychedelic look at the bizarre backyard creatures you might cross paths with in Tasmania and the strange things they might be up to.

Mexico really has a great tradition of stop-motion and Tío lives up to that reputation. On his first day of work as a miner, Martin, a cocky teenager will learn the importance of rituals and respect for his ancestors. Ready for some intense suspense?

To the beat of dripping chemo, an infusion stand fights for the life of a cancer patient. But he is resisting tenaciously. If only death was not constantly making a courtesy call on him. The stand determinedly continues its mission that only finishes with the last drop.

All the way from Australia comes a truly bonkers short. The fall of a civilization leaves a desolate landscape where a single fascist - black hat included - hammers away at the constant resurgence of happiness.

A polar bear dreams of playing the piano. When he passes the concert hall on an easy evening stroll, he hears some music coming from inside the hall. He looks through the window. A professional pianist is playing a Steinway! He decides to go in and give it a go himself. Then he gets detected…

How about a happy music clip for a happy song about a happy relationship? This Israeli music clip captures a journey between moments, moods and consciousness, which produce a portrait of a romantic relationship.

Go on an invigorating walk with this visually bold Russian short. Sasha Svirsky's film is about the transformation and inner liberation of the protagonist, who found himself in the bleak sequence of everyday life of an office worker. He finally goes out of that tight square where he has been used to sitting and embraces the brave new world!
A bonkers music clip for a song by hardcore punks Einä Ninnts.

films.t: We Hope You Won’t Need to Come Back
films.syn: Displaying some wonderfully tender storytelling, Anastazja Naumenko's short proves that you don't need complex visuals to explore complex themes. A young girl has immigrated. Functioning in a new environment is slowly turning into a routine, and she herself - into a modern Frankenstein's creation.

"Stop thinking!" How many times have you had to say that to yourself? Here is a story about a girl who can't stop thinking, what causes her to end up in a chaotic imaginary world full of her own thoughts. In this world, she has to find a solution for all her overthinking and regain her piece of mind.

With its tantalizing title, What Dying Feels Like features a mouse reciting childhood memories in a sterile living room. Shards of an alienating past paint the portrait of human life. A sense of loss pervades the atmosphere as she's torn between being human and being mouse, between being alive and being in a simulation.

films.t: What Really Happened During the Attica Prison Rebellion
films.syn: Dig into the story America's most famous prison uprising, the Attica Prison Rebellion, where prisoners took control of the facility in response to inhumane living conditions, and the violent retaking that followed. Commissioned by TED-Ed.

Don't let your dreams be dreams! You can become anything. This short shows a growing girl's wild imaginations of what she wants to be when she grows up. Commissioned by publishing house Pratham Books.

Thanks to penis-like fauna and flora, little nipple men and a stylish vintage look, you're immediately hooked on this Danish short, in which the life of a colorful beast is abruptly interrupted by the arrival of a small group of humans that are determined to subdue him.

Attention, attention! A person, or rather a diary, is missing!! Where is our beloved Anne Frank? Could you help us look? Where is Anne Frank is Ari Folman's visionary and kids-friendly update of the story of Anne Frank. Rather than focusing on Anne Frank herself, Folman chooses to make Frank's imaginary friend Kitty - whom Anne wrote to - the protagonist. Originally commissioned by the Anne Frank Fonds, the film starts in the Anne Frank House 75 years after the world's most famous diary was written. Miraculously, Kitty comes to life but finds herself alone and confused. Where is her Anne? Kitty sets out on a quest to find her friend. The story of Anne Frank remains a crucial one to tell. We can all agree on that. So dear parents, arrange a special family night out to educate ánd entertain your children with this wonderful take on a diary that must never be forgotten! And that's a belief shared by the celebrated Israeli animation filmmaker Ari Folman. After Waltz with Bashir and The Congress , Folman revitalizes the diary of Anne Frank by giving it a present-day urgency. We travel through modern-day Amsterdam as well as through Kitty's memories of the Secret Annex where she and Anne talked bout movie stars, the boys in school and being Jewish. The innovative screenplay draws parallels between the present humanitarian crises and the important life lessons of Anne Frank, which makes the film so much more than a retelling of the wartime story of one of Amsterdam's bravest girl. Has Anne Frank become no more than a name on tourist attractions? As in all Folman's work, the animation is vividly rendered. The film is composed out of 159,000 drawings made in fifteen different countries. A team of animators even created a miniature model of the Secret Annex. Folman used it to record images of real scenery, after which he added 2D animated characters onto these backgrounds. The director also has a personal connection with the material: his parents arrived at the gates of Auschwitz the same week as the family ... Frank.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: An experimental, animated short movie from Saudi Arabia that takes us on a linear journey, following a string of interconnected phone calls between five individuals that eventually escalate to a bigger conflict. The film explores the concepts of communication, self-destruction, and their domino effect.

What if 'images' become the only reality that is still visible? In this speculative fiction, all the world's photographs have transformed into the objects they represent. The short shows a dizzying architecture, a world where images have gained the upper hand. Piles of selfies, cats, and meals are scattered everywhere. An experimental short that really makes yourself question your behaviour.

An unsettling, almost creepy stop-motion film about the consequences of capitalist and liberal economic development of Latin America. A couple of peasants create an informal metallurgy workshop in the outskirts of Bogotá in the hope of a better life. The social, environmental and organic consequences they must endure in order to adapt to the industrial capitalism that storms Latin America affects dramatically their relationship and their history.

"I'm a dog who lives in the park under a bridge. Awoooooooo!" A Dog Under a Bridge started with filmmaker Rehoo Tang walking under a bridge in China. Here was a quiet, deserted, and wild park with people who seemed abandoned by society and who tried to eliminate the loneliness in their lives. To fit in, he imagined himself as a stray dog living alone. Rehoo Tang ended up winning the Jury Award for Best Graduation Film in Annecy.

A decade on from the release of Back to the Start , which won the Grand Prix for Branded Content and Entertainment at Cannes Lions, Mexican fast-food chain Chipotle has unveiled a sequel. Having changed the global conversation around animal welfare, the farming family epic now turns the focus on human welfare. To support the film's message of regeneration, Grammy award-winning singer Kacey Musgraves has reimagined Coldplay's "Fix You" as the score to the film.

In what seems a dreamy night, a fluoroscopy bus carries the crowd from the center to the edge of the city. In the fixed and crowded carriage, some people just boarding the bus collide with each other, and some people are taking a nap. Depicting a society that increasingly alienates and isolates us, the film is a fragmented and microscopic perspective on thoughts in crowded spaces.

The beauty of watercolour animation is on full display in this wonderfully metaphorical short by Amandine Meyer, which serves as a follow-up of a graphic novel of hers. In a pastel-coloured frenzy, the filmmaker traces the development from being an infant to an adult woman and artist. Whether about femininity, motherhood or the gift of being an artist, this stream of consciousness is sure to tap into every emotion.

Love is as beautiful as it is scary. Balancing between reality and imagination, this work by Hungarian animator Vivien Hárshegyi shows a girl falling in love again. Caught in a whirlpool of old memories, she runs away and relives the highs and lows of her first relationship. Will she be able to free her soul to face the future with an open heart?

We all know them, those hot summer afternoons, lying on the couch ... If only those damn mosquitos would stay away! Aldo shows the clash between a man and a mosquito, and the guilt after the battle is fought.

A candy-coloured psychedelic trip if ever there was one, Amok is truly one of a kind. After losing his fiancée and his good looks in a freak accident involving an evil Santa Claus gnome, Clyde must confront his inner demons. This winner of Cristal for a Short Film in Annecy is a twisted fever dream with a lot of heart ... and a lot of colour.

A visceral experience with a clear anti-war message, this animated short was made for 'Emergency', a humanitarian NGO, and shows the devastating consequences of war and conflict, from WWII to the refugee camps of the 6-Day War, from the attack on the Mostar bridge to the cars set on fire in the war in Syria.

A cabinet as the storage of family memories is a beautiful metaphor to built a film on. In this personal documentary, a young woman searches for her Armenian roots by interviewing her father, her uncle, and her great aunt. Armat is an examination of collective traumas that are passed down from generation to generation.

A sort of marriage between the precise shots of Chantal Akerman and the study of movement by Muybridge, this experiment in film sets the stage for a hitherto unseen magical life form. Arrest in Flight focuses on the character of movement, when transferred to an alien object thus endowed with the life derived from the movement's true to life source.

films.t: Au Cas où le Corps Exulte
films.syn: An impressive student work about the exploitation in the porn industry and the role of the camera as a voyeuristic accomplice, Au cas où le corps exulte lets us in on the lives of a young camera operator and his friend who is an actress. Shooting a rape scene with his friend taking part, the camera man (un)willingly becomes more of an actor of this rotten system than a mere witness.

Practice makes perfect. Does that also apply for an avatar? Nikita Diakur wants to learn a backflip, but that's not exactly safe. You can break your neck, or land on your head, or hurt your wrists. So, he let his avatar learn the trick. Practicing on a 6-core processor, Fake Nikita makes thousands of attempts to do a backflip with the help of Machine Learning. Highly entertaining and equally hilarious, this experimental film mixes age-old slapstick routines with modern tech.
When two neighbours literally and figuratively disrupt each other's rhythm of life, a musical feud arises that shakes their balconies. Instantly and painfully recognisable for some!
Animated trailer to celebrate the 25th edition of the Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival in South Korea.

Seemingly a sly commentary on manhood standards and gender roles, Japanese director Atsushi Wada's latest short dips into a sort of ritual mysticism. Children dance to music under the supervision of their teacher. A young girl attends the scene and comes to disturb their ritual. Bird in the Peninsula received a Special Mention at the 2022 Berlinale.

A perfect, yet hilariously morbid post-Covid story about a mysterious disease that sweeps through the bird population. Everything goes to hell - planes crash, cities burn, all ends - but at least we get to enjoy this WTF-short.

A giant talkative frog casually reciting Nietzsche, Joseph Conrad and Ernest Hemingway sets out to save Tokyo from a massive worm with the help of a schizophrenic bank employee whose co-worker is trying to cope with his frustrated wife and his stray cat. All of this happens right after the devastating earthquake in the city in 2011. This remarkable mishmash forms the basis of French composer-filmmaker Pierre Földes' debut feature, inspired by a handful of Haruki Murakami's short stories. The literary world of Murakami - one of the greatest writers of contemporary literature - balances fantasy and reality, and is filled with cigarette smoke, pondering men, playful philosophy, sex and irony. Bringing his stories to the big screen is tricky, certainly in live-action. Animation might be a better fit, according to Pierre Földes. Between existentialism and delightful irony, and with a characteristic touch of absurdity, the filmmaker perfectly captures the spirit of Murakami's language. As if the two of them are on the same unique wavelength. To convince the famous author and his entourage to sell the rights, the animator even created a "graphic bible" presenting his approach. "What is visible to everyone is not the most important thing", the frog says in the film. But Földes' innovative visual style is one of the highlights of this adaptation. For each shot, a live-action reference was first filmed. Afterwards, the animators would swap the actors' heads for a 3D model of the character's face. Behind all the absurdity - both narratively and visually - are portraits of people struggling with the shadows of their fears and weaknesses, searching for themselves and their place in the world. Before the screening of 'Blind Willow, Sleeping Woman' the Murakami-inspired short film 'Yomoyama Short Stories' by Fuka Katayama will be shown.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: For 18-year-old Finnish-Kosovan Fatu, a simple visit to the grocery store feels as nerve-racking as a lunar expedition: for the first time in his life, he's wearing full glam makeup in public. Luckily his best friend Rai is there to support him through the voyage. Making full use of stop-motion puppetry, the film shows how no one should be afraid to show their true self. Most of the dialogue in Blush is documentary and was recorded during a real trip to a grocery store.

The stuff of spacey nightmares, but also kinda cute, and terrifying, and eerie, but still cute. Anyway, this is a story about a man and a cat. No sorry ... A man, a cat and a dream. Wait ... probably a man, a cat, a dream and a vespa! It's about relationships and how they can shape our lives forever. But maybe it's just a story about a man and a cat. Who knows ...

Dreamlike and exhibiting some strange floral nostalgia, Nocturnal Thought Bus is a music video for the titular song by German band Crystal Glass. The song's lyrics are about those nights in which you're caught in an endless spiral of thoughts and taken on a journey that you have no power over. Those thoughts appear to the protagonist as a foreboding but colourful cast of characters.

The edgy and personal student film Cupid into Transmutation follows a transgender boy named Caesar living in a big city. On the run from his traumatic past, he tries to make a living as a camboy. Until he is suddenly sent into hysteria as his body starts to violently morph and transform beyond all recognition. Follow him in his search for acceptance and identity in this cruel world, focused on normality and outer beauty.

In a very clear and simple style German animator and cartoonist Andreas Hykade asks a very important question: what does power do to us? Despite its short length and almost childlike design, Dealing with War is an impressive film featuring two peaceful sheep and one violent dog.

Diaphony is a hypnotising short animated documentary taking you on a sensory, auditory journey. The film follows three people who share their experiences of the pandemic. Each handles this difficult time in their own way, but it turns out that they share the same way of finding comfort through music. As their worlds begin to intertwine in the animation, the short shows how societal and political differences that have grown through the pandemic, vanish when we find consolation and meaning in music.

It seems to be Judgement Day in a gray apartment building when a cruel chain of events upset seven sinful pigs (and a righteous passerby). The only witnesses are two playful angels. This very first short by the Maru Collective from Australia is one of morbid proportions.

A story for the millions of refugees all over the world for whom their home has turned into a dark place, Diyar revolves around a man who has to leave everything behind and tries to keep the light of home alive on his way to his new destination. A compelling and personal student film.

Oh, how relatable ... Clinging to every last bit of his relationship, a young man hangs onto his ex's dachshund. Quite literally so, which creates chaos in town. For how long will this relational sorrow be stretched?

What's so special about a dog running after a ball at the park? This fascinating short presents a new and experimental perspective on it. We are all one after all: human, dog, tennis ball, nature ... We are all particles in space.

"Don't die on me". Really, again? It's like every time an asthmatic person coughs, he has to deal with that irritating sentence. An expressive short with a lot of snot and a lot of coughing, Don't Die on Me is a revolting portrayal of the noisy life inside a malfunctioning body, and the deadly silence that stops it.

Don't Fear the Finger is a funny, yet truly purposeful short made for the Argentine League for the Fight Against Cancer. Using finger puppets singing the titular song, Fran Colombatti's animated campaign commercial raises awareness on prostate cancer.
Enya's journey trying to make it as a dancer is hindered as her behaviours drag her downhill in this Lebanese student film.

On an empty little rock in an empty black sea lived empty little people ... with a compulsive thirst for tea. And tea is running out on Halloween night ... Protect your tea from these little rascals!!!

Get ready for the greatest adventure ... before your life! Two former lovers seeking closure meet up one last time. This sets up an epic chain of events that may alter the course of their lives forever.

Telling the personal story of Antonia Jardenia da Silva from Brazil, and of how she was forced to relocate, Finding Home is the first film in a series that features testimonies of climate refugees from around the world uprooted from their homes. Director Maria Stanisheva highlights both environmental and human issues with the raw power of animation.
Guided by a sensual TV chef, Roger is preparing dinner for a date when he gets bitten by the salmon he is cooking. But wait, is that ... a fin? Oh my ... is he turning into ... ? Cancel that date!!!

Golden Calf winner Patty Stenger returns with a quirky yet utterly meaningful short about a caring daughter who reluctantly sees her elderly mother reclaim control of her own life. The latter feels that if she will die anyway, she prefers to do so with love and fun. In a deliberately raw style, we follow the mother's path to renewed happiness.

Love is messy! "I wanna fight, marry, kiss you all in one day." Yep, relatable. This bright and colourful dark comedy is a music video for a song by American singer-songwriter GAYLE (featuring blackbear) and sees miniature Gayle and blackbear failing at being good neighbours. Think Celebrity Deathmatch meets Groundhog Day in the style of A Town Called Panic ... A play stop-motion tale of human behaviour gone wrong.

"Pisces have big feet and big hands!" Filmmaker Gina Kamentsky and her mom talk about feet. Using the technique of pixilation, whereby real movements look like animations, Foot Print Shop is a cute and profound short, starring ... feet.

Exploring the effect of past trauma, Freedom Swimmer documents a mass migration story from the 20th century, which is relatively untold in the Western world. Director Olivia Martin McGuire parallels a grandfather's journey to safety from China (swimming to Hong Kong in the 70s) with his granddaughter's fight for freedom in Hong Kong today. A timely, captivating story of the search for a better life.

Fuar: A Counter-Memory emphasises the collective amnesia of the 1922 Great Fire of Smyrna/Izmir by examining the urban park (Fuar) built on top of its ruins. Oblivious to the dark past, the following generations just built counter-memories. By layering two different printmaking techniques, drypoint etching and risograph, the project seeks to highlight the contrast between eras and to inform them of each other. These techniques complement the narrative and explore the transformation of the city.

I think we can all agree that sometimes ... you just gotta say ... FUCK IT. Using different styles and media, Fuck It is a short about not fitting in, wanting to please everyone by acting "right", the stress that it brings and almost drowning in your feelings during the process of it all.

We all deal with grief differently, don't we? Depending on who we are, we conceptualise death in a different way. In this magical visual poem, we find ourselves in a small town where a funeral is held after the death of a gardener. Three brothers are caught up in their imaginations on the day of the burial.

Somewhere between the paintings of Egon Schiele and the eeriness of David Cronenberg lies this mysterious student film. Starting in a science class with a girl who has a crush, the film rapidly descends into a moldy, furry, wet dream-like experiment. When the fumbly feelings of a crush are held out for too long, they turn ugly - and furry.

About the longing to come closer to someone, Fur depicts a girl pursuing a connection with her sister who is covered by a strange grey fur. It may be soft, but it grows between them, and they drift further apart from each other ...

Inspired by the forest fires in Portugal in 2018 and the resilience of the Garrano horse, Vasco Sá and David Doutel made their fourth short film together. Garrano is the inexorable and moody story of the loss of innocence of a young boy. In iconographic painterly animation a Garrano horse is forced to pull a heavy load under a blazing sun while the young boy discovers a man who is about to set a forest on fire. An intense and disheartening tale set in a majestic place where tragedy strikes.

Reminiscent of the whimsical Beatles-inspired Yellow Submarine and filled with bizarre, unorthodox characters, Goodbye Jérôme traces a trip through paradise. Jérôme sets out to find his wife Maryline. In the course of his search, he sinks into a surreal and colourful world in which no one seems to able to help him.

A melancholic sendoff to childhood summers about boyhood friendship and finding happiness. “That day, I thought our summer would go on forever.” In the footsteps of great summery coming-of-age films comes Atsuko Ishizuka’s first original feature film: Goodbye Don Glees! , a transformative journey for its protagonists that makes you reminisce about friendships gone by. We meet teen misfits Roma, Toto and Drop in what will become a pivotal moment in their lives. They call themselves the “Don Glees”, an informal name for their backyard adventures. The trio has a base camp outside town, where they gather and part ways. One day, when the three of them get blamed for a nearby forest fire, they set off into the woods to prove their innocence. As disaster strikes their expedition, tensions flare between the friends as they realise that growing up has taken each of them on wildly different paths. Following up her critically acclaimed series A Place Further than the Universe , director Atsuko Ishizuka (once dubbed the greatest talent along Satoshi Kon in the Madhouse studio) has crafted a grounded anime film evoking the innocence of youth(fulness). Although taking a more lighthearted approach than classics of the genre like Stand by Me, Ishizuka touches on delicate subjects with regards to who we once were and who we want to be. From the get-go you sense there’s something up with Drop, a smiley kid that hides deeper truths. When this emotional trip reaches its almost surreal climax, you’ll get what Drop has been looking for his whole life. Goodbye Don Glees! is a melancholic sendoff to childhood summers that proves the worth of living in the moment.
