films.syn: In Réunion, runaway slaves, gone to live free in the heights of the island, built a kingdom: the interior kingdom of the maroons. In this place borrowed from the invisible, they entered into connection with "Gromonmon". Telling the island's history, this 3D animated film is sure to educate you on a part of forgotten history.

Surely a visit to the hairdresser can't be that exciting? Except, in the hands of animator Dal Park it is! With an aesthetic to die for, this playful little short features a hairdresser trying to keep up with her demanding clients.

films.t: Hallo Vermeer, Girl on a Trip
films.syn: Girl with a Pearl Erring by a Vermeer is one of the most famous paintings in the world. But what a journey around the globe that painting made! This animation was made for the family exhibition Hello Vermeer in the Mauritshuis in The Hague.

Red Dead Redemption 2 is one of the most amazing open-world games out there. But what about the over 1000 non-player characters, the digital extras that populate the background? An ethnographic exploration of the work and daily life of NPCs, the film observes a carpenter, a stable hand, a laundress and a street sweeper whose lives exist merely out of labour routines. Their activities and patterns form a vivid analogy for work under capitalism. You'll never play the game the same way!

Meat is murder! Well, that is, according to these five houseplants who form a secret microcosm on a sunny window sill in Heleen's home. For her birthday, Heleen got a brand new, carnivorous plan called Donna. Will she survive when the plants decide Donna should become a vegetarian?

Your first day in school is never easy, let alone when you have ADD or ADHD. Hi! is the story of a little ADDer child who is encouraged by her mom to go to school by bus. An animation that raises awareness about ADD and helps children who find saying "hi" is not that easy.

By now you know the saying "not all heroes wear capes". This is especially true for some German children whose families are struggling to make ends meet. Almost every 5th child in Germany is at risk of poverty, something which expresses itself in many different ways. This cutely animated and socially relevant film tells the story of three children and their everyday struggles. To cope with reality, they make up the wildest stories, like being a superhero.

They say "home is where the heart is", but what if one doesn't know where exactly their heart is? Omid is an Iranian immigrant in Paris. One evening, in the street, he is attacked and stabbed in the heart. But Omid gets back up! At the hospital, the diagnosis is formal: he has no heart ... Has he left it behind in Iran? A personal story to its director, the film is a humorous yet poignant take on the immigrant experience.

Prehistoric Drenthe, 4000 BC (ish). Four primitive little men are fighting the elements and hunger. One of them is clearly a bit more sophisticated and suggests building more complex structures, but all is sabotaged when a rabbit hops by ... Their clumsiness, however, leads to the building of the mysterious hunebed stones!

BUTTS, BUTTS, BUTTS! In a surreal world of butts and hands, a single act of violence against an oppressed Butt ignites a media frenzy. This leads to a butt empowerment movement seeking to challenge the status quo of their society. Filmmaker Calleen Koh finds joy in turning serious societal problems into wacky stories. Here, she embraces the absurdity of the unyielding power of the media and our current-day obsession with participating in moral outrage.

Mathieu is weighed down by many questions which put him in a heavy state. But as he gives in to his sadness, the rain becomes tears and his tears become rain. He becomes one with his sadness. It's his time to dance, and the tears accompany him. This beautiful symbiosis of music and visuals is a music video for a song by French singer-songwriter Mathieu Boogaerts. It was achieved through the cyanotype photographic printing process, giving the short film very soft textures and a wonderful analog look and feel.

A trailer for a webcomic, How to Adult is a story about a young man as he constantly fails to find the answer to the big question. To young adults, welcoming a new stage of life is really, really weird. Because no one truly knows what they're doing or how the adult world actually works.

films.t: I Am Crying All the Time and I Don’t Know Why
films.syn: The title says it all ... A genuine and relatable stream of thoughts, Jamie Machul's film is a poem of sorts that follows a person's thoughts as they become overwhelmed, confused and ashamed. When the last wave of tears ebbs off we settle in reflection and tranquility.

In three funky minutes, two thieves realise that if you love something, you gotta set it free. Francesca Colombara's animated music video for German artist Klaus Layer tells the story of two weird-looking thieves who steal the Flying Mushrooms and escape across the desert, riding a giant camel. "I usually think about the weirdest things and then I bring them to life", dixit Colombara. Oh, how we love that attitude!

Ice Merchants is the touching story of a father and his son who, every day, jump with a parachute from their vertiginous cold house to go to the village on the ground where they sell the ice they produce. The first ever Portuguese animation to be awarded in Cannes, João Gonzalez's short soulfully deals with grief. Unique and heartfelt. Nominated for the 2023 Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film.

Originally a 360° video installation commissioned by the Nagano Art Museum, Iizuna Fair is a true meditative experience and marriage between the art of painting and film. In the midst of a frenzy night a man finds himself lost in the crevasse of time. A phantom. Inexplicably sad and beguiling, this moving painting is a poetic profusion of faces, bodies and colours.

Abstract and yet inexpressibly haunting, this experimental short by Ukrainian animator Mykyta Lyskov imagines landscapes through purely abstract spots and lines. The viewer is left with their own interpretation.

Captured by slavers, Bai fights back to escape. Surrounded by an infinite ocean, he battles his tormentors to get rid of the name with which they label him ... Ina Kwana Bawa. Animated by Naomi van Heemst, this short is part of Onias Landveld's theatre project Kunu , in which Landveld's texts have taken the shape of animated short thanks to animators and composers.

A film about queer light switches. Yes, really! Capturing teenage angst, confusion and love, this cute stop-motion short explores a love triangle of sorts. Lucie, Maya and their friends are partying. Even the local heartthrob Jimmy joins in and everyone knows he's just there for Maya. However, Maya and Lucie find out they have hidden feelings for each other ...

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: From Hungarian animator Réka Bucsi comes a hypnotising exercise in rhythm and drawing. It's a surprising projection of mental images, which are formed while listening to music. From the simple act of drawing a line, to the intricate movement and complex structure of animation that is able to self-generate.

Masaaki Yuasa's latest is a show-stopping medieval rock opera that dazzles the eye and the mind. "This is a story that took place here some 600 years ago. Taken from us and forgotten - this is our story." Masaaki Yuasa is arguably one of Earth's most uncompromising anime auteurs. If there's one "Maverick" in the art of film, it's not Tom Cruise's Top Gun pilot, but rather the überinspired Japanese filmmaker. His offbeat directorial voice has given us subversive and wildly entertaining features such as Mind Game and - more recently - The Night Is Short, Walk On Girl . Yuasa is such an iconoclast, that it might come as a surprise that he is now celebrating the rigid world of Noh, a traditional Japanese theater form in which masked dancers interpret supernatural tales of old. But - of course - on his own terms, by telling an almost revisionist story in a technically and visually dazzling medieval glam rock opera with show-stopping musical performances. A radical and rebellious anime, Inu-oh is set in 14th-century Japan, when the blind biwa player Tomona and the mysterious, disfigured outcast Inu-oh - characterised by his giant arm with which he can outdance everyone - team up to proof their worth to the people and the establishment. Voiced by Ayu-chan (the gender-fluid lead singer of rock band Queen Bee), Inu-oh is a revolutionist in disguise, challenging all societal codes and conventions by just embracing who he is. Yuasa's imagination - with the help of a novel by Hideo Furukawa - comes up with more plot elements, yet they are all shamed by the electrifying, anachronistic and jaw-dropping operatic (glam) rock performances by Tomona and Inu-oh. Channeling his inner rock god, Tomona plays the biwa behind his head at one point - how much cooler can a medieval artist get?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: A timely and deeply emotional story, Robert-Jonathan Koeyer's It's Nice in Here is a fragmented portrait of a moment, a person, and a place, seen through the subjective memories of a young girl (Imani) and a rookie police officer (David), who both have wildly different recollections of the same fateful moment involving a black boy in a red hoodie in a corner store. Hang in tight for this heart-breaking tale of police violence and racial injustice. The film premiered at the 61st Semaine de la Critique in Cannes and was nominated for the Golden Calf for Best Short Film in 2022.

I'm Late focuses on an important but underdiscussed topic. Known for her work on the female body, filmmaker Sawako Kabuki zooms in on the experience of being "late" with your period. Her trademark colourful style is again married here with her keen eye for vulnerability.

Seasoned Iranian director Iraj Mohammadi Razini tells a tragic fairy tale of a lover going to the king's garden to pick red roses to win the heart of his beloved one. Made by moving tree needles on a backlit glass, the film is an experimental, yet magical experience.

A delicate yet uplifting transgender story, this anidoc is based on the real story of Lada, a trans woman from Russia. She tells her and her brother Ivan's secret. With simple designs, the filmmaker makes a heartfelt case for accepting your true gender.

An insightful short that gives a voice to people with learning disabilities, who often experience worse physical and mental health. Researchers at Surrey Heartlands (UK) collaborated with the SunnyBank Trust and Strange Beast to produce a film that seeks to support healthcare professionals working in Primary Care to understand more about the challenges of people with learning disabilities. Let's break down barriers together!
"You are the one. But I must remain composed." A girl searches desperately to fill her insatiable void. A crooked and dark short which proves how intensely primal attraction can be.

In this touching Singaporean story a grandma tries to recall the familiar stranger sitting next to her. With much difficulty and frustration, she weaves her hazy memories of the stranger together, only for her to forget them once again.
A lovely zombie couple just wishes to have a smooth life like normal humans. However, an avaricious human - who hunts zombies to turn them into sex toys - ruins their life one day. The fight is on!

films.t: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
films.syn: Meet Marcel, the Oscar-nominated shell, and try not to fall in love with him. We dare you NOT to love Marcel. It is just impossible not to fall at the Chaplin-esque feet of this incredibly sweet one-inch-tall seashell. The funnily naive Marcel is a creation that dates back to 2010, when comedian Jenny Slate and her friend-director Dean Fleischer Camp invented him out of sheer boredom at a wedding. They uploaded a three-minute short on Youtube, which was met with millions of heartwarming reactions. Now, more than a decade, two more shorts and a bestselling book later, Marcel stars in his own feature stop-motion mockumentary. Voiced by Jenny Slate, Marcel lives with his grandmother Connie (a larger shell with life experience to die for and voiced by the great Isabella Rossellini) in an L.A. house, abandoned by a fighting couple who have converted it into an Airbnb. Marcel is an admirable optimist who tackles practical issues shell-first, climbing the walls by attaching honey to his shoes, making music with a piece of pasta or making his way around in a hollow tennis ball. Yet, beneath his friendly and smiley manners lies a big grief. He and Connie were once part of a larger community which went missing after the couple moved out. When a filmmaker (Dean Fleischer Camp himself) rents the Airbnb, he decides to make a documentary on the duo and their odd lives, helping them in the process of reaching out to possible community members. Dean Fleischer Camp and Jenny Slate have succeeded in the most difficult of tasks: translating a couple of shorts into a feature film without compromising on any of the ingredients that turned Marcel into a viral sensation. Better even, the film cleverly comments on Marcel's fame and how it influences his life. With a perceptive eye for the minutiae and the poetics of daily live, Marcel the Shell with Shoes On is a poignant animated therapy session for humans and shells alike. By the end of this 90-minute mollusc portrait, you will be cracking your voice when talking about shells. Whether he likes it or not: with Marcel, a star is born.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.t: Modo De Vida: A Goan Sketchbook
films.syn: Come along with animator Rohit Karandadi and discover what's life like in the state of Goa, on the southwestern coast of India. A quaint Goan life hides beneath its touristy facade. A Goa of sleepy balcaos , pushy fish-mongers and of pilot bikes flitting on boiling afternoons; of the blend of traditions and a penchant for slow life. An animated sketchbook film that explores this erstwhile Portuguese colony.

What would happen if mum was always right? Do mums always tell their children the truth? If I squint, will I stay cross-eyed forever? If I eat the seeds, will a watermelon grow in my belly? Based on established parental sayings that are meant to warn children not to do certain things, filmmaker Marie Urbánková takes the consequences of these actions to absurd and grotesque extremes.

During a short bus trip, a young man and his elderly grandmother are confronted with horrible memories. Amidst grandma's usual nonstop nagging, it feels as if suffering will persist simultaneously in the past in the present. Coming from Macao director Weng Chon Wong, the film is a wonderfully weird mix of styles and emotions.

FOOOOOOOOD! Inspired by the online phenomenon of Korean eating videos that make people droll and feast, Mukbang! presents the visualisation and mental reflection of the binging culture through an eventful dinner experience. An explosive and colourful mixture of surrealist classic Daisies and the oeuvre of John Waters.

A story about the acceptance of the inner female rebellion. "Marriage is your destiny." Latvian-born Signe Baumane's sophomore feature My Love Affair With Marriage is a semi-autobiographical tale of a young spirited woman, Zelma, whom we follow into adulthood. Growing up in Soviet-occupied Latvia in the 70s, Zelma is taught that, in order to be loved, she must conform to societal expectations. Her mum makes it crystal clear; as a woman you're expected to abide by three rules. 1: Be a virgin until you marry. 2: Choose and marry well. 3: Hold that marriage together whatever it takes. But the more the young girl tries to conform, the more the body resists. After having debuted with Rocks in My Pockets in 2014, a brave film about battling with depression, Signe Baumane turns her eye towards female identity and rebellion. With her by-now familiar animation aesthetics, positioning 2D characters in detailed 3D backgrounds, the filmmaker tells a clever and meaningful story. A story not only about the legacy of growing up in a close-minded Soviet-Union, but also about how we deal with relationships, about the dynamics between men and women, about our own shortcomings and self-doubts as well as the oppressiveness of gender roles and societal conventions.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: A haunting evocation of the rippling effects war has on multiple generations. "No one really comes back from the war." Angola, 1995. Angola, 2011. In his feature animation debut, Portuguese filmmaker José Miguel Ribeiro eloquently tells an emotional intergenerational story of three women from the same family whose lives have been torn apart by Angola's deathly civil war. Based on the stage play A Caixa Preta (The Black Box) by Angolan playwright José Eduardo Agualusa and Mozambican novelist Mia Cauto, Nayola interweaves past and present, depicting two eras - one during the violent civil war spanning decades, and one in 2011 in an Angola that is still significantly scarred by its bloody conflict. Nayola, a young mother, goes searching for her husband who disappeared during the war, leaving her two-year-old daughter, Yara, and her mother Lelena behind. Years later, Yara is a rebellious teenager and subversive rap sing angered by her mother's decision and by the injustice that holds a tight grip on Angolan society. A haunting evocation of the rippling effects war has on multiple generations, the film is an impressive blend of 2D and 3D animation. Ribeiro infuses his feature with a fascinating mysticism, exploring conflict through magical realism. He covers the harrowing reality of Angola, but not without a redemptive poetic charge, using the jackal as a symbol of strength and resilience, while also showing how people (figuratively and literally) have learnt to wear masks to hide themselves. "We killed so many, have seen so many people die, there aren't many people left to talk about what it was like."

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: The colours. The music. The wild imagination!! In this crazily creative music video for a song by Argentinian electropop band Siamés, a girl tries to go back home with her little brother while protecting him from his live fantasies.

Multi-award winning studio Job, Joris & Marieke is back with another delightful short, with a very timely topic: social media influencing. Nobody is about obsessive Instagrammer Florian who takes too many selfies. He becomes transparent and has to struggle to keep his beloved followers.

With the use of a wood-carved etching art style, Joanna Kozuch tells the story of the vanished Aral Sea by collecting the stories of the last people of the Uzbek town of Mo'ynoq who remember the original shore. Now, only a cemetery of ships remains. A melancholic tale of tracing a glorious past destroyed by ignorance and mismanagement.

A music video for a song by the band Sobotni Rosol made in an art brut style. The lyrics are a commentary on life in the big city, stating that we pass other people on the streets but that we hardly notice each other. More and more, we are becoming invisible to each other.

In modern times we tend to forget that film used to be very tangible. Luckily, there's always Canadian filmmaker Steven Woloshen to remind us of the materiality of film in the most creative ways! Here, he choreographs a physical dance with darkness and light.

persona (noun) - the particular type of character that a person seems to have and that is often different from their real or private character In her graduation short film, animator Moon Su-jin depicts the nightmarish process of being encroached on by the persona. Just how big is the gap between 'me' and 'my persona'? Persona was the first Korean animated short to compete for the Palme d'Or for Best Short Film at the Cannes Film Festival.

In a dimension where Nicolas Cage starred in Casablanca , Rear Window , and virtually all other films - yep, this is BONKERS - Jose Antonio is just enjoying a pleasant afternoon of reading in his apartment in Manhattan. But a quick-talking caller trying to sell his product is about to unleash the destructive power of Phonorama!

Phew, there are some serious "pipes" in this short! Bob the bear is a plumber. One night he is hired to fix a broken pipe, but to his surprise he lands in a gay fetish club. Safe to say the pipe metaphor finds its (hilarious) way into the film's narrative and style.
The inimitable Peter Millard strikes again with a humorous short in his own characteristic style. This one is again laugh-out-loud silly and features a man who desperately wants to get in a house.

You'll never look at plastic in the same way after entering the world of PLSTC , an undersea dystopia that submerges you in the disturbing reality of plastic pollution in our oceans. Through a series of graphically confronting AI-generated and hand-composited images of ocean creatures, this experimental animated film by Amsterdam-based filmmaker Lean Sanches shows the devastating consequences of our habits on marine life, and leaves you gasping for air.

School ... the pressure is sometimes explosive, quite literally so in this graduation short. When a high school girl enters class with her classmates, she experiences a lot of pressure from her teacher to perform well. The pressure gets so intense, that she ... explodes.

Truth be told, there is only one single thing on your mind - at least when watching this short ... PSSY , a pussydelic journey, is an animated segment made for the Netflix series Clark which focuses on Swedish criminal Clark Olofsson, who is known as the "father of the Stockholm syndrome".

Working with 3D animation for the first time, Daniel Wesseik's latest ethereal short film is a threnody for lost friendships, echoing feelings of loneliness and yearnings in relation to friendships that were left behind along the journey of life. Wherever these butterflies are headed, it's a part of the journey of life.

films.t: Questbound: Forbidden Ventures of the Undead Soul
films.syn: Nothing could excite the great king, but then along came a noble knight ... But is the undead king flirting? Infused with delightful humour and some welcome nerdiness, Questbound is a medieval fantasy story embracing that even undead kings have primal needs.
At Kaboom, we have seen many a great weird sh*t. But a psychological stand-off between a young naïve croquette and a bitchy cheese soufflé ... that's something we never dared to dream of.

Reparations experimentally explores the phenomenon of migration (forced and voluntary) through the character of a chair. Symbolically referring to past and present racism and (African) diaspora in Colombia, the film shows the violent consequences of war, apartheid and colonialism.

Like zapping on a television from another planet. That's a bit how Hagar Faibish's debut film feels like - and that's a compliment. The director outlandish style gives way to a dystopian tale about a character losing touch with his other world by diffusing bit by bit with the virtual world of television. Embracing the nonsensical with a distinct melancholic tone, Faibish's surreal film is a demand for self-reflection in our modern world.

A troupe of clowns gather to perform a story about a priest and a refugee in this cut-out animation with puppets. As their misguided tale unfolds, the boundaries between fiction and reality begin to fray. A bewitching and theatrical Shakespearean tale to remind us that our xenophobia and our upheld moral superiority affects real people, who have the right to reclaim the narrative.

In a world where robots and nature live in harmony, an uninvited guest disrupts the peace. A graduation short about the balance between humankind and nature, commenting on our destructive influence on our surroundings.

As a kid, you have a certain wondrous way of looking at the world. You do things just because you like them. But as you get older, you quickly realise that there are certain expectations you have to live up to. Starting from the frustrations of the filmmakers, Scribbles tries to find back that burning fire of our young selves.
Pun definitely intended! In this voyage of 'Sensor Ship', Jina Yoon creates a thought-provoking film using surrealist and grotesque illustrations of contorted bodies accompanied by a soothing voice.

Roel van Beek, the director of the award-winning short A Film About a Pudding , returns with a unique film depicting something we can all relate to: when it itches, you want to scratch it ... When stung by a nettle, Sarah avoids making it worse by not scratching her itch. But as everyday irritations start to accumulate, will she be able to resist the urge?
Coming out and talking about your sexuality to your parents ... Is it ever easy? This cutely put together queer short film documents the story of Polina, a bisexual Russian girl.

Woops, somebody lost a shoe! Go searching together with three colourful apartment dwellers when one of them loses his tap dance shoe. However, the search leaves the building topsy-turvy. The design, the colour, the spaces, the characters ... They all start to shake and change! This fascinating student short reveals a keen eye for playful animation.

"The pleasure of love lasts but a moment." Encounter the right amount of creepy and disturbing with this tale of two swamp women, Siamese twins by one leg. At night the Flayed has terrifying nightmares in which she sees her sister's flesh covering her own body. With echoes of Cronenberg and Julia Ducournau, Skinned is a powerful stop-motion film about an abusive relationship that deeply affects the boundaries between the other and the self.

films.t: Sometimes I Don’t Know Where the Sun
films.syn: With simple drawings in an art brut style and some sprinkles of deadpan humour, Samantha Aquilino pictures a human searching for connection. He comes across a deer. He meets a cat. They all reject each other. Big disappointment ... Then, he follows the way of the sun.

Still Here is an atmospheric post-apocalyptic eco-story, depicting a world on the brink of destruction. The rich are able to live out their days with dignity, the poor must fight tooth and nail for the simplest of pleasures: even a breath of fresh air. In this setting, one poor man is being manipulated by the state to help them weed out a small but effective resistance movement.
Wait for it ... These apples refuse to be silenced, even if that means disrupting their still life.

The retired Hong Kong couple, Long and Sophie, are amateur singers. While Sophie arrives early at her performance and gets herself prepared, Long is caught up in the subway by an unexpected circumstance. Employing both animation and archival live-footage shot during the Anti-Extradition Protests in Hong Kong in 2019, Sunset Singers presents a fictional yet profound commentary on the parallel lives of Hong Kong's individuals.
Oh no, ketchup stain!! Let's throw the T-shirt into the washing machine and follow the colourful, amusing process. Will the stain be successfully removed?
The path towards quitting smoking is no easy one ... This is an authentic first-hand account of the emotional journey of trying to keep away from cigarettes.

films.t: The Best Grandfather in the World
films.syn: Felix has had a very close relationship with his grandfather since childhood. However, everything changes when he tells his family he's gay. Based on a real story, the film is perhaps - first of all - about the possibility of dialogue and the restoration of family ties when politics have destroyed them.

Hang in tight for a lovely bizarre and surprisingly violent hand-painted story about a spirited young woman who persuades a hyena from London Zoo to take her place at a dinner dance held in her honour. Based on a short story by British surrealist writer Leonora Carrington, Elizabeth Hobbs' commentary on elitist society celebrates the emancipation of women and of hand-painted animation.

Two young sisters see their pink-medieval-world-harmony disturbed when a pretty sword appears in their life, revealing a dark vice in the heart of one of them. A surprising student work dipped in dark-ish pink paint.

The bell tower rings and the birds fly away. In the countryside on the outskirts of a small village, a dog tied to very long yellow rope, watches them disappear in the horizon. It's time for him to go. How far will his rope allow him to go? A hand-drawn student film like no other.

You know those true stories that are almost impossible to believe? This is one of them. In 1917, two ships collided in the Halifax Harbour in Canada, causing the largest accidental explosion in history. Among the tragic stories of the disaster is the remarkable account of a sailor who, blown skyward from the docks, flew a distance of two kilometres before landing, naked and unharmed. Contemplating on near-death experiences, duo Wendy Tilby and Amanda Forbis have made another bold blend of comedy, suspense and philosophy. Nominated for the 2023 Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film.

On a hot August afternoon, a Portuguese family gathers at the table and remembers uncle Botão: the war in Angola, his emigration to France where he lived and worked as a garbage man ... Memories of each are crossed to tell the story of a hard-working man through humour and fantasy. A delightful exploration of remembering.

After growing up in her father's glass shop, Lucía López observes her childhood twenty years later, which she tries to treasure using paint and glass, elements that she will soon discover are just as fragile as her own memory. By getting closer again to her family memories, she recognises her greatest fear: the passing of time.

In a mix of live action footage and animation, The Harbourmaster recounts the true story of its titular swan, and of how he went from a local celebrity and mascot to a wanted criminal in the Norwegian town of Osøyro. The story of his planned euthanisation stirred up Norway's most polarising debate in 2017. A creative exploration of wild animal life in cities.

Starting from the grim reality of the anomalous trade on the borders of Ceuta and Melilla that separate Africa from Europe, The Heights depicts the repetitive pilgrimage that hundreds of "mule women" carry out every day in the area while pondering over the impossibility of achieving a better life. Using dehumanised silhouettes, this errant journey into the night is a mysterious and mythical meditation on female suffering, and visualises the Islamic concept of Al Araf, a wall dividing paradise and hell.

These are frustrating times with enormous global challenges, yet motivational and optimistic stories can help us move forward. Here, a young polar bear has to leave her her home and move to Zurich. She tries to make a living until she suddenly has an idea that will change the world for ever. This insightful and delightful film shows that we can all be the change that is needed.

Any (ex-)owners of a VW Beetle? This one is an emotional goodbye. The Last Mile is a heartfelt tribute to arguably the most cherished car on earth as it goes out production. Fx Goby takes us through the decades, telling both a personal and cultural history of our relationship with the iconic VW Beetle over its 80 year lifespan. So long, partner!

films.t: The Rebel Radio That Brought Down a War Criminal
films.syn: Get to know the incredible story of Radio Venceremos, an underground radio collective that fought US-backed fascism during the Salvadoran Civil War. In 1980, farmers and urban workers formed guerrilla groups to overthrow the dictatorship. A TED-Ed animation celebrating the rebel radio that brought down a war criminal.

An antique music instrument dealer receives a magical vinyl record from a traveller that "reads your mind and plays lost memories". Obsessed by this endless record, the antique dealer listens to it again and again, and the memories reemerge until one last and most painful memory is revealed: his separation from his mother on the Swiss border during WWII. The Record - the debut film by Jonathan Laskar - is a story about our duty and need to remember, with a vinyl record as the ultimate archival symbol.

It's all about the sausage in this reimagining of Little Red Riding Hood . The roles of the humans and animals are reversed. Influenced by Paul Driessen, animator Thomas Stellmach decided to use the historical optical device of the Zoetrope to tell this story. Equally hypnotic and hilarious, A Zoetrope Fairy Tale is a critique on our thoughtless meat consumption. Our unconscious habits truly determine our lives.

You don't need perfect materials to achieve something truly great ... In poetic Colombian story Vincho, a street dweller, spends his time recycling and classifying waste produced in the city to use it for his creations. Under a bridge, he works on his masterpiece: The Sistine.

Suna, a young girl, lives in a forest and sleeps in the leaves. One day, she meets a two-hundred-year-old man, who offers to pass on to her a hidden technique ... Armenian actress, writer, producer and director Armine Anda has crafted a beautiful meditative short with a teacher to remember.

Silvia, a young Peruvian woman, finds herself in a world that seems strange, distant even. She feels she doesn't belong. It's always been like this. But in front of a protest against sexual minorities, she is going to find out, even if the tide is stronger than her, she is not alone. A meaningful and queer student short weighing in on the values of tolerance.
Hitchcock! Grace Kelly! Oh no, wrong film ... This Samsung commercial lets you meet a cute spider who falls in love with a device that looks just like him. Love knows no boundaries.

"Think of something nice." Yeah, right Mr/Mrs Dentist, like that's gonna help! In acclaimed director Claudius Gentinetta's latest short, he lets a patient takes refuge in a fantasised story of fishermen and the sea. An equally beautiful and painful experience, the film follows the rhythm of the horrifying sounds in the dental practice as we learn that even the best distractions are fleeting.

films.t: TVFCU – A Place For All of Us
films.syn: Tennessee Valley, a place of pure joy and happiness! Welcome to this stop-motion journey into a place that is committed to being your helping hand. When you help one another, then a community transforms into a place for all of us. Commissioned by the Tennessee Valley Federal Credit Union.

Memories of a world that perhaps doesn't exist anymore. Yet, they are invaluable because they play an important role in the construction of identity and self-awareness. Dedicated to her grandpa, Alexandra Dzhiganskaya tells a personal story about her childhood memories in Ukraine; memories that have acquired a special value since the outbreak of the war in Ukraine.

films.t: Under the Influence – Let’s Break the Silence
films.syn: One of the 7 short films made for the project Let's Break the Silence , Under the Influence tells a story, taken from an authentic testimony, about the issue of psychological control and dependence within a couple. Made by Swiss artists, this project raises awareness about the multiplicity of domestic abuse.

An anti-fascist fable depicting a holy war between cuddly candy-coloured bears and mighty unicorns. Honour, pain and cuddles! An utterly grim, grotesque and graphic journey into the heart of darkness, Alberto Vázquez's Unicorn Wars is an anti-fascist fable depicting a holy war between cuddly candy-coloured bears and mighty unicorns. Imagine a gory 18+ version of Care Bears in which the bears have been programmed to shoot and kill. The entire fantasy epic feels as if sadistic Happy Tree Friends have invaded films like Full Metal Jacket , Apocalypse Now and Annihilation . You get it ... Unicorn Wars is pure midnight-movie mayhem with a surprising exploration of the origins of evil. For ages, teddy bears have been in a deadlock with the unicorns in the Magical Forest. In a military bootcamp, recruits are trained - let's change that to "brainwashed" - with the mantra "Good unicorn, dead unicorn". Two brother bears, Tubby and Bluey, couldn't be more different. But both bears are part of a new squad that must trek into the forest to search for a missing scouting group. From there on, Vázquez's truly fucked-up premise evolves into one of the bleakest animated features in recent memory. It's like a faux-cute slap in the face, a knife - or rather a unicorn horn - in the stomach. And with every turn, the film turns darker, uglier en bleaker. Based on his own short project Unicorn Blood , filmmaker and illustrator Alberto Vázquez’s latest feature uses tropes, colours, and characters we cherished as a child to make a misanthropic examination of militarism, authoritarianism, and religious zealotry. We're not sure you will want to hug your teddy bears after this movie is over.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Ah, the imagination of Jules Verne! Abseiling down volcanoes, going around the world in 80 days ... I wonder where he got his ideas. Wait up ... aren't his adventures suspiciously similar to the writings of Ida Pfeiffer? This short is part of Unsung Women , a stop-motion series that points out - with wit and smartly done cut-outs - the invisibility process that women have undergone through history.

films.t: Why Are Cockroaches So Hard to Kill?
films.syn: Can cockroaches even die?! From poison to brandished slippers, these insects seem to weather just about everything we throw at them. Dig into the genetic adaptations of cockroaches, and find out what makes it so hard to kill them in this animated TED-Ed lesson.
An animated music video in which the abstract and the figurative interact. An example of strata-cut animation in stop-motion, this short is bound to make you want to play with clay as well!

Exhibiting a sort of 'Murakami meets Salvador Dalí' style, this student film made at the Tama Art University takes place is in a certain cafe where we get to see the unusual daily life of the clerk and customers. Mysterious events happen, but no one really cares about them.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: You are the captain of your body! But what do you do if someone doesn't listen to your boundaries? You Are the Captain! is an educational short that teaches children that their bodies belong to them and what they can do when someone touches them inappropriately. This film is a wholesome safe place.

Small shimmering axolotls are in heat, nuzzling and nibbling one another's limbs. Soon a much larger, two-legged forest-dweller encounters the lustful group. A cheerful snack party begins. Fusing different techniques into hybrid forms, this short is a visual treat open to interpretation.
Trailer for the 12th StopTrik IFF in Maribor, Slovenia.
The trailer for fourteenth edition of Anibar Animation Festival in Kosovo.

Bathed in colour, hallucinogenic visuals and liberating sexual fantasies, Flóra Anna Buda's Palme d'Or winner 27 is an existential portrait of a 27-year-old woman that still lives with her parents. After a psychelic dance party on a factory roof, Alice has a serious drunken bike accident. Will she finally find the courage to become an adult and escape the cage of her family life? A cry for freedom in all its overflowing beauty.

Adventures rarely come this delicious. Dimitri, a cookie knight, together with his faithful chocolate friend Pépite and Boubou, his boudoir horse, are sent on a mission to find the heart of the princess that was stolen by the villainous Cherry Ontop. Their adventures across strange, sugary lands inhabited by all sorts of pastries will prove to be dangerous. A knight's tale of epic (and tasty) proportions, made by students during their graduation year at ESMA Nantes.

Drenched in a surreal and bizarre animation style, Stephen Vuillemin's first animated short plays a delirious gag on its audience and its protagonist. A young woman discovers a stranger has been making animations created from her social media feed. Creepy, right?! A thought-provoking exploration of our digital lives and the blurred boundaries between reality and fiction.
Aaaah! is a cry of expressions sometimes good, sometimes bad. A fun take on what we take for granted as human beings.

Goya-nominated directors Carla Pereira & Juanfran Jacinto channel their inner David Lynch with this freaky stop-motion sitcom-like short about an almost normal family that decides to fertilize an egg the mother laid last night. 100% WTF, 100% worth it.
What is weird, is based on a norm. Weird can be anything, and it can be funny, maybe confusing, but most of all it can be authentic. This animation takes those notions to make something new.
It’s a simian smackdown! Deep in the Bakoongie Jungle, two great apes duke it out over the ultimate price: a bunch of sweet grapes! Wrapped up in their own battle they don't notice a threat.

Architect A is an architect who builds houses in a very special way. However, he gives up on his trade after an unexpected accident. One day, an elderly woman comes to his house. Although hesitant, A decides to build the woman's home. During the process of reflecting on the woman's life to build her a haven, A once again confronts his own pain. Can A complete his own house, which he has been unable to finish for a long time?
A stunned crowd faces a fire. The threat has no name, a diffuse anguish spreads. A portrayal of human kind observing symbolic fires, possibly the burning of Notre Dame in 2019.

As The Heat Rises is a music video about life and death and what makes us who we are. This video was made using a variety of techniques. Most of the footage is either found footage or footage the maker shot themselves, largely from the Vondelpark in Amsterdam, the Netherlands.
Ashnikko drives a monstertruck and a squad of develish beasts ride towards the sunset to battle the angelic overlord robots.
An animated documentary on self-harm from those living through it. This film aims to bust myths while offering positive advice to loved-ones.

Don't ever mess with chickens! A chicken coop set up at the foot of a nuclear power plant sees its daily life turned upside down by a series of mutations but tries to save the day amidst atomic chaos. A fluffy and surprising 3D animation film by French students.
A film for Back Market about the impact of overconsumption in tech and the joys of refurbishing. A combination of live action puppetry, 2D facial animation and stop motion.

Three balding brothers travel to Istanbul to get a hair transplant. Stuck with each other in a hotel far from home, their insecurities and frustrations grow faster than their hair. Since 2017, Nicolas Keppens has emerged as one of Belgium's most promising animators, making waves with films like Wildebeest and Easter Eggs (Jury Prize winner at Annecy 2021). His latest tragicomedy, Beautiful Men , found its way onto the 2025 Oscars shortlist.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Bits is a short experimental animation exploring the surreal beauty of nature. The visuals explore the similarities in patterns and formations that occur in biology.
A young woman remembers the day when she was attacked by three men on her way home. A film about survival and carrying on with life.
An animated television ad for the yearly organised Pride Parade in Budapest, Hungary.

Bug-fix is an experimental animated short film, revisiting childhood. It is a short journey through a childhood bedroom where curious six-legged creatures create tiny scenes. A reminder that sometimes all we need is a little bit of bug-like wonder to see the world with fresh, bug-like, eyes.

On a prairie on Mars, a grumpy space farmer is having trouble with one of her hive: a robot bee called Buzz that keeps going rogue. She follows him into a volcano and discovers something that will change life there forever. Made with the support of ESA - The European Space Agency.
Camino is a film about a mental shift, a path to inner calm. A road that leads the viewer from the past to the future.
Dirk Verschure and his wacky humour are back for more! A cat with glasses is sick and tired of his hazy vision, so he turns to Dr. Spoo for a solution. But will the doctor's visit be worth it?

Annecy's big winner, 'Chicken for Linda!' is a zany adventure about the search for a chicken in a strike-stricken city. "When we're dead, are we in the dark?" Apologies are best served in the form of a good meal... And for mischievous 8-year-old Linda that means a chicken with peppers, a dish that reminds her of her late father who was a great cook. Her mother Paulette, however, is no Gordon Ramsay, and favours ready-made meals to heat up in the microwave. When Paulette feels guilty after unjustly punishing her daughter, she wants to do anything to make it up to her, including cooking Linda's chicken dinner. But in a strike-stricken city, a nod to France's political climate, that plan might prove to be more complicated than she thought. Linda's simple request quickly leads to a zany adventure, including frantic chases, rather clumsy police interventions, and musical interludes. Husband-and-wife team Sébastien Laudenbach and Chiara Malta weaves a tender, small-scale tale, firmly grounded in everyday reality. The story might be akin to older French vérité cinema, but the film visually unfolds through hand-drawn animations, painting a Fauvist-inspired dreamscape where characters are assigned one colour that is informed by their personality. Vibrant and unapologetically energetic, Yellow Linda embodies boundless enthusiasm, wanting to make the most of every situation. Orange Paulette meanwhile grapples with finding a balance between mourning and moving forward as a single parent. Laudenbach, acclaimed for his previous and stylistically similar feature The Girl Without Hands , brings his signature visual flair, providing the film with minimalist but dynamic character designs. Crowned with the prestigious Cristal Award for Best Feature Film at Annecy, Chicken for Linda! is an expressionistic and chaotic rollercoaster for the whole family. It shows the joyous whirlwind of childhood, the wonderous embrace of a mother-daughter bond and how one can find a renewed zest for life.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: In a village ruled by a clock of death, Dante’s son (8) has been selected to be sacrificed. Dante refuses to accept this and desperately fights the clock, causing him to miss out on the last moments together with his son.

"A film by Peter Millard" should say enough ... In his characteristically quirky style, the acclaimed English animator and artist shows us that every species has its own life cycle. Masterfully silly.
Clarkii is a Dutch stop motion animated documentary about the American crayfish and the conflicting laws surrounding this little creature.

This film’s stop-motion animation puppets are made using Taiwan’s unique papermaking technique rooted in traditional funeral ceremonies. Compound Eyes of Tropical uses the perspective of a fly to create a montage film language using the metaphor of the compound eye. The film portrays the Southeast Asian folktale The Mousedeer Crossing the River though multiple perspectives, reinterpreting the story’s multiple facets across cultures.
A coot and a ferry skipper peacefully coexist on city river. When a new bridge emerges, it causes major problems for the skipper. The bird then helps the skipper.

At her father's request, Coline returns to her childhood bedroom to sort out her things. The different objects she finds there plunge her into the memories of her childhood. Those items bring back memories of both the good and the very bad.

films.t: Cécile McLorin Salvant – D’un Feu Secret
films.syn: Music video for Cécile McLorin Salvant.

Tian Xiaopeng's unparalleled 3D aquatic odyssey plunges us into a chaotic underwater world and the inner turmoils of a lost child. Ever peeked through a kaleidoscope, imagining a spectacular sea adventure within its mesmerizing and hypnotic patterns? Your prayers have been answered. Tian Xiaopeng's Deep Sea defies everything you've ever seen in animation with its unparalleled technique combining 3D animation with running ink art, resulting in an aesthetically overwhelming experience. Bursting with colours and captivating canvases, it sweeps you into a fantastical world. Every frame is a feast. Beyond its dazzling exterior lies a profound story - an intimate exploration of grappling with depression and trauma. Deep Sea looks like a maximalist masterpiece, but feels like a poignant aquatic reverie that leaves an indelible mark on your soul. Ever since her mother left the family, Shenxiu has felt a deep sadness, unable to shake that relentless feeling of utter loneliness and grief. Amidst a cruise with her father, stepmother, and baby brother, she finds herself wandering the ship alone. However, fate takes a drastic turn when a fierce storm strikes, casting Shenxiu overboard and into the embrace of a surreal underwater world. Guided by a many-eyed creature, the Hyjinx, she ends up in the chaotic Deep Sea Restaurant, led by the magical chef Nanhe. Together they embark on a quest for the Eye of the Deep Sea. Chinese director Tian Xiaopeng - whose breakout film Monkey King: Hero is Back was a major box office success - channels his admiration for Jules Verne's classic Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea into a moving metaphorical coming-of-age story about overcoming sadness. As Shenxiu is troubled with the weight of her grief, Xiaopeng masterfully the narrative forward, infusing every grame with an uninterrupted energy and fluidity. He keeps everything moving, swinging, swirling, flowing, and streaming as if there is no tomorrow. Within the depths of the ocean, there lies mysteries aplenty. And in our hearts, we store depression, confusion, and fear. Through Shenxiu's journey, Xiaopeng invites us to confront these inner tempests head-on. With its mesmerizing painterly visuals, Deep Sea immerses us in a psychedelic odyssey, urging us to surrender to the grandeur of this cinematic spectacle. This film truly demands to be seen on the biggest screen possible.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.t: Design & Transformation: Stories of Czech Design 1990-2020: Textile Mountain
films.syn: Lenka Vackova's Textile Mountain project helps to breathe new life into textiles. The film was made for the exhibition Design and Transformation: Stories of Czech Design 1990-2020, held on the occasion of the Czech presidency of the EU council in Brussels in 2022.

films.t: Design & Transformation: Stories of Czech Design 1990-2020: Wood
films.syn: This film explores the history of woodworking in the Czech republic and was made for the exhibition Design and Transformation: Stories of Czech Design 1990-2020, held on the occasion of the Czech presidency of the EU council in Brussels in 2022.

The film “ Dessert Dachshund ” directed by Betina Bożek is a surreal story about a Dachshund. He lives inside wedding cakes and is a fortune teller for newlyweds. The film also tackles larger themes of superficiality and ritualism during important moments in life.

In South Korea, there's a saying: "A stone thrown carelessly hits a frog and dies." And that's the end of it. But not in this story! Whether a metaphor for our attitude towards nature or for victims in abusive relationships, Don't Die is a clever revenge film. You'll make sure you never throw a rock at frogs ever again.

Who says the superhero genre is dead? Doris & Bettan are two retired women enjoying the sun on a Spanish beach. Topless, smoking and sipping on cocktails, they are living the high life. That is until a manager and his security team tries to kick them out. But the couple fights back in true John Wick style. Cartoonist & illustrator Ellen Ekman's directorial debut is a fun, subversive twist on the superhero flick, referencing loads of classics, including Thelma & Louise. You might want to think twice before going to Marbella now!

Dreams of Yesterday is a poignant charcoal animation that explores the emotional impact of forced migration. Artist Khattar Shaheen, drawing from personal refugee experiences, crafts a raw and intuitive narrative, deliberately eschewing traditional storytelling structures. It invites audiences to contemplate the uncertainties of displacement.

Being adrift at sea can be challenging, but even more so with a partner. Is it possible to be adrift at sea, while also keeping you relation intact? In this dark, humorous and bloody film Jeremy and Aurora will discover this, and find out if their relationship is (ship)wrecked, or not.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: In a small Dominican neighborhood, little kids play around, mixingcuriousity with imagination. An experimental puzzle of children's memories, shapes, colours, mixed together with a melodic music and poetic rhythm.

Electra reconsiders her 10th birthday, mixing memories with dreams. Isolated in her fantasy world full of sexualized dolls and other objects, she builds her own relationships with her body and sexuality. Delving deeper into her childhood memories, Electra goes through the most painful memories to let her suppressed feelings come out.

The multiverse is a bit like sausages ... At least according to this mind-bending Taiwanese student short that delves into time, death and interwoven worlds. Sausages: Into the Multiverse could probably also work as a title. A meaty twist on the multiverse film.
At the break of dawn a snug sleeper is awoken before their alarm by a feeling of dread. Something's wrong.

Human overconsumption and pollution are not only destroying the earth, but also the ocean. When the Manta Rays discover yet another of their peers suffocated by a killer plastic bag, they rise up in revolt. It is the beginning of the Flatastic Era, when fish and other sea animals take over the earth.

A grim but fascinating portrayal of a now-forgotten aristrocatic pastime in 17th-century Europe, Fox Tossing zooms in on a cruel phenomenon that is emblematic of the hedonistic life of people in palaces. Expressionist in style, this Hungarian film explores the complex relationship between power and powerlessness.
These ceramic frogs were made during the 106-day lockdown. The green glaze used for the frog spawn was sourced from the dust in the air.
Five eight-year-olds create the imaginary world ‘George-Peterland’ , a dreamy forest land that you can travel to by closing your eyes. Then the school interferes and it becomes a nightmare.
Gerard has got a bad case of an animated flu in the 50th episode of Gerard and Stipje.
Gigi tells us about her gender transition with humour and sensitivity.

Two shallow people go on a date, they are very self-absorbed and don't notice their surroundings. The woman goes on about her ex, who is a tooth model. This causes the man's ego and teeth to crumble, which he tries to hide. His teeth start to turn into gum .

This film is dedicated to 22-year-old Azerbaijani Turk Hadis Najafi, who was killed during protests in Iran on September 21, 2022, and to those fighting against gender, ethnic and cultural discrimination in Iran.
An educational animation on the origin and importance of braces.
The fear of oblivion can be overwhelming, but it can also be a driving force. I Am Here explores the need to imprint ourselves onto the world and build a legacy.
An animated video with music that follows the inner world of a young man.
Saying goodbye to a collaboration of 30 years, a wife, a son, a father, the studio, the garden and all other aspects of life.
Maya has to get a mole removed for the first time. It poses a health risk but she is very attached to it.

As a freelance illustrator and perfectionist, Maya’s life is a lot of fun, but also very hectic. She has a full personal and professional life and has a supportive inner voice "Little Motivator". After a severe panic attack she and her Little Motivator try to accept a new standard of good.
Kate Is Not Alone is an animated short that tells the story of a sexual assault committed at a school using the visual metaphor of a sinking ship.Based on real-life events witnessed by the director.

A young Embera Katío girl, Chidima, is lured into the forbidden zone of a hydroelectric power plant, where she discovers a sacred cave. A myth told with the participation of the indigenous community of Columbia.

When Greetje's father, butcher Tuitjes, takes on the Italian butcher Smakkerelli, the formerly rustic village of Moppel is turned upside down and Greetje is in danger of losing not only the annual sausage competition, but also her great love Nol.

Three filmmakers embark on a perilous journey inside survivalist game 'DayZ', resulting in an absorbing document on digital lives. "Don't shoot, I'm a documentarist." Imagine if cinematic maestros Tarkovsky, Malick and Peter Watkins joined forces as gaming buddies, embarking on a perilous journey inside an online video game. Their mission: to investigate the dual lives of players who inhabit this digital realm, both as human beings and as avatars with personalities and desires distinct from their real-life counterparts. The film result of that endeavour would likely mirror the deeply melancholic and absorbing anidoc, Knit’s Island . But perhaps those three legendary directors wouldn’t match the charm of Ekiem Barbier, Guilhem Causse, and Quentin L’helgoualc’h, the trio of filmmakers behind this venture. They choose not to pass judgment on their subjects, instead crafting a strangely entertaining document on the hazy borders between reality and virtual worlds. Equipped with cameras rather than heavy weaponry, Barbier, Causse and L’helgoualc’h spent a whopping 963 hours inside the survivalist game DayZ , which hosts a sprawling map of 250 kilometres ripe for exploration. Naturally, they encounter zombies, but their primary focus is sociological. Who are these people who dedicate countless after-work hours to this virtual reality, even to the point that digital memories and real-life experiences begin to be one and the same. Some of the avatars they meet live in communities, others are single wanderers. But all of them traverse this digital land for various reasons. In this free space, they all allow themselves to become anyone they desire. A spiritual follow-up of their medium-length film Marlowe Drive (made with footage from GTA V ), the trio’s virtual odyssey ends up being more than a sociological documentary on online identities. Knit’s Island evolves into a micro-epic about a colossal playground where people come and go. Whether it’s an African man with little money embodying a lone wolf exploring caves or a cute vegan couple with kids who spend their pastime travelling around DayZ , these players harbor fears and fantasies within this vast universe. Awarded the Burning Lights Prize at Visions du Réel, Knit’s Island stands as a poignant reminder of the power of digital landscapes.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: A clip to promote Short Film Day. On the shortest day of the year (December 21), people from all over Germany are invited to organize and attend short film screenings.
A short animated music video about a composer who keeps being interrupted.

Every week, Raquel (41) visits her friend Madeleine (107) in her retirement home in Montreal, Canada and tries to convince her to get out of the house more. First Madeleine refuses, but then agrees. A mix of live action and felt stop motion shows a beautiful friendship and the importance of not giving up.

Tony has always put others first, even as a child. He helps strangers and lives with a literal angel who influences his extreme kindness. When Tony's selflessness backfires, he must learn to balance altruism with self-care.

In a post-Covid world we all know the importance of human intimacy. But how far would you go to feel a touch in a world where touch is eliminated? Welcome to Hotel Vaip, run by Matta and Matto in a dystopian landscape. In the deceptive labyrinth of mind-bending rooms at their transient hotel, clients' deepest desires are fulfilled, but this comes at a price. A brilliant, weird and disturbing cautionary tale from the minds of Swiss directors Kerstin Zemp & Bianca Caderas.

In 1942, on a train to nowhere, a former drag queen remembers a night from her past in one of Paris’ first queer bars. Remnants of customer gossip recall this mythic bar and its mysterious Jewish-Algerian owner. A look back at Jewish and queer people during the Holocaust.

Joost Rekveld's latest experiment is an abstract science-fiction film somewhere between a human fever dream and lively machinic chaos. "It has been several years since many people began to give me credit for discovering chaos." 27 November, 1961. Yoshisuke Ueda discovers deterministic chaos through his computing systems while the Cold War is at its peak. It's a ground-breaking interaction between man and machine, an interaction that fascinates Dutch researcher and artist Joost Rekveld, who has dedicated his life and work to uncover what humans can learn from dialogues with machines - machines that mankind has constructed. In a form of media archeology, Rekveld investigates material engagement with devices from forgotten corners in the history of science and technology. The outcomes of the investigations often take the shape of abstract films that function like alien phenomenologies. Rekveld's latest experimental endeavour plays like a thrilling science-fiction film somewhere between a human fever dream and lively machinic chaos. Starting with the origins of chaos, it evolves into a dance between sound, image, and politically informed narrative. Most computing technology was, after all, a repercussion of the rapid development of atomic weapons and planetary surveillance systems. #59 is entirely composed of images produced and analogue electronic signals. These signals were generated using period equipment, including early oscillators. It's only logical then that Rekveld credits his machines, from an EAI TR-48 analogue computer to an Astro VG-854 video generator. Mechanisms Common to Disparate Phenomena #59 might be indebted to the structures of experimental cinema, but its imagery is real machinal output. Looking at the experiences shared by humans and electronic circuits, Joost Rekveld's film is an accumulation of flashes, shapes, fractals, crystals, waves and more. It's akin to calligraphy but made with early technology. On the soundtrack, Rekveld ironically (and fittingly) places dialogues from classic sci-fi films such as Plan 9 from Outer Space and War of the Satellites . #59 is a cinematic meditation on material processes and the arrow of time.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Melk is about the expectations of and realities of being gay.

The animated short Miserable Miracle was inspired by Henri Michaux’s book of poetry and drawings of the same name. The film explores the limits of language and perception, creating connections between sound, meaning, shapes and movement.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: 'Missed Connections' is an online forum where anyone can post their story, in hopes of reconnecting with someone they shared a passing moment with. Idiosyncratic animator Jack Gray presents several (bitter)sweet vignettes taken from the forum, exploring the humorous, vulnerable and surreal aspects of pursuing romance in a contemporary city.

A bull flees from his herd. The moon goes missing from the sky. The bull runs across this new moonless world, looking for its limit. This is a story of second-chances, and how all is not lost, even though sometimes it might feel like it.

films.t: My Name Is Edgar and I Have a Cow
films.syn: Edgar’s life changes when he rescues a newborn calf. After taking it home, the calf becomes a cow. When it becomes very destructive, Edgar finds a new solution.
In the pool changing room, Anthony realizes he has forgotten to bring his bathing trunks. Swimming class is about to begin, and he needs to find a solution.

Two people are sitting on a bench in the Parc des Bastions in Geneva, Switserland. One, Judith, is a sex worker who talks about her experience with disabled clients. The other one is interviewing and recording her.

In this surprisingly philosphical whirlpool of a film, our isolated protagonist sits in her apartment, daydreaming and browsing the internet. Her soliloquies are interrupted by some mysterious deliveries at the door by a candy-coloured ghost.

Never enough nuns in cinema! Reclusive as they are, each nun also has their own hidden universe, hopes and dreams. Awarded in Annecy, this Finnish short follows a nun that finds a man in the garden. The harmony of the community breaks and, uncertain of her temptations (and what to wear!), she learns that everyone keeps up appearances.

Nurit, the “big mama” who takes care of everyone, wants to become a mother. Her journey to motherhood begins in a still birth. After years of fertility treatments, Nurit arrives at the Eilat cemetery, where she finds closure.

Taking inspiration from 20th-century avant-garde experiments in graphical sound generation, the entire image in O/S functions as an optical soundtrack. Abstract motion becomes sound. What you hear is what you see. A tribute to the past and the contemporary digital art history.
A little boy worries about his parents' relationship in a dystopian future. His father eases his worries through a song.
Our common pain is what connects us. The ambiguity and variety of our existence allows us to imagine an infinity of variables, some of these alternatives may be malignant, and some benign.

Iranian director Yegane Moghaddam unfolds her school memories from Tehran through the wrinkles and fabrics of her old uniform. Inventively animated using all sorts of clothes, Our Uniform is a story about mandatory uniforms and much more. Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Short Film (Animated).

When Mitch is clearing out the room of her recently deceased father, she finds an old family heirloom that brings up repressed memories. Now that her father is gone she must find a way to make her own peace with his passing and their complicated relationship.
With a mix of techniques this film tells a story about mountains and sheep. An exploration of how it feels to be in nature and how peeing in the wild is a lovely activity to do.

At fifty years old, Eli takes care of his mother. The old lady is nostalgic about her wild youth and sexual escapades. She wants Eli to have the same kind of adventures. A film exploring old age, sexuality and mothers.
A family lives in a large white country house in a small town. Their orchard is inhabited by a colony of crows. The crows keep a close eye on the family. What happens when these worlds collide?
Highlighting the community of pigeon keepers in Glasgow, Pigeon Holding explores the relationship between people and birds through a combination of hand drawn animation and photographic collage.
Opening titles for Playgrounds In Motion Festival held in London and Rotterdam.

films.t: Postmates: This Is Your Brain on Donuts
films.syn: An ad by American food delivery service Postmates for donuts. It mixes animation and live action.

films.t: Postmates: This Is Your Brain on Nashville Hot Chicken
films.syn: An ad for the American food delivery service Postmates, highlighting Nashville hot chicken.

In Preoperational Model , anthropomorphic princess Sophie and her maid prepare for a new day. Sophie's struggle to play her role propels the two protagonists forward and backward in time, through worlds and identities to find a way to coexist.

Nightmares are terrible, right? Coco is six and lives in a big house with her mother and aunt. One night, she is startled by a nightmare about a character resembling Woody Woodpecker and asks her mom to call the police.
A TV ad against hate speech sponsored by Budapest Pride. Based on Hungarian poetry by Attila József.
An experimental animation where the viewer sees the image through slits and has to wait for the full picture to show itself, set to an eerie soundtrack.

A very "friendly" rat listens with great effort to a new father. Rat Things is the first animated project by Borja Pakrolsky and inquires the most superficial interior of the human being. A literal drawing of the different 'selves' that inhabit each and one of us.

The peace of a secluded society is disrupted by the arrival of a mysterious object. Zindy is particularly drawn to the object, a pair of red shoes, and puts them on. In this modern interpretation of the classic fairy tale The Red Shoes our protagonist fights for her own agency and discovers whether true freedom is achievable on both an individual and a societal level.

The debut animation and stop-motion film by Antonia Begusic. A great mixture of a Plato's writings, the history of Yugoslavia, Sorentino, Passolini, and contemporary politics. A satire of the political system.
This work is a stop-motion animation created using slime and plastic paper and other materials. The protagonist escapes from a pool and runs away to the sea.
Fed up with people asking to take sides in modern conflicts that they know nothing about, the director made a piece which speaks to possible outcomes and angles of the same event.
A small sheep who works as a quality controller in a stew factory, struggles with the overwhelming nature of the world. At night, this struggle takes shape in a strange musical nightmare.

Welcome to the town of Sourdough Creek for a wacky western musical about a guitar-playing lone hero taking on a corrupt mayor. Bill Plympton is back! "Keep the music snappy and the jacks happy." The king of indie animation is back! Bill Plympton's first feature since 2016's Revengeance is a wacky western musical that is a testament to the American artist's idiosyncratic style of hand-drawn, sketchy (take that word as you will) animation full of exaggerated characters, delirious action sequences and irreverent humour only the man himself can come up with. Last year, we wrote that "watching a Plympton film is like discovering the power of a pencil for the very first time", and Slide emits that power in abundant quantities. Welcome to the logging town of Sourdough Creek. Its egotistical, paunchy, money-grabbing mayor makes corruption his sport and is prepared to sacrifice a fishing village to build a luxury resort called 'Monte Carlo del Norte'. His goal? To cordially accommodate Tinselwood Studios and its film stars, keen on shooting a motion picture in the wild west. Enter Slide, a formidable cowboy and gifted guitar player whose coolness and taciturn character matches your favourite Clint Eastwood gunslinging hero. Will he - and his surprising monster friend or foe - be able to save the day? Inspired by 1940s honky-tonk music by artists like Hank Williams and Patsy Cline, Slide is a zany tale of a mythical cowboy showdown with an eco-villain intent on making gold at the expense of his own people. With the action taking place in his hometown in Oregon and a protagonist who plays the slide guitar, this arguably Plympton's most personal film to date. Plympton provided every frame himself: 30,000 drawings ... In one interview, the American filmmaker described his latest feature as "the kind of film Mel Brooks would make if he'd been a cartoonist". Whether you watch Slide as a story about a mysterious cowboy or a grotesque critique on violence and anti-environmental capitalism, you'll find treasures in every corner of the frame.

films.syn: Stekken is a short 3D animation which explores the themes of serenity, nature, time and reverie. The film tries to capture the dreamlike feeling of a lazy summer afternoon.
A film about storm not only as a weather condition, but also as a state of mind. Storm as a metaphor for the struggles in life.
One day, all the statues come to life. They all leave in the same direction. None of the human bystanders can figure out why.

A remarkable and multifaceted retelling of the life and work of Bengali writer Begum Rokeya Hossain, inspired by her seminal utopian fiction about a land where women are in charge. "In Ladyland you will not see men on the streets. We shut our men indoors! Isn't that sweet?" Envision a land where men - deemed a violent liability - are locked up and where women govern with an ethos of genuine harmony. This is exactly what Bengali writer Begum Rokeya Hossain imagined in her utopian feminist parable Sultana's Dream in 1905, a cornerstone of utopian fiction and ecofeminism. Hossain's seminal work was a defiance of traditional male-dominated storytelling and still serves as a beacon of empowerment for women worldwide. Inspired by the Muslim pioneer's fiction and life, director Isabel Herguera spent a decade making her feature debut, a fascination labour of love that celebrates a cultural legacy, but also serves as an intriguing gateway into the framework of feminist theory and discourse. Like Herguera herself, Inés is an animation director in search of inspiration when she suddenly stumbles upon Sultana's Dream in a bookshop in India. Fascinated by her discovery of this transgressive tale, Inés embarks on a journey across the country to learn more about Hossain and the place of women in the world of yesterday and today. Through Herguera's lens, the film becomes more than a mere adaptation, evolving into a multifaceted exploration of womanhood and feminism as Inés travels to several destinations, including her father's Italian Bollywood movie sets. Sultana's Dream unfolds as a breathtaking triptych, with Inés' contemporary journey depicted through digital figures against hand-painted watercolour backdrops, while a musical retelling of Hossain's life emerges through cut-out animation. However, the most enchanting animation technique is perhaps found in the imaginative voyage to Ladyland, where Herguera employs the art of Mehndi, a variation of henna. Ultimately, Herguera's passion project is a philosophical piece of cinema, featuring real-life luminaries like gender theorist Paul B. Preciado and British academic Mary Beard, whose insights strengthens the film's profound engagement with gender dynamics, literature, and new perspectives.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: An animated music video for a song by Eliza Gilkyson that alludes to the Ukraine and the ongoing struggle.

A short animated documentary exploring the immigration experience through the eyes of a little Israeli girl learning how to swim with clothes on in the Netherlands. She meets other young migrants and discusses their experiences.

There are so many interesting stories to be found in Singapore just by observing kitchen windows. Each of them is unique, and each is home to residents of different races and cultural backgrounds. This film is a snapshot of what happens to the residents and their neighbours.

The film is about communist leader Mao Zedong and his mango cult. Mao gifted replica wax mangoes, entombed in glass cases, to factory workers as a propaganda tool. This lead to the fruit ataining an almost sacred status.

A man troubled by a disease finds himself paralyzed in a remote and hostile environment after an accident. As he is grappling with his situation, he turns to an inner force which brings a whole new reality. A horror film inspired by Santiago Dabove's (1889 - 1951) short story "Ser polvo".
Fish & Meat pulls you into the world of experimental hip-hop group Choolers Division, whose members are artists-in-residence at the art brut center La S in Belgium.

films.t: The Famous Grouse: Full of Character
films.syn: A global ad campaign for The Famous Grouse by Nexus Studios, directed by BAFTA-winning director Paloma Baeza.
The Fell We Climb is an animated short film inspired by the real life experiences of dark skinned youngsters growing up in Cumbria. Its aim is to highlight and combat racism.

Dániel Juhász is an aspiring painter in his early twenties. He is in the final interview for a spot in the Academy of Fine Arts painting department. His anxiety is overwhelming and he starts to imagine his fears as garden pests.
The Hour Coat takes place between the last knowable time and unknowable time. The film is made from approximately 18,000 graphite drawings on tracing paper, made by hand.

A gas station in a toy town is running non-stop. Customers keep buying, the mascot keeps cheering them on. But when acid rain starts to pour, only one girl notices that something is amiss. This French student film seemingly honours Walt Disney's classic The Skeleton Dance but turns up the madness.

films.t: The Lords of Water – Launch Film
films.syn: Plastic pollution is one of the greatest threats our planet is facing right now. This is represented in the mixed media piece The Lords Of Water . Featuring a soundtrack and voice over from legendary actor Matt Berry, the film takes a novel approach to water marketing.
A relationship horror and unromantic comedy about a couple forced to deal with escalating bodily transformations.

Russian emperor Peter the Great ... But was he really that great? In violent shapes, high-contrast images and expressive computer-generated 3D sculptures, Sasha Svirsky formulates an outcry against Russia's mentality and the bloody dream that has contaminated people's minds.
The Miracle is a place where the sun always shines, with endless opportunities to relax and food in abundance. Still something is missing.

films.t: The Order of Detection Through The Mist
films.syn: A promo video for the launch of new characters in the game Identity V. It unveils the mystery of the Misty Kingdom.

The Posthuman Hospital is an experimental animation inspired by Donna Haraway's 'Cyborg Manifesto.' It explores the uncertain boundaries between human and non-human in the context of technological advancement. It does so by showcasing medical records of several posthuman patients in an imaginary hospital, offering insights into the interactions between humans and technological entities.
Princess Zarabanda is part of the oral legend of the Lenca Tribe in Honduras. It's the story of two great Titans who fall in love with a princess. A struggle between the Titans ensues.

A wild utopia. On the edge of a mangrove, a group of girls lives to the rhythm of the climate and the geese around them. They see each other live and grow up at different ages. As time passes, tensions arise and rivalries develop. Clémence Bouchereau's poetic pinscreen animation film is an unembellished take on childhood, steeped in a blend of loneliness and tenderness.

The Rubbings of Trajectories is an intimate story about space and memory. Drawing inspiration from travelling, the film invites the viewers to slip into a person’s consciousness and experience the relationship between one’s inner and outer worlds.

What a night for rock band L.I.O. Starving after an electrifying gig, they're on the prowl for a late-night feast.
