But things take an unexpected twist as the hungry musicians find themselves caught in a thrilling tale of danger and deception, and one demonic old lady. Peruvian animator Alvaro Giraldo proves himself to be a psychedelic force of nature in this bloody music clip.
The Skatebook is a short animated documentary which brings together a variety of voices from the skateboarding scene in London, England.
A film that explores the changing life of a mother and the challenges she faces. It also deals with the sacrifices needed to be a part of a family.
Big boobs vs. small boobs - who has it worse? A group of ladies discusses in what way being a part of a conservative society affects how we feel about our breasts.

A short animated musical, Three Cookie Bakers features well ... three cookie bakers who return to their nest. But a flock of pate disapproves. From there the plot thickens. Tom Schrooten and Jacob van de Water have truly embraced that "bonkers" vibe in their hilarious collaboration.
All the characters from the Théâtre du Passage's 2022-2023 season arrive at the same time in the theatre's forecourt. Two kids witness their arrival before rushing in to be on time for the show.

films.t: To Come to Terms or Make Your Terms
films.syn: Twelve case workers in Bundelkhand, have been dealing with cases of domestic violence for years. They travel to remote corners of the region to meet women and their families and try to help them. Not all women have the choice to leave.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: A surreal story of a group of boys playing a sport, with one outsider. They lose their consciousness and odd things happen.
A water fight for the ages! Pam and Linda are neighbours and sworn enemies. So of course their ongoing feud escalates into an epic water fight that spirals out of control. May the best woman win!

Filmmaker Shira Avni continues her personal animated documentary journey to explore motherhood, fragmentation, neurodiversity, trauma, and healing. Two One Two mixes archival video, sound recordings, clay on glass, under-camera, and rotoscoped animation.
Unique Together is an animated branding video about the collective work environment of the creative agency Infotext.

A filmmaker receives an extortion email claiming to have recorded webcam footage of him masturbating. This leads to an exploration of the link between shame and masturbation through a series of Zoom conversation with his friends.
An experimental documentary animation exploring a mother and daughters relationship and how generational trauma created a vicious cycle across three generations.

An animated music video to create awareness amongt children on the importance of clean water and oceans. The Alpagua by German NGO Viva con Agua makes social hits for Kids to achieve the 17 goals for sustainable development by the United Nations.
Two gnomes are chased away by a flood of tears caused by a childish king. When they meet, the king starts playing with them and is happy again, but only briefly.

Mary, Billybud and Fumbleton are three miniature, human actors who perform in an eighties kids TV series called “Wander to Wonder”. After the creator of the series dies, they are left alone in the studio. With their slowly decaying costumes and growing hunger, they continue to make increasingly strange episodes for their fans.

This film for charity War Child shows fairy tale creatures encountering obstacles. The story symbolically represents the harsh conditions of war and highlights the importance of addressing psychological needs during difficult times.

Remember those dreadful teenage years? 'When Adam Changes' is a heartfelt portrait of growing up, navigating through bodily transformations, impossible crushes and pool parties. "I've always said you had a long torso." Remember those dreadful teenage years? Your parents seemed cringy 24/7, bullies at school were as mean as dictators, managing that big crush of yours was rather depressing, and your body changed for better or for worse. On top of that, the 90s weren't exactly the years of "body positivity" ... Drawing inspiration from the little and low-profile town he grew up in, Canadian director Joël Vaudreuil has crafted a weird and wonderful time capsule with his feature debut When Adam Changes . As a slice-of-life straight from the 90s with oddball characters, dry humour and relatable observations on puberty. It walks a delicate yet entertaining line between iron and sincerity, something which charmed the festival jury in Ottawa, where it won the prize for Best Animated Feature. 15-year-old Adam's life hasn't exactly been one of highlights. And to annihilate any confidence he might have had, his grandmother's final words before collapsing in her hospital bed are a snarling comment on his "long torso", causing Adam's torso to literally extend. It's been this way all his life: whenever his body is mocked, it distorts to reflect the callous remarks of relatives and the targeted vitriol of fellow teens. Yet, his physical transformations are in some ways the least of his worries as he tries to navigate teenage life in 90s Quebec, complete with an impossible crush on a red-haired and party-hard classmate, illegal pool parties, summer jobs, macho films, bizarre dreams, and typical ennui. Through quirky minimalist designs and backgrounds, Vaudreuil constructs a heartfelt and authentic coming-of-age portrait that resonates with our own memories. When Adam Changes defies expectations by transcending its role as playful and occasionally melancholic tale of self-acceptance - it also retains an ironic, sinister undertone, contributing to its overall sense of absurdity. In many ways, this easy-to-love film mirrors the complexity of our own teenage years.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: It's not every day you meet a unicorn. And it's not everyday you kill such a mighty beast. Care to explain, Ray? In this Taiwenese student short, Ray recalls his wild night leading to betrayal and dire consequences for both man and unicorn.

A cat lover, Jesus leaving the cross and Christmas carollers holding pitchforks are set against a snowy and icy scenery in this punk Christmas mosaic of a small fisherman's village. Partly based on Tomek Popakul's own winter memories, Zima is an eerie story of loneliness and of a community where different views, the behaviour of people and animals and their mutual relations clash like ice floes. Infused with punk, choir and piano music, this magical realist animation shows horror, cruelty, but also tender care in a frozen lagoon.
Love punch love. Artist Faiyaz Jafri pushes aesthetics to the max and creates a weirdly soothing experience.

Yuck! Couples kissing on the mouth are gross. Even the moment before people kiss is gross. Little Léo laughs at them, just like all the kids at the summer camp. But secretly he would like to try kissing himself.

Zeze and Mercedes are young friends from the Turkish countryside. Suddenly Zeze comes by Mercedes' house. Hesitant to explain the reason behind his short visit, Mercedes challenges Zeze to a race over the carpet. Throughout the race they are joined by imaginary friends.

On a hot summer’s day at the local swimming pool, 14-year-old Louane is enjoying a moment of peace and quiet until she is approached by Aïssa. Sheltered from the world around them, the two friends share an intimate moment. A sweet and well-told coming-of-age film by the talented Juliette Ragot.

We present to you: the only Belgian film ever to win an Academy Award! Nicole Van Goethem's A Greek Tragedy even beat Pixar's Luxo Jr. in the Oscar race from 1987. In this "tragey", three scantily-clad female figures struggle to hold up the crumbling remains of an ancient Greek temple.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: A whimsical take on life, death, and life cycles, this short follows a group of rabbits in a house. As they multiply, the house overgrows until they all perish. Haunted by their ghosts, new rabbits appear, and the cycle begins again. A rhythmic and charming display of rabbit poetry in motion, this two-minute visual delight by director Sarah Ruyle features a lovely graphic style and, of course, plenty of rabbits!

films.t: A Night at the Rest Area
films.syn: At a midnight highway rest area, the weary bus travelers each quietly relax their minds. A brief moment spent with complete strangers is lonely, yet somehow comforting. Sweet, small observations of traveling life by Japanese director Saki Muramoto.

films.t: A Round of Applause for Death
films.syn: In A Round of Applause for Death , death takes center stage as faceless spectators applaud the inevitable in a series of murderous dreams. A macabre and surreal journey, rich in comedic timing and repetition, by British award winning director Stephen Irwin.

films.t: A Small Garden by the Window
films.syn: In a beautifully designed world by South Korean director Jonghoon Lee, an architect picks ripe cherry tomatoes from a small garden by the window, preparing a lunchbox for work. Eco-energy flows from the tomato vines—an invisible force born from small acts of environmental care. This quiet energy accompanies the architect as they head out once again to face the frontlines of the climate crisis. Get ready to feel warm inside.

films.t: A Town Called Panic: The Noise of the Grey
films.syn: No one really does it like filmmaking duo Stéphane Aubier and Vincent Patar ... In this creative and funny short, their by now iconic characters of Indian, Cowboy and Horse try to throw a party. It's all fun and games, until a troublemaker enters and ruins everything. Just like in their feature A Town Called Panic , Aubier & Patar bring their endless imagination and energy to the table, or playground so to speak.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: A Visualization of a Cut is an experimental animated short film exploring the connection between the cinematic cut and human relations. The film is a meditation on life, love and loss, explored through montage editing in home movies from six Scandinavian families, the materiality of paper and the thread that joins them together.
This Adult Swim ident is a musical and lyrical masterpiece that would make The White Stripes jealous. And... 1, 2, 3, 4!

This funky Adult Swim ident feels like you're watching a worn-out videotape. The glitchy music sets the rhythm while the characters in the animation stretch and reshape, almost literally dancing their asses off.
This Adult Swim ident is a nod to your biggest dreams. Watch up close as a charming person on a sun-drenched beach rubs on the creamiest sunscreen. Squish!
After watching this ident for Adult Swim, you'll think twice before drinking water from a river.
Welcome to Adult Swim's magical winter wonderland. A thrilled snowboarder races down the mountain in style, but his finish doesn’t quite go as expected…

Is it a plane? A bird? Or a crossover between Powerpuff Girls and Panty & Stocking with Garterbelt ? This ident was created by students from HSLU Lucerne, Switzerland, in collaboration with long-time partner Adult Swim.

Seventy-two-year-old Pedro struggles to accept that his adult son Alex is moving abroad. As they go on their final hunt together, which is filled with repressed words and feelings, they discover that their dog Canela has swallowed fox poison. Alex and Pedro deal with this tragedy in opposing ways. A strong and poignant work by award-winning Spanish director José Prats.

films.t: An Elephant in the Porcelain Cabinet
films.syn: An Elephant in the Porcelain Cabinet is a stop-motion and 2D animated short film about damage and how we deal with it, visualized through a fragile space that receives a clumsy visitor. A pretty student exploration into material, technique, and learning to open up, by director Bonne Steinz.
A short and sweet segment for an animated advent calendar, by Swiss director Fabian Meister.

films.t: Art & Davey: The Housemate From Hell
films.syn: Art, a twenty-something year old student returns to his apartment after a long day of work. Only to find out that his stoner roommate, Davey, accidentally let a demon into their apartment! Now, Art’s got a double whammy on his hands: banishing a literal hellspawn and dealing with a roommate who's too high to help out in any meaningful way.

In this dark satire, three babies in a maternity ward talk to each other like men at a urinal, but in the most vulgar way. The topic of conversation? Women. Or more specifically: their own mother! That’s bound to lead to some trouble.

On a warm summer’s day, Léonie shows Rose the village where she grew up. While taking a stroll through the sunny streets, they go right down memory lane, revisiting the moments that made Léonie who she is now. An authentic sensitive story by Mariam Farota.

Alec and Theo are partners, both on stage and in life. They have found the perfect balance between lifting and flying, between leading and following, until this fragile balance is turned upside down by an accident. A sweet and simple stop-motion marvel that depicts the intricacies of a relationship.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Ever felt as if you never really woke up after getting out of bed? Then you can definitely relate to the main character in Between Yawns . Still under the influence of sleep, his actions and visions are not what they should be... This great student work by director Alma Rajot will literally make you yawn.

On July 25, 2020, the MV Wakashio ran aground off Mauritius, and twelve days later, oil began leaking, causing the region's worst ecological disaster ever seen. In Black Tide , Kim Yip Tong blends animated documentary and art film to depict the trauma of coastal residents who fought to save the lagoon.

Can a sheep and a flower turn you on? You’re about to find out. Using surrealist techniques, Bon Appetite explores the process of intimate relationships, where the sheep and the flower symbolize the merging into a symbiotic state. An original student work by Chinese directors Ziyu Wang and Jinhong Yu.

A lo-fi, aesthetically pleasing, and surreal semi-musical about a teenage gig worker who encounters a donut-shaped alien in suburban Florida. “Have a Grubby day!” Welcome in Julian Glander’s wonderfully weird, neon-coloured world, where we meet Billy 5000, a high school dropout who was once dubbed “the human calculator”, but now tries to make it to $5,000 working for food delivery app Grubster. Along the way, Billy encounters a donut-shaped alien who’s being hunted by juice mogul Dr. Dolphin who grows mutated fruits from moon rocks. And what seems like a distant planet full of oddities, is actually just an alternate suburban Florida. Was the pandemic good for something after all? The idea for this deadpan musical comedy about a teenage gig worker with a rise-and-grind mindset came to Glander when he spent a lot of time on Google Street View during the lockdown. He grew up in Tampa and zooming around Florida in 3D made him feel like he was back there again. A brain fart or two later (and loads of hours playing around in Blender), Boys Go to Jupiter was born. Influenced by Peanuts episodes, the offbeat Rankin/Bass holiday specials, the claymation Frog and Toad series, next to his own animated GIFS and work for Adult Swim, Glander delivers a surprising lo-fi indie film that somewhat resembles the look and feel of a cosy game. Boys Go to Jupiter even throws in a few memorable songs, including a ballad about the various ways you can eat eggs and an alien song about combo meals of every shape and size. More of a collage of encounters of the strange kind, it’s a fabulously bonkers film featuring bored teenagers and pretty bizarre interactions, yet Glander’s feature debut is also a timely story about economic inequality and our late-capitalist Western society.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Ukrainian director Mykyta Lyskov based his animations for Bridge on engravings by Dnipro-based artist Andrii Sokolenko. This beautifully crafted short film transports you to a bumpy world of railways, making you feel as if you are traveling east.

In the sea, a man swims. As he does, memories come to the surface. From his early childhood to his life as a man, all his memories are linked to water. Some are happy, some glorious, some traumatic. This story will be that of his last swim. Powerful, heart-wrenching work by director Florence Miailhe.

In a peaceful garden two delicate butterflies engage in a violent turf war. Each lays claim to the control of a beautiful flower but behind their colorful facades lies a dark secret. British director Michael Marczewski mixes bright and vibrant animation with a dose of his dark trademark humor in this short film.

Hunting season has begun! A family of capybaras seeks refuge in a chicken coop, but the hens don't trust them. However, the curiosity of the youngest members of the family will create a union with unexpected consequences. A film about refugee crises and solidarity by director Alfredo Soderguit, based on his eponymous picture book.

Catherine loves pets! But most of all, she loves her cat. As she grows up, she can't seem to connect with people. Her cat is her life, and little by little she grows up to be a crazy old cat lady ... How crazy? Well, according to Belgian animator Britt Raes: very crazy! Boasting expressive colours and offbeat yet cutesy character designs, Catherine is a touching and darkly funny story about (dis)connection.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: The hunter's daughter and a young wolf unexpectedly rescue each other while wandering in the forest in search of their parents. Upon finding them, they face a difficult choice: follow the path of their parents or preserve their friendship. A touching and aesthetically pleasing film by Kyrgyz director Shamir Raiapov.

After a young girl draws a circle on the sidewalk, strangers curiously step inside. Crowding together, they form a fascinating community of diverse people. A great minimalist piece by South Korean filmmaker Joung Yumi.
A short cartoon for Clipphanger about scabies! How do you get it, and what can you do about it? Very educational and... super gross. Scratch away!

A girl wakes up alone on a surreal night, with moths emerging from the TV set, guiding her to explore the darkened room. Through a series of emotional flashbacks, she gradually recalls fragmented memories of neglect by her caregivers. Cocoon is a crayon poem about metamorphosis, darkness, and light, directed by Chinese director Yiwei Chen.

Urban pigeons are seen as pests, like rats of the sky. They are rudely chased away, and their nests are removed. When a group of pigeons hears that the mayor promises housing for everyone, they decide to submit a petition at the town hall. But first, they have to get past the evil janitor. A coo-licious film by Alina Milkina.

Corn Man was just a simple man. One day, his cornfield was invaded by ducks. Fueled by righteous anger at the desecration of his immaculate field, he chased them away, as he held a sacred aversion to animals. It was at that moment that he triggered something tasty that would change his life forever!

Winston Hacking directed this official video for the song Jump Cut by the band Corridor. He delivers a sweet collage music clip with vintage found footage and live-action cuts, mixed in the most surreal combinations. Edited incredibly creatively, every new shot is a welcome surprise.

The intro to Desk Bugs warns you that the film contains flashing images. But that’s not all. There’s a bright red desk and a blue pencil. Also skulls, cups, and a modular synthesizer. They appear when you sit at the desk. With their fluffy purple bodies, they're called Desk Bugs. Still with us? Wow! OK, just prepare for a three-minute psychedelic trip packed with color, rhythm, bleeps, and rapid-fire edits and you’re good to go!

When a sausage dog acts as a bridge, allowing all kinds of animals to literally walk all over him, a cat smells a business opportunity. A very entertaining and satirical nod to capitalism by Jorn Leeuwerink.

Down in the Dumps is a dark fairy tale written by Britt Snel and directed by paper artist and director Vera van Wolferen. It tells the story of Cinelli, a perfectionist ladybug who excludes the outsider cockroach Peri to prevent her party from being ruined. Peri is not amused and seeks… revenge!

Drizzle in Johnson follows a scientist driven by an obsession to unravel the universe’s mysteries, plunging into a surreal journey filled with grotesque and shocking imagery. Deliberately bizarre and provocative, director Ivan Li pushes the boundaries of conventional storytelling in this 20 minute nightmarish odyssey.

Have you felt overwhelmed by the news lately? Then you might have noticed that the battle for our attention has suddenly become an actual war. Information technologies appear not just as mere means for somebody’s ends, but as one of the acting forces. We have no control over it and are doomed to scroll through the newsfeed. At least, that’s what director Sasha Svirsky concludes in this idiosyncratic response to the state of the world.

Edith and the Tall Child is a deeply intimate, hand-drawn film about hair, dysphoria, and the growing pains of a repeating puberty. It follows the titular Tall Child as they outgrow their tiny apartment, their gender, and their giant ground sloth, Edith. A beautiful yet confusing journey about self-image, directed by Kohana Wilson.

A man searching for the shortest thing in Tokyo uttered "da" at the last moment of his life. This witty work, the first in the Bungaku Bideo collaboration between contemporary Japanese literature and animation, features a recitation of Hideo Furukawa's Totemo mijikai , with animation by Koji Yamamura.
A light-hearted, animated introduction to some of the facts, myths and risks of mainstream porn by director Joseph Clark.

In the heart of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Paul runs a grain mill. This morning, he is feverish, which does not prevent him from grinding grain. The machine's transmission belt breaks and that is a disaster. Paul sends Michel to Sakala to get a new belt. While he is hospitalized, he dialogues with his far away lands. This black-and-white sketch animation by Frédéric Hainaut is inspired by his bike trips with Olivier Coufer through rarely visited villages in the Congo. It gave the duo a feeling of being privileged witnesses, entrusted with the mission of sharing their observations, their impressions, their encounters and the voice of the Congolose in the form an animated film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: In 1934, Professor Vangengheim is condemned to the Solovski Gulag, a remote prison camp in Russia. As he pretends to be on a grand voyage of exploration, he crafts imaginative tales in letters to his daughter Eleonora, shielding her from the truth of his sentencing as a "traitor to the motherland". Breathtaking and award-winning document of the political repressions in Russia, by Russian director Alexey Evstigneev.

A series of innocent and harmless actions in the daily lives of four ordinary people in an apartment complex. The joys and sorrows of living next to each other in a colorful cartoon. Flatlife was Belgian screenwriter/director/actor/tv personality Jonas Geirnaert's graduation work and won the Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Following his father's death, French-Iraqi journalist Feurat Alani reflects on his father's life and the history of a country that has barely known peace since its creation. At nine years old, in 1989, Feurat Alani got his first real flavour of Iraq, the country that sent his militant father into exile. Today, many year later, it's his father's Fatiha, a traditional Muslim memorial service to honour the deceased. For Feurat, it's a moment to reflect on his father's political activism and his dream for a flourishing Iraq, but also to unlock memories of his childhood and to retrace the broader story of Iraq - a story that transcends the images spread in Western media. Instead, we see a country of profound cultural wealth, one that has tragically barely known peace since its creation. Flavors of Iraq , an animated documentary directed by Léonard Cohen in collaboration with Franco-Iraqi journalist Feurat Alani, is a dazzling trip through Iraq's history, from a secular state of great prospects to an ultra-authoritarian cage, an occupied and embargoed nation, and a war-torn land of religious leadership. Alani first chronicled his personal and familial history in over 10.000 tweets, recounting the vivid experiences he had in Iraq as a child. These tweets were adapted into an award-winning book illustrated by Cohen, followed by a web series. Now, the feature film reassembles this material into a highly emotional, non-Westernized look at more than half a century's worth of history, and continues the story by revealing the scars left by the Islamic State. Cohen and Alani's film offers detailed yet stylized impressions of a vanished homeland. In evocative and fluid animations - interspersed with archival footage, Flavors of Iraq guides us through musings about apricot ice creams, family visits and broken dreams, while also facing the devastations of dictatorship, illegal wars and oppression. What ultimately emerges is a collection of stories - both deeply personal and strikingly universal - that reveal the flavours, perfumes, tastes, and essence of a nation shaped by triumph and tragedy.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: A green garden full of garden gnomes stands peacefully, until golfers on the other side of the fence start doing their thing. When wayward golf balls bombard the garden gnomes, the mood shifts dramatically. Fore!

Format Error Occurred at Offset cuts through the administrative paperwork required for the director to live in different countries, exploring the ambiguity and fragility of identity within bureaucratic systems, cultural contexts, and today's social industry. An AI-critical animated documentary by Zirui Chen.

A young woman filled with regret retraces her footprints in the sand. As she walks along the shore, she relives how a shocking confession to her friend Fryd changed the course of their friendship forever. Intriguing, mysterious and beautifully designed short by director Adelen Holt.

Fusion investigates the interplay and love affair between sound and picture as an abstract experimental experience. Using a wide variety of colors and shapes, director Richard Reeves creates a sense of dimension and space in this trippy, handmade short film, with both sound and pictures created by drawing onto 35mm film.

An infectious, freewheeling and unusual anime hangout movie about a girl who befriends a giant, ghostly cat. When a wide-eyed, human-sized and immortal “ghost cat” – who has a side gig as a masseur – isn’t the most bizarre thing in town, you know you've stepped into a whimsical world. Yet, for all its quirks, infectious characters and freewheeling turns, Ghost Cat Anzu is an emotionally sharp tale about a teenager trying to cope with loss. Three years after her mother’s death, precocious tween Karin finds herself abandoned by her father in rural Japan, in the sleepy coastal town of Iketeru. She’s now forced to live with her widowed grandfather in a temple. But that’s doesn’t mean he lives alone. A long time ago, he took in a stray cat that is now grown into a giant and capricious feline called Anzu, who gambles his way through life while taking various odd jobs. Anzu, a ‘bakeneko’ (a supernatural creature from Japanese myth), is asked to look after Karin, who desperately wants to see her mother. Based on Takashi Imashiro’s manga, Ghost Cat Anzu starts off as a breezy, hangout movie, before morphing into a wacky, surreal and spiritual odyssey. Where else would you find a protagonist, her ghostly feline companion, and the God of Poverty travelling to the underworld via a Tokyo toilet bowl? With charm and wit aplenty, the film transitions seamlessly from a slice-of-life countryside comedy into a magical meditation on the blurred connections between the dead and the living. What sets Ghost Cat Anzu apart is its grounded, naturalistic feel – a rarity for a story involving otherworldly characters. Live-action performances were rotoscoped into animation, breathing authenticity into its fantastical world. It’s all thanks to the collaboration between animator Yoko Kuno, maker her feature directorial debut, and live-action director Nobuhiro Yamashita ( Linda Linda Linda ). By the end, chances are, you’ll be longing for a ghostly sidekick of your own. Preferably one like Anzu.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Pinocchio feels a longing deep within him. Someday, he would become a real girl and live a life beyond the confines of make-believe. Experimental animation at its finest!

Sam, Lexi, and Jane spend the first day of eighth grade plotting to secure the ultimate lunch table. Their plans unravel when Katy, a preppy sixth-grade TikTok influencer, beats them to the coveted spot. A rebellious, lighthearted high school story filled with bullying and power games, by Los Angeles-based director Ofre Sparrow Vaknin.

Three people are confronted by their fears of inadequacy. By following their stories, director Jamie Machul tries to understand what it means to be good enough. They deliver fascinating images by experimenting with various printing techniques in this meditative short film.

Geoff is a creative individual who sometimes struggles with his feelings. Is there something wrong with him? In a group session with his favorite tools – an all-star cast of peculiar puppets – and through a ridiculously catchy song, he finally discovers what has been going on all this time…

Once seen as terrifying dragons, glaciers are now evaporating, warning us of what’s catching up. They fly away, leaving the mark of a thousand-year-old reign. HIC SVNT DRACONES plunges through these giants, on a journey where the scales of space and time fragment. With beautiful paint-on-glass animations, director Justin Fayard memorializes the world we still know today.
In the heart of a dark forest, two silhouettes meet, attract and repel each other in an explosive bridal parade. Hold Me Tight is a dark, sensual portrayal of sexual pleasure.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Honkytonk's Dream is a charming animated collage featuring a waddling, paddling menagerie of found illustrations! A commission for 1927 and the Friends of Pymmes Park, directed by Laurie Hill.

In House of Broken Hearts , Anna follows her heart as it leads her to different relationships, which manifest around her as clingy, alluring and comforting pieces of furniture. After a few dramatic breakups, they try to navigate love and deal with the pain of heartbreak. Striking short by director Aisha Madu.

Hurikán rushes out to save his favorite beer stand from closure by fetching a new keg to impress the bartender he has a crush on. In a wild Prague district, he faces robbers, cops, and his own thirst. A tense but very funny black-and-white animation, incredibly directed by Jan Saska.

I Died in Irpin is a testimony by animator Anastasiia Falileieva, who escaped Ukraine with her boyfriend during the war. Spending 10 days in a blockaded city, they managed to escape with the last evacuation convoy.

Chinese director Ziyin Wang began creating this visually striking short during her graduation year, a time filled with goodbyes and uncertainty about the future. The story follows a protagonist waiting alone at an ice rink, where a chance encounter with a stranger leads to shared reflections on loneliness, warmth, and the desire for understanding, ultimately bringing them solace in each other's stories.

A magical elf party in the woods comes to a sudden end, leaving the forest goddess all alone. Luckily for our music-loving heroine, nature always finds a way to celebrate. Illegal Mana is a commissioned anthology by the director trio Nice Try, consisting of Pia Graf, Jack Zhang, and Julia Müller.

Immature is a colorful animated documentary by director Eddy Wu that explores the fluidity and complexity of gender identity. The film delves into the evolving experiences of a transgender gay man, capturing the nuances of his self-exploration.

Director Qianhui Yu was commissioned by GIPHY to create a 28-second personal animation. The result is a hand-drawn, imaginative story based on the events in her own garden after she moved to Stoke-on-Trent.

Gina, a young musician, spends the weekend at her family’s mountain hut to focus on her music. However, strange figures intrude, disrupting the peace with their obtrusive behavior. The escalating tension leads to an emotional explosion and a casual flower jam. A great student film by Swiss director Laura Kohler.

Méditerranée is an animated music video by Juniore, directed by Clement Soulmagnon. You follow Anna as she reminisces about her carefree days in Nice, discovering the magic of the Mediterranean, which culminates in a solitary swim. A tribute to the beauty and tranquility of the Mediterranean.

Kissing Day is a short animated documentary based on an interview with the renowned Russian journalist and LGBTQ+ activist Elena Kostyuchenko. This poignant film tells the story of the Kissing Day protest, organized by Elena, during the first hearings on the law banning 'gay propaganda' among minors.

You have weird, and then you have WEIRD. In this fruity graduation film, a man crawls out of a banana and explains how he found himself there. Meanwhile, a fish is contemplating her own beauty. These two stories are observed and dissected and cause a reaction that cracks the reality the observer is in.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: The 3D animated documentary Kupalba tells the deeply moving story of a family torn apart by the Russian-Georgian war in Abkhazia. During the conflict, up to 300,000 people were displaced from their homes, forced to seek refuge in areas under Tbilisi's control. Director Vano Tvauri delivers a well-constructed and emotionally powerful narrative of war’s lasting impact.

A dog loses grasp of its shape and time while balling like Shaquille O'Neal in this psychedelic short film. The colorful animation feels as if you’re constantly stretching and reshaping your own handmade Play-Doh figure. Larry is an intriguing ongoing project by director Takeshi Murata in collaboration with Christopher Rutledge.

What if Władysław Starewicz, Tim Burton and Terry Gilliam would make a movie together? It might as well end up looking like Les Bêtes ! A mysterious rabbit with a set of magic keys summons a host of strange creatures to entertain a wicked king and his decadent court. Terrific dark stop-motion animated fantasy by director Michael Granberry.
This music video for Les Savy Fav’s Guzzle Blood depicts the gory war between cats and robots. Expect a lot of violence, blood, and unnecessary victims set to a soundtrack of intense rock music!

A sapphic sci-fi adventure through gay space, including a lesbian princess, straight white "maliens", and a problematic spaceship. In a gay-laxy far, far away ... A queer cult classic in the making, Lesbian Space Princess is an outrageously fun sci-fi adventure about Saira, "the most boring royal in the history of Clitopolis". Where the flipping f**k is Clitopolis, you might ask. Well, it's a planet that is "famously hard to find". Saira is devastated when she is unexpectedly dumped by her girlfriend and sapphic cool kid, Kiki - who also happens to be a bounty hunter. But when Kiki is kidnapped by the galaxy's most obnoxious villains, the forgotten (and desperate-for-chicks) Straight White Maliens (yep, you read that correctly), Saira is forced to step up and blast off on a mission to save the girl she definitely (maybe?) still has feelings for. The stage is set for a cosmic rollercoaster through gay space (which is of course protected by a safety bubble). Transport comes in the form of a mansplaining spaceship with a problematic personality stuck in the 21st century. Proudly wearing its influences on its sleeve, from Futurama and Rick & Morty to even Fritz the Cat - Lesbian Space Princess is the first ever fully animated feature film to come out of South Australia. Making their feature debut, Emma Hough Hobbs and Leela Varghese have written a hilarious quest for (self)love which warps us to an offbeat collection of hazardous encounters with gloom goo, blade-wielding maniacs, dangerous dick turrets and the scariest thing of all: self-doubt. Lesbian Space Princess is a queer-positive space opera filled with tongue-in-cheek humour, and ... euh ... a lot of tongues in cheeks. The film playfully flips heteronormative tropes, combining classic Saturday morning cartoon chaos with postmodern irony. Now, where's Clitopolis again? 👑 DRESS-UP CONTEST ✨ Be the (intergalactic, queer) princess you always wanted to be.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: In this vibey music video, a pajama awakens alone in his room, immersed in nostalgic thoughts. Suddenly, mysterious shadows appear and captivate him. His bed comes to life and carries him away in a strange and magical dance.

This minimalistic short film by director Daan Lucas follows the life cycle of the seemingly useless organoid. Its movements, character, dry lips—everything about it is a part of life. Ain’t it beautiful?

Director River Roest sees Lil' Guys as an exploration of his love for animation, the exhaustion it can cause, and ultimately, the joy it brings. In this groovy short, lots of small elements come to life, moving to the rhythm of the funky soundtrack.

This is a story about migration, but above all, it is a story about hope. In this crayon animation, migrant children share their experiences and expectations about their journey to the United States and toward a different life.
Little Edy is bored to death while Banjo is glued to his smartphone. But fate lends Little Edy a hand. An inattentive businessman mistakes Banjo for a valet and hands him his car keys. Let’s go!

While on a school trip to Italy, the three schoolgirls Emma, Lydia, and Alice stay in a convent. As time passes, Emma finds herself attracted to Alice. When things are about to get steamy, Emma suddenly feels as though the religious statues are judging her! A hilarious short by French director Clémence Taveau.
A fly goes airborne to meet a close friend—another black-and-white pixel art masterpiece by Swiss filmmaker and video game designer Michael Frei.

Lucky Dog is an animated musical satire, following Dice, a dog raised in an Indian household who dreams of a better life. Believing he's entitled to more privileges than the pests in his apartment, he decides to follow his owner, Disha, when she immigrates to Canada. The story humorously critiques privilege and explores the contrasting views on immigration.

The vibrations of an abandoned phone in the woods attract several music-loving fairies. They join their musical forces to create a tiny fairy rave. A vibrant and funky ident, produced for Adult Swim Off the Air (MUSIC) in close collaboration with musician Xav Clarke.

Director Rebecca Blöcher's mother led a very unorthodox life, living in palaces and under bridges. Her independence was most important for her, which in the end became her undoing. She decided to live in her tiny car for 10 years. Only when the car broke down and she was unable to walk even, mother and daughter got the chance to re-connect. Loving portrait of an eccentric mum.

Revisiting her childhood memories, including her restless mother, her father struggling with potatoes and herself growing up in the bustling city of Nairobi alongside her two sisters, Norwegian Oscar winner Torill Kove ( The Danish Poet ) looks back at those flickering memories that have matured into key experiences. Maybe Elephants is both a playful coming-of-age story and a loving autobiographical homage to family and the therapeutic power of memories, however unreliable.

Through audio recordings made in the field and poetic moving images, Mealitancy portrays activists who use food as a tool in their anti-consumerist struggle. This short film by Marie Royer and Zinia Scorier highlights the positive impact of activism in the pursuit of creating a better world.
A short animated trailer commissioned by the Miami Jewish Film Festival, celebrating the joy of the colorful Miami. Created by Daphna Awadish Golan.
To give a snake an orange… MIMT is a fable about animals chasing each other across planes of existence. A beautifully crafted, abstract, experimental animation by director Ted Wiggin.

films.t: Mindaugas and Crusade for Love and Freedom
films.syn: Lithuania, 1251: just as Mindaugas is about to say 'I do,' his bride-to-be is suddenly beamed out of the church. What follows is a rather absurd series of attempts to find and rescue her. Chased by the police in true American fashion, he goes from bad to worse. Or rather, from heaven to hell!

After a soldier is knocked out, he awakens to find a little girl staring at him. He tries to kill her but misses, after which he sets off in pursuit. Upon arriving in an urban ruin, he is captured by a mysterious being, which gives the soldier the insight to follow a new path. A disturbing dystopian short film by director Max Gierkink.

A young boy is on holiday with his parents in Semarang, but their trip is marred by frequent arguments. During their journey, they stop at a gas station, and while his parents are distracted, the boy is lured into the forest by a mysterious woman. Director Elisabeth Katie Soleman presents a dark and unsettling story based on an old Indonesian folk tale.

Mary can't catch a break. Fusing motherhood with being a full-time carer for her disabled son has her up to her ears in red tape, barely keeping afloat. A surreal situation is looming. Director Naomi Noir pays tribute to society's true heroes in her surreal yet touching animation, giving a voice to those who dedicate their lives to others.

films.t: Motoyama Engine Works: Connected to History
films.syn: In Connected to History , an employee interacts with valve spirits, similar to tsukumogami—objects that have acquired a spirit. The commercial illustrates how the company has endured to the point where helpful spirits now inhabit the tools used by its employees.

Mountain Mountain follows two young adults, Charlotte and Valerie, as they ride a cable car up Mount Faber in search of mountains in Singapore. As they ascend, memories of their adventures in the mountains of New Zealand intertwine with the present, creating a fluid, almost dreamlike narrative. This smart and heartfelt student work by Ben Tan and Grace Cheu explores memory and the feeling of missing places.

Who can withstand a gory puppet musical that offers commentary on how cannibalistic the arts scene truly is? In Moving Parts , a weary traveling salesman encounters a grotesque, singing behemoth. This towering, two-headed monstrosity tempts him with a terrifying yet lucrative proposition.
Meet the world's cleanest superhero: Muscle Man! He battles a giant robot set on destroying the city. But his obsession with cleanliness and order might just be his downfall!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Sylvie and Karim have given it a lot of thought. At every breakfast and on every walk from the loo to the bathroom. They're ready to put the money they earned from scrubbing toilets in the hotel into Sylvie's latest aspiration: acquiring a domestic football player! Absurd and original story that makes you think, by the talented French director Cheyenne Canaud-Wallay.

films.t: Naive New Beaters & Star Feminine Band: Ye Kou Si Kuo
films.syn: Funky, sexy, and just plain nuts. Director Lola Lefèvre created this vibrant, colorful music video for the song Ye Kou Si Kuo by Naive New Beaters & Star Feminine Band. If this doesn’t make you swing, what will?

A snoozing fisherman, a dozing gardener, a restful raver... A diverse cast of characters drifts off while listening to The Sleeping Forecast in this beautifully hand-crafted stop-motion spot for the BBC Sounds podcast.

A moth leads u to the waiting room of a night-time station where a surreal sketch takes place. The first and last film to be made in its entirety in 'Servaisgraphy' (a technique to blend live-action with animation), Nocturnal Butterflies is inspired by the work of Belgian painter Paul Delvaux. A unique piece of animation history, crafted by the godfather of Belgian animation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: The sun moves lower and the days grow shorter. Birds fly south, porcelain animals and insects hide from the freezing wind and snow. Only a small porcelain girl wanders the abandoned landscape, with no way out. A wintry poem by director Anu-Laura Tuttelberg about Nordic nature, where animation and the rhythm of nature intertwine.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: A breath, a movement, a touch—followed by dissolution. This short film portrays the varied, sensual gestures of everyday life, floating in pastel colors. Beautifully told by Japanese director Yoriko Mizushiri.

In outer space, a captain and his loyal robot burn their bridges and decide to follow a creature called "Intuition." This leads them to a mysterious, desolate planet where they search for the meaning of life. Director Mickaël Dupré takes you on a nostalgic science fiction journey, accompanied by atmospheric music and a much-needed sense of wonder.

Six-year-old Lily visits her grandmother after she has had a mastectomy and no longer has breasts. Confused by her grandmother's changed appearance, Lily struggles to understand and tries to find a way to cope with the change. Beautifully animated in picture book style by Iranian creator Shadab Shayegan.

In early 1990s Hungary, three youngster devise a masterplan to travel abroad affordably. But freedom always comes at a price. Hungary's first feature-length animated documentary. "Those who can, will leave the country that forbids them to leave." It all started fairly innocent ... All great "crime" stories like that, don't they? After the end of communism in 1989, Hungary steps into a new decade with great prospects and high hopes regarding the freedom of its people. With the fall of the Iron Curtain, Hungary's borders suddenly open up. Everyone is eager to travel to Western Europe, young people in particular. But the price of a train ticket is prohibitive. What good is freedom if you can't afford it? Faced with this newfound but unaffordable liberty, three youngsters devise a masterplan: using household detergents they dissolve the Pelikan Blue ink on the train trickets (which were still handwritten), allowing them to make counterfeits to almost any destination. And off they go. A scheme of spying on ticket booths, researching procedures, studying timetables and stealing ticket covers helps an entire generation travel abroad affordably. But such freedom always comes at a price. Before long, the three young men are being eyed by the police. Pelikan Blue , Hungary's very first animated documentary feature, originated in archive audio interviews with many of the people involved nostalgically reminiscing the time when Eastern Europe was finally freed from its cage. Jumping between timelines and following the narrative codes of fiction filmmaking, director László Csáki's debut feature is an eclectic gangster comedy with great wit and an even greater sense of civil disobedience - or as one character puts it: "My mother told me that stealing from another man is a crime, but stealing from the state is glorious."

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Set against the backdrop of the sea and the urban Algarve, we follow the complete life cycle of a unique shellfish called Percebes (goose barnacle). From their formation to their place on the dish, this journey takes you through various contexts, offering a deeper understanding of the region and its inhabitants.

The ruthless Phallic Don is killed by his deceased arch-nemesis Lord Megaf*cker. That was something this charming guy with the memorable name really shouldn’t have done. Phallic Don plots revenge, and not in a loving way. Or does he?

A deranged Korean eco-horror fable about a pig that survived the foot-and-mouth epidemic, only to become as corrupt as the humans he detests. Nothing screams “Kaboom” more than a deranged Korean eco-horror fable about mutated pigs, armed desertion, a suicidal young woman, metamorphosis, and the chaos they all provoke. Drenched in atmospheric misanthropy, Pig That Survived Foot-and-Mouth Disease has been called a gory cross-over between Bong Joon-ho’s Okja and the nightmarish classic Watership Down . Even Sylvia Plath’s poetry gets thrown in the mix – and script. In a narrative where the humans are perhaps the real animals, Korean Academy of Film Arts graduate Hur Bum-wook’s sophomore feature dives into the foot-and-mouth epidemic of 2010 that led to the culling of hundreds of thousands of pigs. But what if one pig survived, built himself up from the ground (quite literally so) and retaliated? At the same time, what if a humiliated soldier, haunted by the murder of an officer, yearned to become an animal? These are the exact questions that kept Hur awake at night, causing him to direct a muddy fever dream of almost Dantesque proportions. Through all the anthropomorphising going on, corruption stands front and centre – making Pig That Survived Foot-and-Mouth Disease feel like a Shakespeare play transported to an era where humanity has stopped caring for every living being, whether human or animal. Impressively told and animated, it’s a monster of a film – in all the right ways.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: In Motion is a festival where a variety of artists and studio's share their love for animation, design, and film. These opening titles were created with the idea of playing and experimenting with anything that can constantly be in motion. The result: A sequence of experiments full of looping animations and playful patterns.

films.t: Please Make My Wish Come True
films.syn: Please Make My Wish Come True follows anonymous characters from their first wish as newborns to their final prayers. Through various rituals, it explores universal emotions of frustration, determination, surrender, and hope. A visual poem about hopes and unfulfilled desires, directed by Başak Kırıcı.

films.t: Pune Design Festival Versus Ident Film
films.syn: This film was created for the latest Pune Design Festival, themed 'Versus.' It depicts a fun competition between a designer (represented by a hand) and an idea (symbolized by colorful clay). Using stop-motion, the film showcases their interaction with bright colors, dynamic movements, and lively sound effects that bring it to life.

When every global citizen is required to have their CO2 emissions tracked through a mandatory mobile app, it seems to have little impact… that is, until they discover the consequences of reaching their designated quota! A hilarious and spot-on short film by Job, Joris & Marieke.

South Korean director Inju Park gave birth to this film to move to a world where the remains of her sister and herself can be reborn together. Reborn with You can be seen as a mesmerizing installation that naturally flows from one striking image to the next. A poetic short that could be looped for ages—if only we had the time…

Take a peek at the period of time between classes when the children are allowed to play. Location: a remote, secluded, or secret place. Everyday rituals in a rough, rhythmic, and playful animation loop, directed by the talented Talos Prophet.

For those who feel time-poor and overwhelmed by choice, this is a must-see. In the throes of his overstimulated, energy-poor midlife, Ray (Domhnall Gleeson) fantasises about everything he’d love to do in retirement, once he finally has ‘the time.’ Irish director John Kelly manages to capture the essence of life in just a few minutes in this poetic short film, which is nominated for Best Animated Short at the 98th Academy Awards (2026).

Meet Kurt and Freddy, two rednecks who own gas stations across from each other in South Dakota. They lead boring lives until they hear about a posthumous award for the person who dies in the most ridiculous way. The winner will have his face engraved on Mount Rushmore! Fascinated, they begin a crazy competition for the macabre honor, unknowingly putting a nearby scout camp in danger.

Although she left him, Gaspard is still very much in love with Leïla. When they meet up in a crowded bar a month after their break-up, the conversation takes a bit of an awkward turn. Gaspard feels tears welling up and seeks refuge under the tablecloth, away from the prying eyes and closer to his memories… A touching and honest story by Raphaël Jouzeau, told through vivid yet dreamy animations.

An old lady seems to be showing signs of mild dementia. Or is that just the appearance? Although she claims to know nothing, there are quite a few things around her that don’t seem quite right. Those old folks these days...

Shadows tells the true story of Ahlam, a teenage mother who fled Iraq, driven by a desire for freedom. The narrator recounts her memories in a metaphorical journey through the heart of an airport, where dreams and ghosts of the past mingle. Heartbreaking documentary by director Rand Beiruty.

In this animated miniature, a drawing gradually comes to life before our eyes, telling a story not only of a wild boar on the run, but also of the ways people have occupied places that used to belong to nature. Animator Nicolas Piret uses a single sheet of paper to tell this meticulously crafted short.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Using organic animation techniques, animator, illustrator and painter Rocío Álvarez goes on a poetic journey through the history of sex, which has long ignored and repressed the female pleasure. A journey from our cellular past to our Tinder present.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: In 1939, a young Romanian woman fell in love with a soldier. As their love blossomed, the man was sent to the front. They wrote passionate letters to each other, but when the woman had to move, they lost contact. Since then, she was never able to forget him. Will they ever meet again? Simply Divine recounts the secrets of a 91-year-old woman, revealing them at last.

A graffiti wall in Vienna transforms into an archaeological site and a graffiti sculpture, as ‘skrffologists' activate traces of the past with stop-motion animation. But can history ever be remembered clearly in all its complexity? Corrie Francis Parks and Daniel Nuderscher deliver a hypnotizing short, uncovering layer upon layer of color.

Humans and some kind of gnomes have posted videos on social media platforms in their dimension. Skroll is a short compilation of these clips—an animated, random flow of social media content that will truly surprise you and is worth watching until the end. A bizarre film by Marten Visser.

Solid as a Rock is a short documentary from the perspective of a 16-year-old climate activist. In her light-hearted way, she recounts the chaotic experience of being arrested and the rather unsuccessful intimidation attempts by the police. A personal story, brought to life by director Tiva Pam, offering insights on civil disobedience as a source of hope.

In this short film, puppets visualize how incredibly difficult it is to truly be there for a friend when their life is figuratively and literally falling apart due to illness. A beautiful film by Anna Eijsbouts, set to the music of the Irish band Bell X1.

In a Buddhist temple, young monks begin their meditation when the master arrives. One of them gets distracted by a sparrow, follows it outside, and embarks on a journey off the beaten path that becomes the adventure of his lifetime. A wholesome, spiritual story by director Arnaud Demuynck.

States of Matter is an experimental strata-cut animation crafted entirely from wax and paper. Inspired by Oskar Fischinger's pioneering wax experiments of the 1920s, the film is the result of director Marvin Hauck's research and creative explorations during his postgraduate studies. Complemented by a tactile soundscape, States of Matter offers a space for contemplation and personal interpretation.

The 24-year-old Olla takes a moment for herself. Her ‘cheat meal’, an instant noodle soup, awaits her on a small tray above her warm bath. Perhaps not the best place to store it, because, as she cleans herself, the noodles end up in the water… and in other places! Well-animated and relatable story about discomfort, by emerging French director Louise Labrousse.

A little girl enters a tent and emerges from it frightened, all grown up and strangely dressed as a rabbit. What follows is a complex inner journey in which a young woman tries to understand the original drama that causes her today’s suffering. A distorted universe of twisted feelings and visuals by Veronica Martiradonna.

films.t: Textile Translations, a Labour of Love
films.syn: What is lost and what is gained when pixels become fabric? Textile Translations, a Labour of Love contains a series of knitted animations exploring the translation process from pixel design to physical objects.

A Silent Voice director Naoko Yamada returns with a touching and musical portrait of three searching teenagers. If you could see your own colour, what kind of colour would it be? For Totsuko, a vivid and religious high school student, this question lingers in her mind as she navigates life at her Catholic boarding school. Gifted with the ability to see the 'colours' of others, she is captivated by Kimi, a classmate whose blue colour is unparalleled. But when Kimi drops out of school, a chance encounter at a secondhand bookstore leads the two girls to form an inpromptu band with Rui, a reserved dreamer and theremin player whose mother expects him to become a doctor. As the trio practices in an old, abandoned church, their shared musical and emotional journey lets them find freedom, joy, and love. In her first feature film for Science SARU, the anime studio known for the films of Masaaki Yuasa, director Naoko Yamada continues her lyrical exploration of youth. Reuniting with screenwriter Reiko Yoshida and composer Kensuke Ushio - with whom she made A Silent Voice and Liz and the Blue Bird - she crafts a musically inspired coming-of-age tale about the complex road to self-discovery. As in her previous work, Yamada favours a mix of realistic and impressionistic animations with gentle and detailed character designs. The Colors Within is a contemplative portrait of adolescence, finding harmony in both music and friendship. As the final performance of Totsuko, Kimi and Rui crescendos into one of the year's most heartfelt third acts, Yamada leaves us with an afterthought - one that will echo long after the last note fades: what colour lives inside your heart?

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.t: The Girl Who Lived in the Loo
films.syn: A 10-year-old girl has an obsession with… the loos! Her life, moving from one toilet to another, is calm and safe but somewhat lonely. As she grows up, she tries to make sense of this obsession while navigating her way through life. Clever, well animated short by Indian director Subarna Dash.

films.t: The Great British Bake Off: Sweet Relief!
films.syn: Step into the whimsical world of Sweet Relief with The Great British Bake Off 's first-ever fully animated campaign. It combines nostalgic 2D cell animation with playful, contemporary characters. Hosts Noel Fielding and Alison Hammond guide us from stormy skies into a vibrant land filled with cakes, jammy dodger flowers, and iconic bakes.

Seasoned storyteller Mr. P.N.K. Panicker from Kerala, India, narrates the story of the humble reptile Arana. In this charming folktale, you will uncover how Arana came to embody a distinctive and memorable character trait. A delightful short film by Indian director Adithi Krishnadas.

Have Noah and Darwin overlooked something? Could it be we are not the greatest form of evolution after all? Aboard the Lying Angel, the party of the most succesful liars is getting out of hand. Who survives the Homo Sapiens? Honouring and mocking human evolution (and its art), The Lying Angel is a political commentary about the possible demise of our species.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Victor is an ugly man with a mustache and an overcoat, but he's brilliant! With this in mind, he goes to the store to buy a bottle of Mole pipe cleaner for his wife. However, after a curious incident, he loses his memory. His only clue: a shopping list with the word 'Mole' on it. What follows is a mysterious and asburd quest for his identity, where Victor goes from the frying pan into the fire.

Chinese director Yuan Shui created this animated music video for Chris Lee’s song The Ostrich Escaped , based on a true story of an ostrich escaping a safari park and dying of exhaustion after running 20 kilometers. Various artworks were inspired by this story. Yuan Shui distilled these into animation, symbolizing the subjective projections of people onto the ostrich and playfully reflecting how an ostrich might perceive humans.

The Painting explores the 1652 portrait of Queen Mariana of Austria by Velázquez. Playing with shadow and light, the film evokes the tragic fate of Mariana, who was married to her uncle at the age of 14. Both painful and tender, this experimental work is a poem of a film: a meditation on the brutality of institutionalized incest and art’s power to capture the soul. Director Michèle Lemieux demonstrates incredible mastery of the pinscreen in this short film.

On Valentine's Day, the romantic Icaro wants to propose to his girlfriend Vanilla in their favourite restaurant in Brussels: The Golden Mussel. But the chef is hell-bent on making sure Icaro fails. Framed as a silent Technicolor film, Gerlando Infuso's award-winning short is a delightful throwback to slapstick humour and Hollywood romanticism.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Dumped waste lies around two garbage containers. An old mattress sighs, "They say I’m dirty..." As the objects share their stories, an old piece of paper begins to dance gracefully, sparking a profound, musical transformation in how the waste perceives itself. With The Refusers , Dutch director Wiep Teeuwisse delivers a playful, all-around fun short.

Overwhelmed by her family life, a woman abandons her husband and children for an afternoon in pursuit of a roe deer. Unfolding through parallel stories that intensify one another, director Delphine Priet-Mahéo bases her animations on folklore drawings that perfectly complement the clever storytelling.

As night fell, the marsh came alive with the much-awaited concert of nocturnal creatures, attended by the inhabitants of the wetland. All was well until an ardent fan could no longer contain its excitement. A lovely claymation by Indian director Suresh Eriyat.

films.t: The Shortest Relationship in the World
films.syn: This animation may depict the shortest relationship in the world. Two people enjoy each other’s company with such intensity that it would make a mayfly jealous. A colorful short film by Chinese director Xiaoxuan Han.

How does society deal with offenders, and how can harm to potential victims be prevented? The animated documentary The Virtue of Voice deals with a difficult subject matter and gives a glimpse into the minds of two people who have committed criminal offenses. A confronting work by Leticia van Neerven.

films.t: There Will Be No Other End
films.syn: This five-act social satire examines the behaviors and flaws of our society. Director Piotr Milczarek presents a cautionary tale, warning of the consequences we may face if we fail to address foolishness, apathy, and irresponsibility. With light, engaging visuals, There Will Be No Other End delivers a powerful message.

Perhaps you must be a little bit crazy to explore the loaded history of Belgium's colonial grip on the Congo through feverish meditations in animation. But in the crafty hands of acclaimed stop-motion wizards Emma De Swaef & Marc Roels, it's an idea that led to a brilliant anthology film. Set in late 19th-century Congo, This Magnificent Cake! spins five different stories following a character into the "heart of darkness". In dreamy vignettes, we see the (mis)adventures of a troubled king, a middle-aged pygmy hotel workers who frequently serves as an ash tray, a disgraced and lonely businessman on an expedition, a wandering porter, and a young army deserter. The film's title is a reference to a quote by Leopold II, who desperately wanted "a slice of the African cake". De Swaef & Roels have arguably made one of the most important political films in Belgian history. By steering clear from over historical references, they allowed themselves to infuse their mosaic with their trademark surrealism. That might come off as wholly absurd, but it actually produces something which underlines the brutal truth of colonial humiliation. The soft aesthetic - the characters are entirely crafted from felt and wool - contrasts sharply with harsh realities of the subject matter, creating a surreal experience that ultimately points out the complete pointlessness of Leopold II's greed.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.t: Totto-Chan: The Little Girl at the Window
films.syn: In 1940s Tokyo, a spirited young girl named Totto-chan attends an unconventional school. But beyond its walls, the war comes ever closer. In 1940s Tokyo, a spirited and inquisitive young girl named Totto-chan struggles to conform to the rigid education system. Expelled from her traditional school for her unconventional behaviour, she finds a new beginning at Tomoe Gakuen - a unique and progressive school led by its compassionate founder and headmaster Sosaku Kobayashi. Under his guidance, children are encouraged to explore their individual talents through creativity and joy. Yet, beyond the whimsical world of Tomoe, the grim spectre of war looms ever closer. Candy machines stand empty, and the contents of children's bento boxes grow increasingly sparse. Shinnosuke Yakuwa, in his first non-franchise anime feature, brings to life Tetsuko Kuroyanagi's beloved 1981 autobiographical memoir, capturing the delicate balance between childhood innocence and the gruesome realities of World War II. Rendered in warm, luminous colours and enriched with expressive dream sequences, Totto-chan: The Little Girl at the Window evokes the carefree charm of classic children's book illustrations. It’s an invitation to see the world through Totto-chan’s eyes. An invitation worth accepting.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: A young adult grappling with his thoughts and daily struggles learns he has autism. With the support of therapy and his friend, he strives to accept this reality. The vignettes in this short film are based on the personal experiences of director Loek Vugs. Understanding and accepting who you are was a central part of his therapy and has become the foundation of this project.

films.t: TV or The Disturbance on Forest Hill Road
films.syn: Six-year-old Diego watches too much TV and gets square eyes, causing strange phenomena to spread through the building’s screens. When officers Kim and Mike respond to a noise complaint, they find themselves caught in a disarray of blended worlds and must face off against fictional characters brought to life. Swiss director Frederic Siegel instantly immerses you in his untamed universe.
Set to music by Danny Elfman from his album Rabbit and Rogue , the award-winning short Urge follows the epic and tumultuous flight of a small ladybird.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Get ready for the most vegan and spicy animation you will see this decade. Only suitable for adult audiences who bring their sense of humor to the theatre. She is all that: A super empath, a justice warrior, and your favorite confidence queen… but then again, maybe she’s just a sausage. A tasty short film by Hungarian director Luca Tóth.

films.t: Welcome to the City of Love
films.syn: Drawing a close parallel between romantic love and the passion athletes feel for their sports, this breathtaking film for the Paris Olympic Games showcases an intense choreography. In just 60 seconds, it features 58 shots and 36 athletes. Using the universal graphic appeal of 2D animation, the film captures the human spirit of endeavor while retaining warmth and texture.

On a summer's afternoon, a kid gets involved in a car accident and ends up in a field surrounded by the rolling hills of rural Italy. There seems to be a lunch party, to which he is summoned to be late. During the meal and conversation, he tries to piece together what actually happened to him. Visually charming student work by Emma-Claire Sardoni.

What's your favorite sandwich topping? Ask Michael, and you'll definitely get sick to your stomach when you hear the answer. But Michael loves it: his own scabs! He even thinks it's so delicious that he experiments with it and has a Michelin-starred chef taste it. Bon appétit!

Going on a safari is the absolute dream holiday for middle-aged couple Linda and Troyer. Sadly enough, their wildlife experience turns into a nightmare when they get left behind. Through mixed media (combining live-action and animation), Wildebeest tells a surprisingly touching story of a couple in crisis - albeit with tons of effective gags.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Country in Focus: Belgium)

films.syn: Will You Come With Me? is a little story born in Berlin. A city that appears liberated but tends to give you a slap in the face when you get in intimate relationships. You soon discover things aren't so different from the dark days of the past, when women had to bear responsibility not only for their own actions but also for men’s, facing the consequences alone.

In this surreal animation, you follow a strange interaction between a wandering man and the mysterious creature Yapolaponky. A quiet and intriguing film about loss and grief by Japanese director Masataka Kihara.

films.t: Yet Only Here I Am Home
films.syn: How do second-generation Dutch people with a migration background view their native country? This poetic documentary explores shared memories, insecurities, and conversations revealing how being treated as the "Other" can be internalized. Through interviews, it raises the question of whether one is allowed to feel at home in the Netherlands. An intriguing graphic novel-style documentary by Dutch director Michael Hauwert.

films.t: You’ve Got a Friend in Me
films.syn: Buzz puts on a magnificent performance singing Randy Newman’s You've Got a Friend in Me . His friend Woody gets all soft-hearted about it.
Zapped is a very short, fast-paced exquisite corpse film in which a family's fight for the remote control spirals out of control.

This short animated film is inspired by the worst zoo in the world, located in Gaza, where animals that died in the war were embalmed and exhibited. The surviving animals, including a tiger named Laziz, were rescued to safe reserves. Yet, nothing has changed for the people living in Gaza. Zoo highlights the desperate situation in war-torn countries, telling a story of friendship and suffering through the eyes of a child.

Five high school students try to break free and find happiness by any means necessary: carving their bodies, pretending to be blind, reshaping their image on social media, and diving into drugs. Their intertwined journeys lead them to glimpse a ray of hope—until everything falls apart at 2:14 PM.

An innovative experimental animated film that makes moving images with a photocopy machine. Through bizarre images and a pulsing electronic musical score, the filmmakers have created a mind expanding work that will long remain in your memory.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: The ocean is paradise for Fran the shrimp. Her deadly claws take whatever they desire. For the blind fish Milva however, it’s a daily fight to survive. Fran thinks she’s beautiful and wants her to see the ocean in the same way. Can they overcome their differences? A darkly humorous love story by Bára Anna Stejskalová.

This year’s spring, Kaboom’s selection celebrates the eternal renaissance of life with a Czech animation. An enchanting story where human actions contrast with the deep fatality of pagan customs. Guiding us through this short are logs of wood and death’s head crow puppets, combined with real-life settings.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Luna, the granddaughter, helps her grandmother bury her dog. But what happens when you’re dead and buried underground? Her grandmother evades the question, so Luna is tempted to see for herself what happens below. A colorful short film exploring the tension between childish innocence and death.
In a restaurant in China, waiters try to swat flies while a number of diners eat their food.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: When the hedgehog is about to go into hibernation, he notices that one of his spines is missing. Soon he discovers it’s stuck… in the dog’s behind! He tries to get the prickle back as quickly as possible, but the dog isn’t easy to catch.

One night, a little boy goes to bed. But instead of falling asleep, he starts thinking all kinds of thoughts. Dangerous thoughts. Admirable thoughts. Questionable thoughts. Beautiful thoughts… until a very serious thought strikes him. If Earth is just a tiny marble floating in space, and he is only one child among many living on this marble, what does his existence matter in the grand scheme of things?

A Story of Unfolding Wings is a short abstract stop-motion film composed of colorful woven frames. By weaving the frames for the film on a handloom, Stellata Koppe created a sensitive travelogue about her transition, in which the violin sound of Eefje Habraken is indispensable.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.t: A Year Along the Abandoned Road
films.syn: Between the cold houses of the village of Børfjord, where people only show up during a short and hectic summer season, we follow the cycles of nature going as they have always done, independently of what people might do.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: An exploration of the connections between sex, love and technology. A woman connects to the Internet. She not only embraces technology but surrenders to it entirely as she sends her entire body and soul to her electronic lover. In this world of Pandora's boxes, sexual desire and dehumanizing machines intertwine till they're finally and brutally disconnected.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: In Acid City , all climate fears seem to have come true. This fictional documentary explores an overheated city floating on toxic water. Despite the harsh conditions, a dynamic society persists, doing everything it can to survive. Drawing on sound recordings from the streets of New York, the animated film imagines a future in which humanity endures even in the most extreme circumstances.

The always stunning slit-scan animation (motion control) technique known from famous Title Sequences like 2001, SUPERMAN, STAR TREK, "Dr. Who" and others was used here to create transitions between a Lion and the TROS logo as an Ident of Station Call. Many combinations were created and broadcast, this one however never made it to the Master Control Room as it was labeled "Rejected"!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: The creative team at Oh Yeah Woq paired with the beautiful music of All India Radio to bring you Rippled . Painstakingly animated frame by frame, the piece is all shot in camera, by real people, in the real world, using long exposure techniques.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Every day, Vladimir, an elderly Beirut resident, reads the obituary and attends funerals, mourning his wife, his home, and a decaying city. Rituals, denial, and a brief encounter with a young girl guide him toward acceptance. In the end, he faces not only personal loss, but the disappearance of the world he once knew.

First came Hiroshi Sakurazaka’s ‘light novel’ in 2004. Ten years later, we saw adaptations as manga, American graphic novel, and the Hollywood blockbuster Edge of Tomorrow . And now, an anime directed by Kenichiro Akimoto. Each time, the story starts over, but slightly different. Which, funnily enough, is exactly the premise of All You Need Is Kill. In its Groundhog Day (1993) meets video game concept, each time you die, your day starts over, you just know a little bit more about what’s coming (something about an alien invader and the total annihilation of Earth). The two most significant changes made by Akimoto and his team are that the main characters aren’t military anymore, but civilian, and that the lead role has shifted from Keiji to Rita. With as an additional story layer the fact that Rita – although the word isn’t explicitly mentioned – is depressed. Which neatly fits the pattern of each day feeling the same, and having no interest at all in tomorrow. Which effectively turns All You Need Is Kill – with all its clearly choreographed fight scenes and the angular, sketchy design for which Studio 4°C is known – into a series of therapy sessions (after all, therapy also requires endless repetition for even minor progress): unless Rita wants to keep dying for the rest of her life (‘Live. Die. Repeat’ was Edge of Tomorrow ’s concise slogan), she has no choice but to take an interest in every single detail of today in an attempt to finally make it to tomorrow.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: One moment you’re playing in the streets of Guinea; next, you’re a child soldier. On his way to his aunt in Liberia, twelve-year-old orphan Birahima is arrested by warlords, armed, drugged, and sent out on raids. An unsettling, moving, occasionally joyful, and extensively researched adaptation of a renowned Ivorian novel.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Ever thought that not having a conscience must be nice? After seeing Amarelo Banana , you’ll think again. Another sleepless night brings a man across a strange community living in his building.
