To break the boredom, he decides to pay them a visit, but leaving their jungle feverish rooms is not as easy as he imagined.

Did you know you can grow a new pineapple from the top of a pineapple—again and again, forever? Ananasi follows three animal friends who do exactly this, dancing as they go. A bright and colorful reflection on the infinity of nature, the film is a hand-drawn musical short by Anna Bawa, inspired by her lifelong curiosity about non-human life.

A grizzly moves effortlessly through a vast landscape, as others flee from an unseen threat. Meanwhile, a human, driven by his own instincts, navigates the same terrain. Both apex predators dominate the top of the food chain, but their worlds collide when they cross paths.
Say hello to Colin, a grumpy cuckoo with big opinions and even bigger shoes. For Telstra’s App O’Clock campaign, Nexus Studios with +61 and Bear Meets Eagle On Fire created playful, self-aware spots.

Afraid of ghosts? Don’t be—because in Arguments in Favor of Love , you’ll discover that they aren’t so different from us after all. Though they inhabit a desolate world of fire and floods, they engage in heated debates about genetic testing, grief, and lost love. Director Gabriel Abrantes blends absurd twists with sharp insights into contemporary social dynamics and relationships.

Art, a 20-something year old student living in a crappy apartment, is woken up in the middle of the night by the sound of his roommate loudly playing videogames. After a long argument, Art finally manages to get his roommate to shut off the game. However, getting a full night’s sleep might still prove more difficult than expected.

In the 1990s, 8-year-old Agata leaves Poland for Belgium to live with her mother. Anxious about her journey, she writes a letter to her father, but her pencil falls and is lost on the bus. Crawling between seats to retrieve it, she plunges into a fantastic world of strange half-human, half-animal passengers, turning the reality of migration into an initiatory experience through her eyes.

A lost boy wanders aimlessly along a forest road until he finds a squirrel that has been run over. He then decides to enter the forest, where that same squirrel appears to have risen from the dead. What follows is a journey through a nightmarish world ruled by unnatural materials.
Leader in three sections using cut-out animation to reveal the program's title.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Rotoscoped and silhouetted feet wearing different footwear are the stars in this leader for a home & gardening DIY programme.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: In a barren cell, two dogs endure the silence—one restless, the other distracted. A sudden figure at the door upends the balance, triggering a surreal transformation that blurs the line between animal and the unknown. When the door opens, only one leaves; the other is left in shock.

films.t: Basketball Explorer Presents: The Shot Doctor
films.syn: In an ’80s-style self-help video, minor regional basketball player “Pissy” Pete Denny explains how to shoot the perfect jump shot while struggling with the demons that haunt him. “F*CK!” Why is he called Pissy Pete again?

The lonely teenager Yo hurls tomatoes in frustration and accidentally hits Lydia, an elderly woman with a disability. Rushing to her aid, he soon discovers that Lydia is not as helpless as she seems. Gradually, the line between perpetrator and victim blurs.

Beelong is an animated short about a happy little bee whose meadow is turned into a housing estate. He must find a new home and learn to live in a changing world. The film comforts young children, showing that even when things change, happiness can be found again.
Bergamot , also translated as 'Buddha's hand', explores a binary mother-daughter relationship as it shifts as it grows.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Ordinary life repeats itself every day. The succession of repeated moments is never the same, and everything changes. Only the feeling of the body touching something—something that exists solely in this present reality—can be recognized as “now.” That moment is lovely.

Welcome to a world of ever-growing muscles. Better Man explores the phenomenon of bodybuilding and the relationship fitness-oriented men have with their bodies. Through interviews, the film follows three men who use exercise to cope with inner traumas that have often led to low self-esteem.

films.t: Biting the Hand That Feeds You
films.syn: Biting the Hand That Feeds You is a sharp and engaging portrait of the lives of female animators in the industry. When the protagonist, Chantal, gets the chance to enter a competition—this time ticking all the boxes as a female director—she is ready to dive in. But working on a project is not that easy when family life tries to take over.

This is the opening teaser animation for the 2025 BLON Animation and Games Festival, which was held in Klaipeda and Palanga, Lithuania. The animation was shown at the beginning of each screening and on Lithuanian television. The characters featured in the teaser were also incorporated into the festival's overall branding, which included posters, banners, bags, and an award trophy.
Animated on location at a beach, in the snow, and underwater, this stop-motion short details a transoceanic conversation between two characters via objects in a bottle.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Boundaries explores how individuals and communities relate to one another. How firm are the lines we draw between us? And what does a boundary say about your identity? These relevant questions are posed by various figures within a series of artistic, abstract, and above all visually stunning spaces. A unique work by director Seun Yee.

Journalist and activist Hoi Yi fights against the growing global rise of surveillance and censorship while suppressing his queer identity from his family. The personal repression he faces is reflected in his commitment to the freedom of others. Breaking Walls is a poignant documentary that throws you into the protagonist’s dilemmas from the first scene.

Young Candice is bullied by the other children in the village. They really shouldn’t have done that… She has, after all, brought a number of animal friends back from the dead, who are more than happy to scare the bullies out of their wits.
Cartoon Lovers features the classic popular cartoons. Including Ed, Edd, Eddy and Rick & Morty.

The story revolves around the peculiar relationship between a princess, a castle, and the Bug King. Through a fragmented narrative style, the princess's yearning ambition for her past kingdom is personified, transforming into the Bug King, a being of only faint power. He becomes a surrogate for the princess in reviving the kingdom, creating an imagined fantasy within a forest of strange creatures.
Ceci n'est pas un Spectacle is a knitted animation inspired by downtown Montreal, whilst hinting at the absurdity of ‘representation’ in arts and the critical limits of public realm projection.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Sam, a grumpy raccoon, is stuck sharing a cell with Bob, a sweet but dim manatee. In their chaotic, clumsy jailbreak, Sam’s hardened edges soften as Bob’s loyalty shines. Will they escape? Maybe. But together, they’ve already cracked something bigger: trust.

Chalisa is a short stop-motion musical that explores the power, dedication, and wisdom of the Hindu deity Hanuman while celebrating his extraordinary life. The film brings the lines of the "Chalis (40) Chaupais," written by the esteemed poet Tulsidas, to life through playful yet meaningful clay visuals.
Procedurally animated embroidery in a 120 seconds loop.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Office worker Stephan is accosted by the smitten mermaid princess ChaO who insists he loves her too. In an intricately detailed near-future Shanghai, they must navigate the urban masses, the politics between humans and merfolk, and their own romcom romance. Visually stunning Studio4ºC production won the Jury Award in Annecy.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Amusing story of an attempted seduction like no other. Made in pixilation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: While working alone at a remote gas station, Mia is visited by her estranged boyfriend, Damon. After a tense encounter, Damon reveals himself to be a monster. Literally. Will she manage to tear herself away from his claws? A chilling piece of horror by Tim Smink.
Characters made entirely from clothes, dance and perform in celebration to a 1940s jazz track.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: A tiny little fish explores the vast underwater world. Because of his size, he is sometimes overlooked by his bigger friends. But maybe that’s exactly what gives him a special, curious way of seeing the world.
High school lab partners Marshall and Frances uncover a conspiracy by big pharma and the government to suppress a rare mushroom that could cure all diseases.

films.t: Common Side Effects S01E02: Lakeshore Limited
films.syn: Marshall is on the run, trying to flee New York; Frances confides to her boss, Rick, about the mushroom; Rick sends her to Marshall's farm to get more, but the situation gets out of hand.
Marshall seeks advice from his old mentor, Hildy. Copano and Harrington are drawn further into the mystery of the mushrooms obtained at the raid.

Marshall buys a plot of land near a chemical waste site with a plan to grow more mushrooms; Frances rushes home from Europe after a huge development; Copano and Harrington investigate a connection between Marshall and Frances.
Marshall, Frances, and their crazy neighbors deal with the aftermath of a dangerous incident.

films.t: Common Side Effects S01E06: In the System
films.syn: Marshall arrives in jail and learns that some very important people refuse to let him out, while danger lurks around every corner; Frances makes a fateful decision; Copano and Harrington pick up the pieces.

Marshall is rescued by another inmate, but now Marshall owes him a favor; desperate to get out of prison, he works on a risky plan when he runs into a surprising ally; Frances grapples with a life-changing event.

films.t: Common Side Effects S01E08: Amelia & Wyatt
films.syn: After being declared dead, Marshall Cuso and Amelia must resolve unfinished business by staying hidden. Francis deals with his supposed loss while facing unexpected changes in the development of Reutical mushrooms.

films.t: Common Side Effects S01E09: Cliff’s Edge
films.syn: Marshall discovers what Hildy has been up to, but obstacles remain. Copano and Harrington zero in on Marshall's location.
The FBI/DEA raid the compound, resulting in awful consequences. The fate of the mushroom is decided.

The peaceful life of a hardworking farmer and his beloved cow is upended by an alien abduction. What starts as a calm day spirals into a wild ride of surreal transformations and chaotic mutations. Blending humor and absurdity, the film celebrates how even the most outlandish circumstances can deepen the bond between two unlikely souls.

films.t: Cultivation, Harvesting and Dispersal of Thorns
films.syn: Cultivation, harvesting and dispersal of thorns is a beautifully animated, poetic and minimalist film about planting, patience, and harvest. Told with tender precision, it shows how a sudden storm wrecks a meticulously planned orchestration.

Young Freya loves her dad, even though he doesn’t always love her back. As she grows up, she develops a passion for climbing, but her father disapproves. His harsh words weigh on her until they take over her life. Through self-acceptance and hard work, she learns to break free from his opinion. Dad Said is gripping story about how parental influence can shape one’s growth.

The heroes of this epic interplanetary space adventure are… four dandelion seeds! Japanese director Momoko Seto spent years refining her exceptional technique, combining CGI characters with slowed-down and sped-up footage of real-life nature. No humans, no words – like a flora version of Flow . Paul Grimault Award, Annecy; Fipresci Award, Cannes. Don’t make a dash for the lobby just yet! Stick around after the credits for a 15-minute brain-tickle with our guest philosopher and the creative visionaries from Asian Movie Nights. We’re bridging the gap between popcorn cinema and deep theory to unpack the film’s biggest "wait, what?" moments. Whether you’re here for the aesthetics or a minor existential crisis, this quick-fire Q&A is the perfect digestive for the soul. Conversation supported by Het Filmgesprek.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.t: De Lekkerste Recepten met 1 Klik in Huis
films.syn: Commercial for Dutch grocery delivery service Picnic.
When his world turns upside down, Jos, who lives with his wheelchair-bound mother, struggles to maintain his daily routine.

Thinking of his children’s future, Félix Dufour-Laperrière ( Archipelago , 2021) experienced profound doubt and fear. Thus he created Death Does Not Exist , an urgent film in times of growing global inequality, social injustice and rising authoritarianism. What to do, when you see all that happening around you? Hélène’s friends argue that a violent attack on an ultra-rich family could provide the required revolutionary spark. Although she has her doubts, she nevertheless takes part in the armed raid. At the moment of truth, however, she freezes when an elderly woman in a wheelchair looks her straight in the eye. This costs her friend Marc his life, in a gruesome way. Hélène turns around and flees into the forest. She is followed there by her revolutionary comrade Manon. Or maybe by her ghost; from the moment they enter the forest, the boundary between reality and magical imagination becomes blurred (not unlike in Stalker – one of Dufour-Laperrière ’s favourite films). Colours, visions and animals all represent Hélène’s inner turmoil, in a spellbinding mix of tranquil scenes and hallucinatory (and hand-drawn) transformations. This provocative film, with its subtly mesmerising soundtrack and its monochrome characters often blending into their surroundings, gradually abandons all certainties, until only one, extremely pressing moral dilemma remains: the impossible choice between violence and inaction in the face of a dangerously unhinged capitalism. Will you fight? Or rather flee? Won Best Feature Film at the Ottawa International Animation Festival. Don’t make a dash for the lobby just yet! On Saturday 14 March stick around after the credits for a 15-minute brain-tickle with our guest Rolf Deen. We’re bridging the gap between popcorn cinema and deep theory to unpack the film’s biggest “wait, what?” moments. Whether you’re here for the aesthetics or a minor existential crisis, this quick-fi re Q&A is the perfect digestive for the soul. Conversation supported by Het Filmgesprek.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Miserable mouse Arnold has the creeping ‘ Black Mirror meets The Truman Show ’ suspicion that his whole world is a decorado – a set. With touches of Unicorn Wars ’ extreme violence, Vázquez adapted his own darkly humorous comic (2010) and short (2017) into a much more existential drama.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.t: Diverse Materialen tot het Vervaardigen van een Leader
films.syn: A unique look into some of the original footage filmed on a miniature stage and outdoor in Paris and Amsterdam plus the final result where these shots are composited into the station call outro that would conclude an evening of TROS (Televisie & Radio Omroep Stichting) programming.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Marta returns to Portugal after loneliness forces her to leave London. When she goes to see her grandfather, she hears the mournful cries of a broken soul. She discovers it’s an abandoned dog who has been keeping the neighborhood awake day and night since his owners died. Marta decides to investigate—and soon finds herself caught up in an extraordinary adventure.

In a world that demands community participation, individual desires inevitably collide. A group of neighbours, each absorbed in their own goals, must learn to communicate and consider one another. But when small, everyday actions trigger unexpected consequences, they are forced into interactions that challenge their independence.
The hen is supposed to lay eggs, just like all the other chickens. But when she sees the swallows soaring through the sky, a new dream awakens inside her: she wants to fly!

A sauerkraut is lonely and bored out of its mind. Until a duck flies by. In its sausage-filled head, they instantly become friends for life. But the duck mainly sees the sauerkraut as a tasty snack. Duck & Sauerkraut is a recipe for madness: a story about the impossible love between a meal and a quacker.
It's a perfectly normal day in the park. The sun is shining, and everything is as it should be… until someone decides to feed the ducks.

With an unacknowledged mental disorder, Adela seeks answers in popular rituals. She feels something is watching and harming her, and only religion seems to understand her. During a visit to a healer, she confesses the disturbing origin of her suffering. Illustrator and comic book author Bea Lema showcases her stunning techniques and compositions in her debut short film El cuerpo de Cristo .

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: White Canadian Seth wants to record the stories of his Indigenous half-brother Pete for this oral history animated documentary. But that’s not easy, with Pete’s seven children and twelve dogs running around. It turns into a cartoonish, colourful, cosy chaos – without ignoring the mistreatment of First Nations by Canadian authorities.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Error: Connection Lost is an autobiographical story that portrays the quiet, disorienting experience of a child shaped by migration’s instability. Centered on a brother and sister growing up in Ukraine in the early 2000s, the film follows their move to the Netherlands and the way they eventually drift apart.

In this cel animation, painted, formless figures haunt recent photographs of empty public spaces, expressing the helpless, frantic energy of our time. They are displaced from their locations as their environments dissolve and their printed record evaporates.
Left alone at home by their owner, Greg, an anxious Persian cat, confronts his existential dread on a journey toward spiritual enlightenment.

Extinction follows a woman who observes everything that is wrong in the world. She is shocked by how humanity is divided over our differences, leading to the neglect and destruction of our planet. Director Lucy McGonigal hits a nerve, showing how people often ignore these issues and carry on with their lives. The film encourages us to set aside our differences and work together to gradually restore Earth.

Two friends, lovers, soulmates, a pair of two, searching and ultimately finding each other. This pair traveling between worlds and changing forms, expressed through 15 styles of animation, by 15 animators from across the world.
In a dreamy, pink world, three little birds get ready for their very first flight! Lifted by a symphony of friendly frogs, they embark on grand adventures.
A quiet day at sea is disrupted when the catch turns out to be a neurotic, overthinking fish. A witty short by Copenhagen-based director Tobias Rud, reflecting on insecurity in modern times.

This animated short reimagines the story of Laika, the first dog in space, giving her the adventure she deserved. In a surreal, dreamlike adventure, she runs, jumps, and dances through the solar system, traveling ever closer to the sun. Short, colorful, and very sweet tribute by Nina Fock.
As Anna wanders through the snow, she meets an unexpected playmate.

As Dev drives home from a mysterious, aging nuclear facility, he becomes stranded at an isolated emu farm run by old mystic lesbians. Suspicious of their intentions, Dev fears they will sacrifice him at the local stone circle. A delightfully twisted folk-horror comedy by Lizzie Watts.

Who doesn't love Elizabeth Hobbs' cute yet trippy animations! Using an Underwood 315 typewriter, this film is a celebration of Amy Johnson's journey. Johnson worked as a typist for a firm of solicitors before her record-breaking solo flight from London to Australia in 1930. Now, we feel bad typing.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Get ready for a hell of a train ride. Literally! Director Jocelyn Charles introduces Ariel and Paul, who pass the time on their journey by sketching their worst fears. When a fellow passenger walks by, they realize she looks exactly like one of their drawings. From that moment on, their worst fears start crawling out of the sketchbook. God is Shy is a neck-grabbing debut that drags you into the darkest places. As one of our reviewers put it: “I love it when a film makes me wonder what the fuck possessed the people who made it. Extraordinary.”

In de wieg van de Industriële Revolutie wenden arbeiders zich tot de natuur om te herstellen van de zware omstandigheden in de fabrieken. De handgemaakte film Green Lung reflecteert op de geschiedenis van Derby Arboretum, het eerste openbare park van Groot-Brittannië, geopend in 1840 door fabrikant Joseph Strutt.
Ever wondered what happens when you swallow chewing gum? Not much—it just sits in your stomach for seven years. The kids in Gummy Mummy are about to find out for themselves.

We all carry obscure thoughts deep within us. While much time and energy can be spent keeping these emotions confined, this film does the opposite. Raw, instinctive sketches are transformed into surreal animated loops, turning agony into movement and memory into visual rhythm. A reminder to keep moving forward while confronting the strange inner creatures that live inside us.

Mother Earth is sick, and her body will fight the pests. Harmonies explores humanity’s disconnection from nature and our inevitable self-destruction. This graduation film combines hand-painted textures, 2D animation, and poetry by Doortje Schoonbrood.

A true collector’s item, Have to Have is a quirky animated short about obsession and our instinct to hoard. In a parallel between a caveman and a modern collector, both are on the hunt for the centerpiece of their collection. In the heat of battle, their worlds begin to merge.

How do you pack your bag when you go on a trip? Probably not with the same patience as the protagonist in this short. In calm, meticulous detail, director Naohiro Zama brings his favourite hobby to life. Consider your meditation for the day done. Bold student work!

Fake it 'til you make it: when computer animation was still in it's infancy and was totally unaffordable for the animators creating leaders for Dutch TV, one could at least make it look like it came out of a computer - and perhaps computer drawings aided the analog hand-crafted animation of this leader.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: In one of Aesop’s fables, a crow is searching for water. It spies a pitcher— but the water inside is beyond its reach. So, the crow begins dropping in pebbles. One-by-one, they displace the water, and the crow quenches its thirst. This is just one of many fascinating displays of intelligence from corvids. Ted-Ed digs into what makes this bold, brainy family of songbirds so smart.
A truly humanistic act of skateboarding.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: How many tiny creatures does it take to turn someone into bones? Left for dead in the woods, a girl is devoured by chatty spirits.

Lea is searching for a subject for a documentary film. When she believes she has finally caught her prey, the roles reverse and the hunter becomes the hunted. Director Lea Favre delivers a cold, electric shock to the spine in this striking, confrontational student film.

Location: Kanaal40, a bar located in Amsterdam’s Warmoesstraat. Working behind the bar, the protagonist gets in touch with Jay, the security guard. At the threshold of the club, he found a sense of security: a space to express themselves and explore who they want to be. I Can See Jay There is a documentary about identity and belonging, grounded in friendship.

One day, Guy the bird is running through the forest when he stumbles over a mysterious little box. What is this strange object? And what can it do? Together with his forest friends, he sets out to investigate.
When six-year-old Otto writes his very first story, words come to life as images. As he reads aloud, his imaginative world unfolds in an animation lovingly created by his mother.

April 6, 1994. A day like any other turns into an apocalypse for the Rwandan people. In Kigali, young parents Valentine and Jean-Claude face the threat of mass destruction. With the help of several people, they repeatedly attempt to escape their region, hoping to survive the worst. Ibuka, Justice unfolds at a slow and quiet pace, offering an almost dream-like portrayal of a family’s courage and strength in dark times.
A collection of American animator Jane Aaron's early experiments combining live-action and animation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: On a foggy morning, a simple conversation between two anglers sparks collective panic. In the Mist examines mob psychology in ambiguous situations, showing how individuals distort events and spread this distortion through the group. Even when confronted with facts, the group ignores reality, merging illusion with what actually happens.

Among the scattered pebbles, a woman sits carefully in an abandoned theater. In this hall of silence and decay, the story of In the Sand unfolds, inspired by the work of Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish. With minimalist imagery and music, the film reflects on erasure, turning away from suffering, and the responsibility that artists carry.

During a stormy night, our familiar reality becomes entangled with another dimension. Two timelines collide, leading to a fatal outcome. This dark, unsettling stop-motion thriller by Patrick Raats will literally make you grind your teeth.
A short documentary film on the radical power of self-affirmation that clothes offer us.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: What would you do if you came across a video that defies the laws of physics, yet still somehow feels convincing? I'm Looking for Mr. Laser is a short story about following in the footsteps of someone who may or may not exist, mapping the maze of imagination and illusion created by this mysterious figure.

Insight into the filmmaker's stay in hospital, where she repeatedly experiences absurd, funny moments between pain, homesickness and disgust of her own body. Meanwhile, she tries to come to terms with the hospital's own procedures and hierarchies. An emotional trip through the long underground corridors of the hospital with lots of small talk and tubes.

When hoping to shape their future home in a furniture store, Jeanne and Jean Jean find themselves in a heated debate. Will they choose a minimalist, industrial style, or go for something bohemian and maximalist? After a much-needed bathroom break, Jean Jean proposes a compromise. Jeanne, however, becomes distracted by the unsettling ballet of the other couples in the store and leaves without even listening. A fun and highly relatable short film by Thanis Martin.
Urban folklore explored through the female gaze using cut-out and sand animation.

Frankie, a lonely factory worker, believes he’s about to die with no one to say goodbye to. But on his way to the stars, he accidentally becomes a planet, and life erupts across his surface—including creatures that look just like him. For the first time, he isn’t alone. Yet his love for his new friends is put to the test when he realizes they could destroy all life on Planet Frankie. A bloody bizarre short by Belgian director Levi Stoops.

Simple yet very effective, this 3D title extraction animated in 2D in what seems to be a cut-out technique. It makes one think "how did they animate this?". Bumpers with dates in the short running TV programme used the same typography but where not animated.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: While Oscar struggles to choose between staying with his toys or following his best friend after girls, a sudden act of terrorism forces him to leave his hometown and grow up abruptly. Four decades later, during the COVID-19 crisis, he returns in search of shelter and food, haunted by memories of his past.

Lark in A Sky Shop is a music video based on Jacob Collier’s eponymous song. It explores the depth of tension within one’s soul and life, stretched between light and darkness, day and night, oppression and freedom, and the turbulent navigation through it all. It’s about being pressed, found, and brought into a spacious place. It’s a dialogue, a confrontation, a story full of twists and turns, which ultimately suggests the possibility of discovering a source of life, freedom, and everlasting love.

Living a lonely life of isolation, a girl dreams of luxury and beauty. She fantasises about possessing the looks of her celebrity idol and and winning the heart of her unrequited love, an oblivious worker at her local takeaway. In a surreal, dreamlike turn of events, featuring a moth-like spirit, she discovers that perhaps she should have been more careful what she wished for

In Soviet-occupied Lithuania, two young pioneers are promoted to serve on the legendary 'Red Wall.' But as they journey through a decaying industrial nightmare, they uncover a horrifying truth: the Wall is built from living flesh. Faced with eternal torment, they make a desperate bid for freedom.

A snow bunting and a raven have a very special dance! The raven has taken the mother bunting’s song from her little chick, and now they swirl and swoop through the sky in a magical chase. Their movements twist and turn like a flock of birds in flight, changing shapes and colors, creating a dazzling, ever-shifting dance full of surprises and wonder.

The Loading Nouns come to East London for a delirious dance session in this ingenious film mixing 2D animation of cutout paper characters shot in stop-motion in real-life environments captured in timelapse. The result is intoxicating and leaves you wanting to dance!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Ella works at the lost-and-found desk of a busy train station, collecting abandoned belongings and storing them in her booth. At first glance, they look like a random mix of books, wallets, and other trinkets. But what no one knows is that Ella is creating something extraordinary from these lost objects. In a world driven by hurry and efficiency, is anyone still willing to pause for a moment of wonder?
Erotic body horror blurring the lines between reality and art through hand-drawn animation and rotoscoping.

Very playful and inventive leaders and bumpers were created for a documentary about match sticks ("Lucifers") using a mix of live action recording (sometimes played back in reverse), clever dissolves and stop-motion animation.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Waken in the middle of the night by a giant rock in its bed sheet, a sleeper starts to wander in the maze he lives into.
In a world controlled and timed by light, an ordinary man has a plan that could change the natural order of things.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Two disabled squeaky toys escape from the factory and find themselves lost and alone in an urban world full of over-sized humans. It’s new, strange and a little daunting.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Mamiko catches her boyfriend cheating. That night, she stress-eats and gets a stomach ache. But in a bizarre twist, her toilet mishap ends up killing her cheating boyfriend instead of her.
Cut-out and drawn animation at its scariest in this Dr. Caligariesque anti-militaristic short.

Ten-year-old Max moves with his father into an apartment that a real estate agent would call a “property with potential.” But strange things start happening: unidentifiable noises, unusually irritable neighbors, and a hermetically sealed room on the top floor. Max begins to investigate and gradually gets closer to a deeply unsettling secret.

When he was away from home, Michel Gondry used to create cute animated shorts for his young daughter Maya. Her imagination perfectly fitted his absurdism: she came up with titles, which he turned into grand adventures in his distinctive, handcrafted cut-out style. With Maya always their hero – whether cop or mermaid.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: What exactly is ADHD? And what are its characteristics and effects? A short animated film with several chapters addresses all these questions.

films.t: Meow Meow Meow Meow the Meowsical
films.syn: Actor by day, magical girl by night! Kat lands the role of a lifetime voicing her favorite character, Tala, but soon faces her greatest foe: inexperience. A meowful tribute to the dubbing industry, by Velocity Jade De Lumen.

Merrimundi is a cosmic dystopian sing-along—an ecstatic transmission from a sentient machine of the future, attempting to speak to us in our crumbling tongue. The film unfolds as a surreal symphony, where singing cherubs dissolve into psychedelic decay: a mad theatre of fading puppets, karaoke, and golden relicts.

Another very basic animated leader for a TV course on math & measurements. Taking a closer look shows this origami style measuring tape written title sequence was animated very precisely with great care.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.t: Mind The World | Pune Design Festival 2025
films.syn: What happens when the world has had enough? When the scars of human greed, negligence, and mindless invention push nature to the brink—how long before it retaliates? This year, we partnered once again with Pune Design Festival to craft their signature film, bringing the 2025 theme—Mind The World—to life. Through the metaphor of a tormented bull, we witness a planet pushed past its limits, no longer enduring but fighting back. A world we tamed, controlled, and exploited finally turns—reminding us that nature is not an infinite resource, nor an idle spectator. As designers, we hold the power to reshape this narrative. To move beyond fueling industries that drive destruction and instead become the architects of change. Because when the world fights back, there’s no escape—only reckoning. Watch. Reflect. And most importantly, Mind The World.

A nonfiction reflection on being out of the closet. As a queer person of color, it's taken me a long time to be as comfortable as I am through navigating forms of intimacy, gender, and self worth. It doesn't always get better, but you're beautiful however you decide to present, including the choice of garments you decide to wear.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: A unique preview of the yet to be released third part of the Mononoke the Movie series: The Curse of the Serpent.

films.t: Mononoke the Movie – The Phantom in the Rain
films.syn: Wildly designed, borderline psychedelic psycho horror drama is the first in a trilogy, following the 2007 Mononoke series. Once again, a mysterious ‘Medicine Seller’ is fighting mononoke : spirits formed from human grudges haunting the Edo Castle harem, where young concubines Asa and Kame are discovering the court intrigues and each other.

films.t: Mononoke the Movie: Chapter II – The Ashes of Rage
films.syn: When another mononoke haunts Edo Castle’s women’s quarters, the ‘Medicine Seller’ once more attempts to determine the vengeful spirit’s “shape, truth and reason”. Hallucinatory supernatural thriller revolves around the value of a potential heir to the throne, both to the pregnant woman herself and to the bitter power struggles of feudal Japan.

Superstar Mr. Sun is idolized by day, but by night, he mostly admires himself. Until one day, a lock of hair comes loose while he's running his hand through his golden locks. Is he going bald?! Frightened, he faints and drifts through the universe, searching for a solution. Confused and angry, Mr. Sun is encouraged by Miss Universe to accept the natural cycle of life and its inherent decay. A vibrant cosmic journey by Souffien Melad.

Piet, an elderly man in a nursing home, gets restricted in his actions when he realizes he is suddenly turning into a bird. Even though he is still accepted within the group, Piet feels it is time to join a new flock. An enchanting, internationally acclaimed stop-motion film from Janneke Swinkels and Tim Frijsinger.

My Good Boy follows a day in the life of a woman busy caring for her obese dog. Her affectionate attention is suddenly interrupted by the arrival of her partner, whose need for her attention disrupts the cozy atmosphere of the house. A witty and colorful short by Sara Priorelli.
Grace Lee, an overworked mother in Singapore, collapses at work and is admitted to the hospital, where she unexpectedly finds freedom as a patient.

The most successful Chinese 2D animation ever confirms the growing strength of the national animation industry. This comical adventure of four yaoguai (animals with human capabilities and questionable morality), who impersonate the heroes from the classic novel Journey to the West , offers both contemporary social criticism and classical Chinese painting techniques.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Feature Films in Competition)

films.syn: Noelle is decorating her Christmas tree when there’s a knock at the window. It’s a cat. Outside it’s snowing and freezing cold, but Noelle’s dad is allergic to cat hair. To help, Noelle invites the cat to take shelter in the barn. Soon a dog, a hen, a goat, and a donkey knock at the window too. Noelle sends them all to the barn — until her dad has to go out and get his car…

The NOS logo (Nederlandse Omroep Stichting, a Dutch broadcaster responsable for the news, sports and big events) was designed by Johan Volkerijk and in use for 36 years. A mesmerizing Station Call with a fitting electronic soundtrack that makes one think "how did they animate this?"

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Teenagers reclaim public spaces as their playground—until their joy collides with the vision of an angry capitalist. Through his power, the spaces are transformed, shifting from places of freedom into a manufactured “paradise.”

films.t: Once Upon a Time in Dragonville
films.syn: Samson is a dragon who’s often bullied by the other residents of Dragonville. One day, he has to venture into Humanville, where he meets Simon, a kind little boy who helps him through all the tricky situations. Together, they discover a whole new world—and the joy of friendship.

films.t: Out of the Inkwell: Invisible Ink
films.syn: Part of the popular series Out of the Inkwell. Max Fleischer draws the clown, who tricks him with invisible ink.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: A spinning globe and contra-spinning superimposed titles with a zoom synced to the tune are all that's needed to create this effective leader.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Paper Trail is a high-speed study of a person’s life, seen only through pieces of paper. Director Don Hertzfeldt developed new animation techniques to create the film’s unique look and pace.

Welcome to a place where houses are full of holes, tomatoes are ticking time bombs, and snails wander the streets in search of refuge. In Paradaïz , Sarajevo-based artist Matea Radic uses absurdist animation, archival footage, and fleeting memories from his own childhood to explore the deeper meaning of home.

A woman adapts to a changing body and redefines her femininity, discovering the strength to finally accept herself. Through beautiful textures and colors, several women share their unique yet universal experiences of menopause in this stop-motion documentary, offering a compassionate and positive reflection on this natural transition.

In a drought-stricken world in the aftermath of war, innkeepers Pembe and Eflatun shelter stranded refugee women and children. As the newcomers settle in, secrets emerge about how the couple has managed this inn, once a prison. A beautiful sand-animated short film by Alix Bortoli and Dal Park.

The last remaining hair at the front of a man’s thinning hairline decides to quit and explore the world beyond the scalp. He is drawn into a darkly comic showdown with the scalp’s desperate head of HR, who believes this single resignation will trigger total follicular collapse and the end of everything he has worked for.

"If it keeps starting over, it must be forever," says the white moth. But a gentle whisper greets each dawn: "One day, all days will be gone." Blending the aesthetics of vector graphics and screen-display technology with the human condition, Ploo is a profound meditation on the fragility of life.

Pol and her friends are hunting for treasure when they discover a mysterious cave filled with sparkling fireflies and a mushroom with countless dots. While counting, they realize they forgot Lou! Rushing back, they hear a scary sound and think it’s a monster. Sticking together, they hide as a bush—and discover it’s not a monster at all, but Lou, snoring in the dark.
Skip announces that he has new water skis and races on a long rope behind Bamboom.
A polar bear is very bored with various marine animals in the deep blue sea. The film follows the ancient tradition of "Caricatures of Frolicking animals" in a scroll painting-style.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: The name you are given at birth can shape your destiny. Marciano knows this well—he only wants a friend to sing with. But the universe has a way of conspiring to make your dreams come true.

Porcelain is a colorful 2D animated short about a tiny porcelain dog chasing its ball across a magical pottery shelf where drawings suddenly spring to life. As the dog tumbles from one world to another, each piece of pottery transforms into a new adventure. The journey celebrates imagination, creativity, and the joy of exploring art from many different times and places.

A journey in 2D animation, in which every drawing has been traced onto blank postcards then hand painted, stamped and mailed. Every frame has traveled through the international post prior to appearing in the film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: This abstract animated film is a tribute to the unique and long-established art form of patchwork quilting. Using computer animation, digital drafting, and experimental design techniques, this mesmerizing film choreographs quilt motifs and designs and sets them to music.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Red Meat is a short animated film that explores pain, discomfort, and vulnerability through a poetic visual language based on a poem by Anne Carson. Created by Eleni Aerts, a graduate of the Royal Academy of Fine Arts (KASK) in Ghent, the film has been recognized with awards at Anima Festival Brussels and the Turku Animated Film Festival.

Don’t expect heavy guitars, but actual rocks when watching this short — and not the kind that give you a bump when dropped on your head. Entirely made from hand-dyed fabrics, Rock Song is a stop-motion about getting hurt, picking up some cracks along the way, and slowly figuring out how to heal. Charming film that joyfully sparks the imagination.

S The Wolf is a hilarious autobiographical flashback about growing up—or, more precisely, about losing hair. Through intimate anecdotes, the film follows the directors’ capillary journey from adolescence to the present: from the trauma of the barber’s chair to his first love, and finally to the loss of the most important person in his life.

Sad Cat Crunch is a short animated film about the shooting of a breakfast cereal commercial that goes completely awry in the actor's mind. Obsessed with fame and fortune, he begins to notice suspicions of doubt and delusions within himself. Only, as his inner conflict grows, does the commercial take an unexpectedly deadly turn. David Lynch would be proud.

films.t: Saq Nikté and the Spirit of the Mask
films.syn: In a remote Guatemalan community, 11-year-old Saq Nikté performs an old invocation that awakens Iq’, a curious and playful spirit. Entirely in the K’iche’ language, the film follows their encounter as Saq Nikté crafts a mask as an offering, bridging the worlds of the living and the spirit.
A children’s folktale meeting the degeneration of an adult world in this cut-out and hand-drawn short
An animated look into the sparkling ocean at night. Sounds and pictures drawn on film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: This intro and outro uses animated mattes to key in multiple video channels which must have been quite a puzzle to the makers. The outro also has a very special cameo.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: What if you could break free from reality and do anything you want—what would you do? In a suffocating era marked by anxiety and crises of self-identity, Chinese director Qi Duan explores a series of environments where accumulated pressure finds an outlet. This bold student film is characterized by a variety of styles and textures, in the spirit of Masaaki Yuasa.
A story about letting go of one's former self. It revolves around two characters: the Present Self and the Past Self.
In a mysterious forest, a woman is slowly lured into a nostalgic daydream as she observes butterflies.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: A masked boxer waits nervously in his locker room. When the fight begins, he faces not only a formidable opponent, but also his own demons. The battle erupts into a visual storm, where reality twists into absurd shapes and vivid colors. A little visual treat by Bram Fokkens.
Trailer for the Ottawa International Animation Festival 2025.

Bertil is lonely and bored at home while his parents are at work. One day, out of nowhere, Nils, a tiny thumb-sized boy, appears under his bed! They immediately become friends, and Nils shows Bertil a fascinating magical world hidden inside his bedroom walls. From that day on, neither of them will ever be lonely again.
Phnom Penh. Nakry and Sothear meet on the Sisowath Quay for their first date. When night falls, their romance turns into a nightmare as Nakry transforms into a strange creature…

Sixtyseven Milliseconds follows a bullet caught on surveillance camera footage and traces its path alongside that of its main protagonists. Combining traditional and new animation techniques, the film questions the legitimacy of policing in France and warns of its abuses. A powerful and terrifying reminder of police violence, social injustice, and life on the edge of the law.

It snowed! Lou and Marius are outside, rolling snowballs and building a snowman. But Mom calls them inside—Marius has to practice his clarinet, and Lou has homework to do. Lou sighs and opens her notebook. Marius plays a few hesitant notes… but... incredible! Outside, the snowman has moved.

Snake Soup volgt een soldaat op weg naar het slagveld. De ontmoetingen die hij onderweg heeft prikkelen zijn rijke verbeelding. Tot een verwoestende explosie zijn levendige herinneringen aan het verleden vervagen en samensmelten tot een hallucinante waas.
Laughs and chills combine with stop motion and hand-drawn animation in these dark-humor miniatures.
Silk screen printing and rostrum camera moves along with film printing techniques are the ingredients for this simple yet elegant AVRO sports programme leader.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Painstaking rotoscoped mattes isolate the goalkeeper to set him against a playful graphic background. Bumpers reveal the number of the "Goal of the Month".

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: In all its honest plainness, this leader combines what appear to be cut-out, paint and screen printing techniques with exact plotted movements on the rostrum camera tabletop combined with multiple exposures of the film. Looks can be deceiving, this is a piece of painstaking, nerve-wracking, patience-defying art.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: After a party full of nauseatingly similar couples, Tina rushes home—only to find her boyfriend proudly wearing the same shirt as her. In desperation, she struggles to prevent them from becoming a fused couple as well.
Combination of landscapes and drawings in stop motion.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: A large meatheaded man is stopped at a red light next to an innocent baby in a stroller—who inadvertently taunts him into a street race.
Strokes is an abstract movie about searching for beauty in chaos and the mess. Expect hypnotising rhytms and ever-changing forms continually popping up from simple pencil lines.

Two friends are enjoying a picnic in the park when a strange bee interrupts their day. This rude guest causes one of them to undergo a bizarre transformation and lose all bodily autonomy, sending them on the adventure of a lifetime.

Mr. Ham decides to have his heart removed in order to be relieved of his complicated feelings. The doctor assures him that this is no longer a problem in this day and age. However, Ham keeps his heart for a while after the removal, hoping to understand it better after all. Tako Tsubo is an animated, surreal reflection on dealing with feelings in a meritocracy.

films.t: Tamala 2030: A Punk Cat in Dark
films.syn: Tamala is back! Following cult hit Tamala 2010 (2002), future cult hit Tamala 2030 continues down the myriad winding roads connecting ancient occult mythologies, black-and-white Astro Boy aesthetics, cyber-noir capitalism critiques and colourful psychedelia, while our foul-mouthed kawaii hero keeps on dancing, and kicking everyone to the ground she doesn’t like.
Tatarang the dog wanders around and meets new friends. He plays with a mole, cat and a fish, and later they all gather together to listen to a tiny bug’s magical music.

Tears is a film about the impossibility of making a decision. A world full of possibilities, and a woman who may not want to choose at all. An intriguing portrait of an emigrant’s life, captured through a unique technique and storytelling, surprising you with every new scene.

films.t: TED-Ed: What Happens to Your Brain Without Any Social Contact?
films.syn: This year’s Kaboom selection engages with psychological effects of solitary confinement. Set in a US prison, the video explores how perception, memory and mental health change following solitary confinement. With an educational tone and accessible way the animation aims to convey complex topics.
A Mykola Hohol folktale adapted into a rotoscopic vision of horror.

A young boy explores the darkest depths of his grumpy, meat-grinding grandfather’s garage. There, he is confronted by the surreal memories of the man he thought he knew. An absurd slice-of-life by Areito Echevarria.

The great losses of a mother repeat themselves in a mourning ritual in the middle of a swamp. A heron brings a new loss each time, after which the depression takes hold of her once more. Where words seem to have lost their meaning for her and her daughter, dance and movement become the way to connect. A stunningly beautiful and utterly dark story about profound grief, from director Eva Lusbaronian.

A grandfather tells his granddaughter about his adventurous youth in early 20th-century Montreal. He falls in love with a girl whose tears turn into pearls, which he trades to a ruthless pawnbroker who becomes obsessed with their value. As he becomes caught up in the pursuit of wealth, he must choose between his love and the promise of riches. A fascinatingly beautiful stop-motion film by Chris Lavis and Maciek Szczerbowski.

For her biggest production yet, lauded experimental filmmaker Jodie Mack travelled the world for five years, collecting collages of textiles, maps, alphabets and more. Using her 16mm Bolex camera, stop motion and time-lapse techniques, she animates colourful pieces of fabric traversing the globe to her own pop soundtrack.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.t: The Horizon from the Tip of the Nose
films.syn: Étienne Bonnet, the director and main character of this film, was diagnosed as completely nearsighted at the age of six. Having spent a large portion of his life in a blur, The Horizon from the Tip of the Nose invites the viewer to rub their eyes as it explores the not-always-clear twists and turns of ophthalmology.
A young man feels lost in the modern digital world—until he finds himself in a hot piece of clickbait.

films.t: The Lighthouse: A Monument Valley 3 Story
films.syn: Sula washes up on a mysterious island full of puzzles, illusions and surreal challenges. Will she unlock the island's secrets and reconnect with her lost community?

The Phoenix is a 2D animated music video set in a dystopian heaven where angels rise against oppression. In a city of brutalist towers and masked enforcers, a lone hero joins a growing revolution. Symbols of resistance spread across the streets, protests erupt, and flames spark as the angels confront their golden-gated rulers. Blending imagery of repression, uprising, and fragile beauty, the film unfolds like a dream of resistance—where the gates of paradise are forced open and hope takes shape in a new world.

British Indie-pop Royalty and Pulp frontman Jarvis Cocker introduces BBC’s ‘The Sleeping Forecast’. A diverse collection of characters fall asleep whilst listening to Cocker’s dulcet tones in this hand-crafted stop motion spot for the BBC Sounds podcast.

A nude model poses with statuesque stillness for an elite drawing class—until an unfortunate mosquito bite tests his self-control. Tormented by the itch, he teeters between the ruthless demands of perfection and his most unhinged, animalistic impulses.

A delivery rider spends an ordinary day navigating a city far from home, trapped in a cycle of work that feels endless and unseen. As voice notes from his mother punctuate the hours, her distant warmth briefly softens the rhythm of survival. The Voice Of Mother reflects on quiet burdens and the simple comfort of being remembered.

How does a machine learn to read the world? Through testimonies and screen recordings, Their Eyes immerses you in the experience of online micro-workers from the Global South whose invisible labor trains the AI of self-driving cars to navigate the streets of the Global North. This documentary unfolds as a technological, sociological, and ethical commentary on the contemporary world.

This is Not Your Garden is a theatrical fulldome animated documentary that exposes 500 years of colonial violence, industrial exploitation, and ecological collapse. Rooted in the disappearing wetlands and century-old forests of Bogotá, Colombia, this impressive film reconstructs ecosystems on the brink of extinction and reimagines a future in which plants reclaim agency.

Every day, Tiddler, a little fish with a big imagination, comes up with a new story to entertain his classmates. One morning, while dreaming up his latest tale, he gets lost in the middle of the ocean. He sees no way home—until he hears a familiar story and is saved by his own storytelling.

In To the Woods , memories of a lost loved one come vividly to life. Every scene feels like a painting as a brother and sister explore the forest beside their home under the starry sky. Although the events feel strikingly real, their journey ultimately reveals itself to be a mirage from the past. A hauntingly beautiful film about loss, directed by Agnès Patron.

This leader uses computer (aided) animation techniques in combination with hand painted artwork to create a new fresh modern look for the show. The computer animation technique used (with machines like the ADO, Bosch, Cubicomp, Antics, Scanimate or Quantel Paintbox) marks a new era and the end of analog animated leaders recorded onto 16mm film.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: From the start of the first season the director and designers for TopPop used mixed media combining film and video compositing techniques and animation with intricate set designs and scale models to create unique registrations of performances (early music videos). This leader shows a combination of bluescreen and miniatures in a multi-layered videomixed extravaganza that was used often in the show

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: In this leader 2D cell animation is combined with blue(screen) to be keyed in with clips from previous seasons of the show.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: In this season's animated leader intricate cut-out techniques were used to create split screen effects and a three-dimensional rotating cow, not to mention the sync talking red hot lips!

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Some examples of many leaders and bumpers created in this very neat, graphic style painted animation based on photos taken by the producer, involving intricate camera movements and painted simulated matte wipe transitions.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: High contrast photo-based prints combined with paper cut-outs create this fast paced replacement animation split screen sequence with some inventive fitting logo animation at the end. Other TROS Station IDs and bumpers from this year used similar cut-out splitscreen techniques.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Lucille, a 14-year-old alligator, finally spends the summer with her estranged father, Bill, a blues guitarist. She joins him and his band on tour as a roadie and looks forward to spending time with him. On stage, he is charming, but getting to know him is not what she expected, as she uncovers the true meaning behind his music.
In a karaoke bar in post-apocalyptic Los Angeles, an expired can of tuna and a fake Louis Vuitton purse encourage each other to embrace their artistic voices—even if the world sees them as trash.

Two Weeks - Two Minutes is a sort of film-book, exploring the double page format and the notion of time in both media. During her two-week residency at the Center for Book and Paper Arts in Chicago, Judith Poirier printed simultaneously on paper and 35mm clear film stock using letterpress. Edited as two vertical screens side by side, the film mimics the format of a book and suggests a different reading experience.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: A stubborn baby refuses to do his homework, making excuse after excuse, while Grandma warns him he’ll end up like his hapless Uncle Tung. When a bathroom mishap literally sweeps him away, Tung dives in to save him. Together, they get lost in the open sea, facing bizarre and mischievous sea creatures in a wild, adventurous escape.

Three young adults, obsessed with the horrors of the modern world, find themselves trapped in the depths of a sprawling underground subway, which progressively transforms into a giant, nightmarish organic mass eager to assimilate them.

When Dolores misses a period, she anxiously heads to the drugstore for a pregnancy test. What begins as a simple errand becomes a transformative journey, as she unexpectedly overhears and engages in conversations with women about their unconventional stories of motherhood. Director Juliana Erazo Gómez interweaves fiction with personal anecdotes in this compelling animated documentary.

films.t: Van de Beste Makers: Lutjewinkel Kaas Moet Je Proeven
films.syn: Commercial for Dutch grocery delivery service Picnic.

An early animated leader in the lineup of Dutch TV title sequences, and a very inventive one for this programme that looks into the future, covering topics ranging from healthcare to space travel. With color broadcast having just commenced and the majority of programs still produced in B&W, the double exposure technique was effective enough to create these superimposed titles.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Veils of Landscape takes its title from a phrase in Japan’s traditional 72 micro-seasons, “Kasumi Hajimete Tanabiku,” describing the softening air and hazy mountains of late February. Recognizing that landscapes are shaped by multiple layers of nature, director Chihiro Yamanaka layered several levels of animation to explore how the medium can convey space and time unfolding on screen.

Through a series of animated art boards depicting a decaying Venice, Venezia Diorama unfolds like a set of postcards, capturing the mythical city's final moments of fragility. Blending archival footage with contemporary observations, and anchored by the story of the 1902 collapse of St Mark's Campanile, Venezia Diorama invites us to reflect on a city slowly eroding, yet suspended in time.

Visiting the Zoo offers a glimpse into the lives of three characters navigating the city like animals in a cage, gradually reconnecting with their primal instincts—until a final showdown with real animals shatters all social rules. A short full of edgy revenge fantasies from director Maria Zilli.

Warp and Weft is an animated documentary short about traditional textile crafts.A love letter to the act of hand-making, traditional craft practices, and the people who love them. Stemming from the fear of these artforms slipping away in a society that no longer values the human labour behind them.

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: In the serene Wadden Sea, where land and water meet, a unique roadside restaurant for birds operates along the migratory flyway. Here, guests eat and are eaten, until a single footstep throws everything off balance.

Dan has a gaping wound in his neck that refuses to heal. Why? He can neither remember nor talk about it. To confront it, he must return to the shadowy arena of his childhood and reclaim the part of himself he left behind, the part that keeps him from being whole as an adult. What We Leave Behind is a powerful, haunting film from the award-winning writer-director duo Jean-Sébastien Hamel and Alexandra Myotte.

films.t: Where Wool Speaks, and We Must Listen
films.syn: The film explores the deep connection between Deccani wool, the land, and its people, highlighting its cultural, spiritual, and ecological significance. It delves into the resilience of the Deccani sheep, the traditions of shepherding, and the sacred role of wool in daily life. Through the story of Balu Mama and his revered flock, the film contrasts a rich heritage with the modern neglect of India

ap.sel: Officially selected (section: Festival Theme: Human Touch)

films.syn: Winter in March shifts the viewer’s perspective to the other side of the war. A young couple is overcome by a sense of powerlessness as the ruling regime in their homeland tightens its grip and increasingly oppresses the population. Escape seems their only option, but even that becomes a surreal nightmare. A touching and beautifully crafted stop-motion documentary by Natalia Mirzoyan.

In a colorful world where, after each break-up, ex-partners must exchange a chosen body part, Wish You Were Ear explores the lasting impact of relationships. Here, people not only lose a literal piece of themselves with each split, but also carry visible reminders of every past love. Feeling fragmented and deformed, the protagonist is stunned to see their former ear on another person. That encounter begins their path to self-acceptance.

Witness: An Organima Film is meticulously hand-animated using organic matter. This experimental animated short captures the sentience of small life-forms: ancient beings on stone, an intelligent water droplet, and spirits of sunlight. It lets natural materials guide their own story, while elemental archives invite viewers to question the nature of human purpose and renew their childlike vision.
What's the future? A row of spectators is seeking answers while the world is in flames. WTF?!

films.t: You Are Not Part of the Cake
films.syn: Ping gets into conflict with her girlfriend’s homophobic and aggressive father. He describes his relationship with his daughter as a layered cake—and Ping is not part of it. When the argument spirals out of control, Ping is forced to defend herself mercilessly. Whoever wants to be the cake will end up becoming it… A twisted portrayal of personal experiences by Taiwanese director Ting-Jui.

films.t: You Don’t Know How I Love You
films.syn: To what extent can you choose how close to come to another person’s body? You Don’t Know How I Love You explores how crossing physical boundaries can come from care or self-interest. This fairytale-like analog animated film, set in a deserted winter forest, delicately examines loneliness and bodily autonomy.

A girl’s peaceful sleep is ruined by a relentless mosquito. She tries hiding, hunts it down, and finally catches it—then hesitates, feeling a strange compassion. But when it returns, her patience snaps, and she kills it. Only then can she finally return to bed… until the next mosquito appears.
